LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: cf target points at the wrong org; isolate the session with CF_HOME
Symptom: cf push lands in another product's org/space and its route blocks the right push; cf target set in one command is gone in the next; logging into a second landscape overwrites the current target.
Cause: There is one machine-wide ~/.cf/config.json shared by every project; cf target does not persist between an agent's shell calls; several customer orgs share the same API endpoint.
Fix: Use a dedicated CF_HOME (pointing at the folder that CONTAINS .cf) for scripts/automation, set the target in the same command as login, check cf target right before every push; delete CF_HOME afterwards (it holds tokens).
Workaround: If you must change the global target, back up config.json and restore it afterwards. Only delete apps/routes you can prove your own push created.
Tip: 'No API endpoint set' usually means CF_HOME points one level off. In Git Bash set MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 and give CF_HOME as a Windows path; check shell syntax so CF_HOME really is set. Check the org name before any write.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: Bare HTTP status codes mislead on CF and behind the approuter
Symptom: curl to a /srv-* path behind the approuter returns 200 as if the backend were up; on CF a missing route and a healthy app without a root handler both return 404; one probe says the host is dead.
Cause: The 200 is the XSUAA login bounce page (text/html), and the approuter also bounces client-credentials bearers; the CF router only adds x-cf-routererror: unknown_route when there is no route; a first silent response is a cold start or transient.
Fix: Assert content-type and body, not just status; a 404 without x-cf-routererror means the route exists and the app answered; to prove the service level send the bearer to the service host, and prove the approuter hop separately with a real browser login.
Tip: Retry once with a longer timeout before declaring a host dead. A browser CSRF flow showing 403 then 200 is normal.

rows.text: KNOWLEDGE HUB - PEOPLE, ROLES AND ACCESS (read live, never from memory). The access model changes; always read the current one: GET https://kh-keycloak.cfapps.br10.hana.ondemand.com/realms/knowledge-hub/kh/catalog with the person's token (kh-helper: 'kh catalog', MCP: kh_catalog). It lists roles, project levels (owner, editable, readonly) and their permissions, kinds of account (system-admin, tenant-admins, kh-users) with what each may do, the tenants, and the projects every user reads by default. To add someone to a project: 'kh members add <project> <email> --level readonly|editable|owner' (MCP: kh_members); an e-mail without an account gets one in the inviter's company. How to connect a CLI: GET https://knowledge-hub.cfapps.br10.hana.ondemand.com/auth/help. Written 2026-09-28.

WORKBEATS - HOW TO LOG WORK (the process). Seeded 2026-09-28 from the Workbeats handoff; hours are logged as actually spent.

# Handoff: logging work into Workbeats

You are a Claude session helping your user log their weekly work hours into **Workbeats**, the company timesheet app, and submit them. This file tells you everything needed to do it the same way it is done on another machine. Read it all before starting.

- App: https://laidon-time-tracking-prod-simplemdg-web.cfapps.br10.hana.ondemand.com/main/time-sheet
- Trigger phrases: "log work", "logwork", "log giờ lên Workbeats", "fill my timesheet".
- Golden rules:
  1. Nothing is entered before the user approves the list.
  2. Only the items they approve get logged.
  3. Nothing already in Workbeats is logged twice.
  4. The job is not finished until the week is **submitted**.

---

## 1. Default range: Monday to Friday

- Always log the work done **Monday to Friday of the current week**.
- If the user asks for another range ("tuần trước", "chỉ thứ 5"), use it **for that one request only**. Next time, go back to Monday to Friday.
- Timezone is UTC+7, the same as the app.

## 2. Build the task list

Collect what the user worked on in the range. Good sources:

- Your own session history or memory.
- Their git commits, e.g. `git log --since=<monday> --author=<them>` across their repos.
- Merge requests and PRs, Jira tickets they touched, and their notes.

Rules for the list:

- If something is unclear, ask the user instead of guessing.
- Make **one task per piece of work**, not per commit. Merge follow-ups into one task.
- Record which day(s) each task happened on.

## 3. Never log these

- Work with **no project**, such as personal experiments or scratch tests.
- **Code scan or indexing** actions, such as ingesting a repo into a knowledge base.
- Internal AI tooling that is not a company project: SMDG AI, Buzz (the private test build, not Solace Buzz), RITA and all its tools and sidecars, Knowledge Hub and all its tools and sidecars, and the orchestrator.
- **Fixes of bugs we caused ourselves.** Examples: removing something we added that nobody asked for, or fixing a regression from our own earlier change.
- If you cannot tell whether a fix was self-caused, put it under "needs decision". Do not decide it yourself.

## 4. Map each task to a Workbeats project

| Work belongs to | Workbeats project (pick by this visible name) |
|---|---|
| SimpleMDG 2.0 / SMDG v2 | `SIMPLEMDG 2.0` |
| M360 (PM App) | `INTERNAL-SMDG-360 View` |
| Pacific (Par Pacific) | `PARPACIFI-US-2025` |
| Ticketing System | `INTERNAL-SMDG-Ticketing System` |
| Stella Jones | `Stella Jones` |
| Any other internal app, e.g. Solace Buzz | `INTERNAL APP - INTERNAL APP` (listed as `INTERNAL APP — INTERNAL APP`) |
| Unknown | `INTERNAL-SMDG-POC` has no known meaning. Do not use it without asking |

A project that is not in this table goes under "needs decision".

## 5. Open Workbeats and READ WHAT IS ALREADY THERE

The user may already have logged some tasks by hand. Before planning anything:

1. Open the timesheet page and let the user log in (step 11). You do not need to click through weeks: read the week through the API.
2. Read every entry already in the week with `readWeek()` from the appendix: day, start time, hours, status (`draft`, `submitted`, approved, rejected), project and task name.
3. If a planned task matches an existing row (same Jira id, or clearly the same work), **do not create it again**. Skip it, or add only the missing days to that existing row.
4. Existing hours **count toward that day's total**. Plan only the hours and time slots that are still free.
5. Never edit or delete a row the user did not ask about. Never touch Approved or Submitted entries.

## 6. Plan the hours

**Log the time actually spent.** Do not round a short day up to 8h and do not stretch a task to fill the day.

- Use 0.5h steps; the app allows 15-minute steps.
- **Estimates:** show a task's real estimate (Jira Original Estimate, or one written on the task) beside it in the approval list. If the time spent is above the estimate, log the real time and say so in the list; the user decides.
- **Short day:** a day under 8h stays under 8h. Say in the approval list that it is under 8h and why (for example: few tasks, time off, work not tied to a project).
- **Long day:** a day over 8h is logged as it is. Say so in the approval list.
- Hours already in Workbeats (step 5) count toward the day.
- If a Monday-to-Friday day has no work found, tell the user. Do not fill it.
- Working hours are **08:30 to 12:00** (3.5h) and **13:30 to 18:00** (4.5h).
- Entries run **back to back with no overlap**, starting at 08:30. The app warns on overlap.
- One task can hold **only one entry per day** (there is no "add another log" button), so **no entry may cross lunch**. Hours beyond 18:00 continue back to back from 18:00.

## 7. Show the list for approval (in the user's language, Vietnamese by default)

Group the tasks by Workbeats project. Write one line per task, using a **bold plain number**. Do not use a markdown list: `- 1.` nested under a bullet renders as a, b, c, and the user rejected that.

```
**PARPACIFI-US-2025**
**1.** [Pacific] PAR-463: tìm nguyên nhân treo 15 phút, trace lỗi Event Mesh. *T2 3.5h, T3 3.5h (estimate 8h)*
**2.** [Pacific] Sửa trang TIN Matching bị trống, copy key Sovos. *T3 1.5h, T4 2h*
**3.** [Pacific] PAR-500: làm trọn ticket trong ngày, theo estimate. *T5 6h (estimate 6h)*

T4 chỉ 2h: chỉ có 2 task nhỏ, không nâng lên 8h được.

**Đã có trên Workbeats**
**4.** [Ticketing] ... (đã log tay, bỏ qua)

**Cần quyết**
**5.** [Vicor] ... không có project tương ứng, log vào đâu hay bỏ?
```

- Keep each description under 20 words.
- Show the day and hours for every task, and the estimate when the task has one.
- Mark every day that stays under 8h, with the reason.
- Mark every day that goes over 8h, with its official basis ("trọn ticket trong ngày, theo estimate").
- Wait for an answer like "duyệt 1-12, bỏ 13". Log only those numbers.

## 8. Create the tasks (English)

- Do it through the API, not the UI. `logTask` creates the task **and** its first time log in one call (see step 9 and the appendix).
- Task Name is always **English**, in this exact format:

  `[<JIRA-ID> or <ACTION>] <Project name> - <short description under 20 words>`

  - `[PAR-463] Pacific - Random 15-minute stall on single request submit`
  - `[FIXBUG] Pacific - Prod TIN Matching Settings page blank`
  - `[FEATURE] Ticketing System - Okta SSO sign-in`
  - `[PAR-441] [PAR-434] Pacific - Promote dev changes to UAT`
- ACTION tags used so far: `FIXBUG`, `FEATURE`, `INVESTIGATE`, `SETUP`.
- Read the week again (`readWeek()`) right before creating a task, and never create a duplicate. Also check the project's task list (`findTask()`): if a task with that exact name already exists, add a log to it with `saveLogs()` instead of `logTask`.

## 9. Enter the time (API)

- **New task + its first day:** `logTask(projectId, taskName, day, start, hours, desc)`.
- **Another day on an existing task, or editing a log:** `saveLogs([...])` (the `bulkTimeLogs` action). Pass the log `ID` to edit it in place; leave `ID` out to create a new one. The reply says "Create time logs in MDG successfully" even for an edit; that is normal, it does not duplicate.
- The **Description** is **required**: one short English sentence about what was done that day.
- Times are sent in **UTC**. The user's day is UTC+7, so 08:30 local is `01:30Z`. `duration` is in **minutes**. The appendix helpers take local `HH:MM` and do the conversion.
- `billable`: copy what the project's other tasks use (M360 tasks are `false`).
- **Check every entry**: run `readWeek()` again and compare day, start, hours and description with the plan. Each day's total must match the plan: normally 8h, less on a light day, more on a day with the official over-8h basis.

## 10. Submit (required)

1. Collect the log IDs of **exactly the approved entries** (from the `logTask` replies or `readWeek()`).
2. Check that their hours add up to the planned total.
3. Call `submit(ids)`. The reply should say "Time logs submitted successfully".
4. Run `readWeek()` once more: those entries must now show `submitted`.

## 11. Browser access

The API runs **inside the logged-in Workbeats tab** with `fetch()`. You cannot take the login out to a script: the session is an HttpOnly cookie that code cannot read. As long as the tab stays open and logged in, every call works.

- **Preferred: Claude in Chrome.** Open the app URL in a new tab, let the user log in, then run the appendix code with the `javascript_tool`. Paste the helpers once per page load (a reload wipes them).
- **If the extension is not connected**, run a separate Chrome with a debug port and run the same JavaScript through Playwright `page.evaluate(...)`:
  ```
  "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=C:\RWTemp\chrome-workbeats --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check "<workbeats url>"
  ```
  The separate `--user-data-dir` is what makes the port open while the user's normal Chrome is running.
- **The user logs in themselves** in that window (SAP login page). Never type credentials. Wait until they say they are done.
- When you finish, **close that Chrome** (kill the `chrome.exe` processes whose command line contains `chrome-workbeats`). Then check that `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version` no longer answers. An open debug port lets any local program control the logged-in browser.

## 12. Report back

Keep the report short, in the user's language:

- whether the week was submitted
- how many tasks
- hours per day
- any change from the approved plan, for example hours moved so an entry would not cross lunch, hours trimmed to an estimate, or a day left under 8h

---

WORKBEATS - THE API (for the log-work process, see topic workbeats-log-work). Seeded 2026-09-28.

## Appendix A: Workbeats API

Tested end to end on 2026-09-25: read the week, create 2 tasks with `logTask`, edit one log in place with `bulkTimeLogs`, submit with `submitTimeLogs`, read back.

- Base: `/srv-workbeat/TimeTrackingService/` on the app's own host (SAP CAP, OData V4). Metadata: `$metadata`.
- Auth: the logged-in tab's HttpOnly session cookie, sent automatically by `fetch()` in that tab.
- CSRF: every POST needs header `x-csrf-token`. Get it with a GET to `/srv-workbeat/UserService/UserInfo` carrying `x-csrf-token: fetch`; the token comes back in the response header. **It rotates**: a token fetched earlier once got `403 Forbidden`. On 403, fetch a new one and retry once (the helper does this).
- The same `UserInfo` call returns the user; `userID` is their email and is the `userId` on every log.

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET Projects?$filter=fullName eq '<name>'` | Workbeats project by visible name |
| `GET Tasks?$filter=projectId eq <id>` | tasks of a project (`name`, `timeEstimate`, `billable`, `isDone`) |
| `GET TimeLogs?$filter=userId eq '<email>' and entryDate ge '<from>' and entryDate le '<to>'` | the user's entries in a range |
| `POST logTask {input:{projectId,taskName,description,billable,entryDate,startTime,endTime,duration,status:'draft'}}` | new task plus its first log; returns `{taskId, timeLogId}` |

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: A budget killswitch that unlinks billing takes down the whole project
Symptom: Every Cloud Run service returns 503/500 from the Google front end although Ready=True; the API says 'check billing account'.
Cause: A budget-alert Cloud Function ('stop_billing') triggered via Pub/Sub unlinked billing from the project.
Fix: A Billing Account Administrator relinks the project; first raise the budget or disable the killswitch, otherwise the next alert takes it down again.
Tip: When everything fails at once, run 'gcloud billing projects describe' first. The audit entry is on the billing account, not the project. A spike in read cost (short poll interval) can trigger it.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: BTP to on-prem S/4 needs Cloud Connector or VPN
Symptom: Direct API calls from BTP to the customer's S/4HANA (or another core system) fail during integration, close to the handover date.
Cause: Corporate network policy around core systems; traffic must go through SAP Cloud Connector or a dedicated VPN, approved by the customer's security team, which takes weeks.
Fix: Ask about network path, auth method, rate limits and a test environment as soon as a core system enters scope; file the access request in week one; count the handover date from when the connection opens.
Tip: Schedule access approval as planned work, measured in weeks.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: cf API tooling silently reads the wrong tenant or nothing at all
Symptom: A probe reports a plausible but wrong fleet (another org's apps), or an empty estate; mapping a subaccount GUID to a CF org GUID finds nothing.
Cause: Every org has spaces with the same names, so /v3/spaces?names=... returns spaces from every org; with an expired token cf curl exits 0 with an empty body; logged out it returns JSON with an errors array; a subaccount GUID is not a CF org GUID; listings only cover spaces where you hold a role.
Fix: Resolve the org GUID first and filter spaces by organization_guids, refuse if no org is targeted; treat an empty body, an errors array or 'Not logged in' as hard failures (distinct exit code), not as zero data; map cockpit to CF by name.
Tip: Zero results from a role-scoped listing means 'no permission', not 'does not exist'. Error messages should print the valid unblocking command; test error paths as thoroughly as the happy path.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: Traps when cf pushing a Python app
Symptom: Push aborts with 'file has been modified since the start of push'; 70 MiB uploaded despite .cfignore; UI missing; staging picks the wrong Python version; secrets set with cf set-env vanish after push, push log leaks secrets.
Cause: The push log is written inside the app folder; folder patterns in .cfignore with a trailing '/' do not match; the Python buildpack does not build an SPA; the buildpack ignores .python-version; pushing with an env block in the manifest resets env set by cf set-env.
Fix: Write logs outside the repo and ignore *.log; folder patterns without a trailing '/', verify by upload size; build web/dist first and refuse to push without index.html; use runtime.txt and pin a non-deprecated stack; re-set secrets after push (or use a bound service).
Tip: cf push packages the FOLDER, not a commit, so push from a clean tree. Parameterise per-environment values with a vars file. CF disk is ephemeral; cf ssh may be disabled in the space. Use a separate session secret per environment.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: Python buildpack drops old patches, a runtime.txt pin breaks staging
Symptom: BTP deploy fails with BuildpackCompileFailed / 'no match found for 3.12.x' with no code change; the Actions UI only shows an unrelated artifact quota error.
Cause: The SAP Python buildpack removes old patches when it adds new ones, so the patch pinned in runtime.txt disappears; the deploy script redirected cf push output to a file so the real error is not in the Actions log.
Fix: Bump runtime.txt to a patch from the list the error prints; record the procedure in the deploy notes.
Tip: Diagnose with 'cf logs <app> --recent | grep STG' and 'cf app <app>'; an old 'last uploaded' is the fastest proof a deploy did not land. A quick /healthz probe right after push can fail during rolling restart, so retry until healthy.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: cf login from a non-interactive shell
Symptom: 'cf login' / 'cf login --sso' fails immediately with 'Unable to authenticate' at the prompt; cf target still shows org/space but every call says token expired.
Cause: The agent's shell has no stdin so the prompt reads EOF; --sso and --sso-passcode are mutually exclusive; the passcode flag belongs to 'cf login', not 'cf auth'; the target survives token expiry.
Fix: 'cf login -a <api> --sso-passcode=<code> -o <org> -s <space>' with a freshly fetched passcode (use the '=' form if the code starts with '-').
Workaround: 'cf login --sso </dev/null' prints the passcode URL before failing.
Tip: Test the token with a real API call, not cf target. Browser logins (gcloud) work, stdin prompts (cf, btp) do not. Let the user type the passcode instead of the agent holding credentials.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: A single-use SSO passcode burned while probing regions
Symptom: cf login says 'Invalid passcode' right after the user supplies a fresh code, in every region tried.
Cause: A UAA passcode is single-use; the agent tried it against several regions' token endpoints to discover the CF region. The cockpit/global account region does not imply the CF region.
Fix: Determine the CF API endpoint from a non-consuming source (saved cf config, org quota name, stored knowledge, or ask the user), then use the passcode exactly once for the real cf login.
Workaround: Ask for a new code and run 'cf login -a <api> --sso-passcode <code>' once.
Tip: Get the code from the login host the CLI prints, not the UAA host. Dev/QAS and prod may be in different regions. Ignore endpoints in local hybrid-binding files.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: A slow network to the BTP region looks like a broken app
Symptom: SSO sign-in slow or failing, e2e tests time out randomly; the identity server or app is blamed.
Cause: The local network path to the BTP region drops or delays replies; router logs show the server answered in milliseconds.
Fix: Read gorouter response_time in cf logs to separate server time from network time; retry from another network.
Workaround: Test harnesses should cap wait time, print progress and only retry idempotent GETs.
Tip: Run heavy DB migrations from inside the region (in region: 211 changesets in ~15 s; from a laptop: 58 changesets in 13 minutes).

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: CI credentials for cf push on BTP
Symptom: A long-lived token is needed for the deploy pipeline.
Cause: CF UAA on BTP only allows username/password/passcode; access tokens live ~18 minutes, refresh tokens rotate and die on password change; client credentials need an SAP-managed UAA client; the xsuaa 'apiaccess' plan does not work for cf push.
Fix: Use a dedicated technical user (SAP ID service, password auth) with Space Developer on ONE target space only; cf auth reads CF_USERNAME/CF_PASSWORD from env so the password is not on the command line.
Tip: Add a 'login only' mode that authenticates and reads the app back, proving password and role without deploying. SSO login cannot run unattended.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: The deployed estate has drifted from the repo config
Symptom: A deploy to a new environment runs with dev sizing and bindings; HTTP calls between services fail; the live UI lacks fixes already on staging.
Cause: Environment-to-config-tier mapping silently falls back to dev; inter-service URLs use a legacy hostname that no longer exists; a destination points at a stopped v1 app; services run different SHAs, a UI bundle was pushed by hand from an old commit.
Fix: Declare every environment tier explicitly; derive routes from app names instead of hard-coding; audit destinations against running apps; redeploy from staging via CI.
Tip: Verify the runtime, not the repo: a /healthz exposing the runtime SHA makes drift visible. Tiers may use different schema mechanisms, so a migration error may appear in only one tier.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: The approuter image date says nothing about the UI5 bundle age
Symptom: The approuter app has an old 'last uploaded' so the UI is assumed weeks old; the cockpit has no build stamp.
Cause: The approuter serves UI5 apps from the HTML5 Application Repository, not from its own image; applicationVersion in the manifest is static.
Fix: Identify the deployed UI from the served artefact: last-modified of Component-preload.js and search it for a symbol from the new commit. For Docker backend apps, cf ssh in and inspect the bundled library code.
Workaround: If nothing identifies the build, use a behavioural fingerprint: run the same input through old module versions and see which matches.
Tip: Image tags often carry the branch name, proving which branch an environment runs. Route/destination names may differ from the CF app name.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: BTP services (Custom Domain, PostgreSQL) need a global-account entitlement
Symptom: Org Manager/Space Developer cannot add a custom domain; no postgresql-db offering in cf marketplace nor plan in entitlements.
Cause: Entitlements live on Cloud Foundry at global-account level and are then assigned to a subaccount; only a global account admin can do it (may need SAP/commercial). Region is not the cause. 'certificate-service' is for client certs, not server TLS.
Fix: Have the global account admin add the entitlement and assign the plan to the subaccount, then create the service ('cf create-service postgresql-db <plan>') or domain + TLS cert, and map the route.
Workaround: Keep hosting where the domain already points and move only the database.
Tip: Never point DNS before CF has a route for the hostname. Check Discovery Center and the btp CLI before blaming the region. The CF org GUID is not the subaccount id; for a simple read, send a cockpit deep link instead of fighting btp CLI login.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: Measuring CPU/RAM balance on a live CF space
Symptom: The balance conclusion flips sign within seconds; the anchor run loses half its samples; a saturated service is labelled the other way round.
Cause: Raw utilization includes the runtime's idle floor; sampling through cf CLI costs ~20 s per sample; a rolling redeploy happens in the window; a stale process GUID after restart is treated as fatal; an anchor near 100% inverts the formula.
Fix: Use /v3/processes/<guid>/stats (normalized cpu_entitlement); compute utilization against a measured idle baseline; track uptime to flag freshly restarted instances; NotFound is a per-instance gap while auth errors stay fatal; a saturated anchor is a finding of its own.
Workaround: Query the CF API directly with a bearer token if ~1 Hz sampling is needed.
Tip: Do not compare numbers across environments with different build shapes or quotas. RAM tripling with flat CPU and never returning to baseline signals retention, not working set.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: Diagnosing a Node app on CF with no logs
Symptom: The error window has scrolled out of 'cf logs --recent'; the SAP Cloud Logging dashboard opens but every query returns 403 security_exception.
Cause: The recent-log buffer is short; the Cloud Logging dashboard needs a BTP role collection, a service key only grants ingest credentials.
Fix: Request the Cloud Logging dashboard role collection; meanwhile stream cf logs live while reproducing.
Workaround: Attach the Node inspector: 'kill -USR1 <pid>' in the container, 'cf ssh -N -L' to forward the inspector port, then use CDP (Runtime.evaluate) to read live state.
Tip: The inspector stays on until the instance restarts. Exit status 137 in cf events means killed for out-of-memory.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP BTP & Cloud Foundry]: Deploy 'Start unsuccessful' caused by a failing Diego cell
Symptom: The deploy stage reports 'Start unsuccessful' and the app logs nothing.
Cause: A CF platform fault: container creation on one cell fails with 'external networker encountered an error running up action', not a code bug.
Fix: If the cell keeps failing, cf restart the app to land on another cell, or open an SAP BTP support ticket with the cell ID.
Workaround: CF usually reschedules the instance a few minutes later; rerun the pipeline just to turn it green.
Tip: Check cf events and cf app before debugging code; a pipeline can report UNSTABLE/FAILURE while the app runs fine, so check CF directly.

Symptom: cf curl and single v3 GET/DELETE return CF-NotFound; cf ssh refused; bulk migration from a laptop takes ~11 s per record; parsing VCAP_SERVICES from cf env fails as JSON or never ends.
Cause: The user's permissions are limited; each record is dozens of round trips to a distant region; cf env prints several JSON blocks back to back and braces inside strings (certs, JDBC URLs) break brace-counting parsers.
Fix: Use official cf verbs and --guid / ?guids= filters; run bulk jobs inside the landscape with 'cf run-task <app> --command ... -m 1G --wait' (inherits VCAP bindings, ~55x faster); parse VCAP with json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode.
Tip: cf run-task only works if the script is in the app's droplet. Read task output with 'cf logs --recent' filtered on APP/TASK. HANA bindings can be read straight from 'cf env <app>' and connected read-only with hdbcli.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: HANA is not SQLite/Firestore: dialect and column widths
Symptom: Inserts fail with 'inserted value too large for column' (SQL 274) during migration; a LIKE prefix returns rows from another collection; 'incorrect syntax near #' when creating tables.
Cause: There is no CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; upsert is UPSERT ... WITH PRIMARY KEY; '_' in LIKE is a wildcard; Firestore has no widths so composite ids and long MIME types overflow NVARCHAR; Python '#' comments leak into SQL.
Fix: Check SYS.TABLES before create and tolerate the race; escape LIKE patterns; size columns from the measured max plus headroom, boot-time schema code only widens columns; strip comment lines from DDL.
Tip: Real data volume is the first test of column widths, so migrate on staging first. SELECT seq.NEXTVAL consumes a number; after migration restart the sequence above max. Use transactions for merge writes when running several instances.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: Switching backend leaves half the app on the old store
Symptom: The backend flag is set to HANA but login still hits Firestore; the admin page returns 503 'backend_unsupported'; some data has nowhere to live after cutover.
Cause: Each repository factory decides on its own; identity only knows some backends; the HANA repository lacks tables/methods; tests encode the old split so they stay green.
Fix: Before cutover, audit every method of every repository interface per backend, add missing tables idempotently, and have the migrator report document names it cannot map.
Tip: A service holding DB credentials does not mean it uses that DB; only the selector decides. A new backend value can make other factories fall back to default; use a narrow flag when switching a single repository.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: Data migration traps: wrong target, NULL columns, reruns
Symptom: A 'verified' relational migration has created_at NULL on 3 of 4 rows; the new table is filled but the app does not read it; prod was migrated into a nearly empty schema while the real data lived elsewhere.
Cause: The mapping stored differently formatted timestamps in an 'extra' table instead of typed columns and the round-trip test only checked the document came back; the app reads the document table; nobody compared id sets between the two stores; the Firestore sample was taken by doc id (oldest first).
Fix: Migrate through the app's own repository, idempotently, with --verify reading back, assert typed columns directly, and compare side by side with the old backend on the same input. Determine by id which store is the superset before cutover.
Tip: Migrate before flipping the flag; never rerun a JSON-to-relational migrator after cutover. Apps sharing a schema must switch together. Do not migrate derived caches. Separate 'data loss' from 'informational' in the report.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: A data backfill run on only one store locks users out
Symptom: After a deny-by-default auth change, most users on the HANA environment see 'not authorized' despite signing in; admins still get in so it looks like a per-user fault.
Cause: The access-map backfill ran only on the Firestore store; the HANA identity schema was never backfilled, while a comment claimed 'backfilled every document'.
Fix: Run a merge-only backfill on every identity store, derive rights from existing roles and normalise unknown roles. Do not reuse a whole-document migration script, it overwrites store-specific fields.
Tip: When a data migration is a prerequisite of a code change, list and check every store and environment that code runs on. An email-keyed doc index without roles can inflate the 'denied users' count.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: Document-shim merge write deadlocks itself and crashes the app
Symptom: A user creating a record sees 'couldn't reach the server' yet the data is written; ~2 minutes later the CF app crashes on liveness timeout; other roles work fine.
Cause: set(merge=True) holds a non-reentrant threading.Lock then calls a cache-eviction helper that takes the same lock, so the thread deadlocks itself; only that role's path does merge writes, on the event loop; tests against real HANA were skipped in the gate.
Fix: Evict the cache directly while holding the lock; add an offline regression test proving the merge write returns and releases the lock.
Tip: When one role fails while another works on the same screen, diff each role's write paths. Audit every helper called under a lock for re-acquiring that lock.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: App-managed tables need the HANA 'schema' plan, not hdi-shared
Symptom: The runtime user can SET SCHEMA but CREATE TABLE fails with 'insufficient privilege'.
Cause: An hdi-shared container needs deployed .hdbtable artifacts; the runtime user has no DDL rights. An app creating its own tables needs the 'schema' plan where the user owns the schema.
Fix: Create a HANA 'schema' plan instance per environment and bind it; take credentials from VCAP_SERVICES, with explicit env overriding.
Tip: Read rights look identical on both plans, so prove it with a write probe (create/insert/select/delete/drop a diag table). A HANA Cloud allowlist block shows up as a silent timeout on connect, while wrong credentials fail fast.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: Cross-region app-to-DB latency eats the whole page time
Symptom: Pages take 30-45 s for a few records; /readyz 1.6-11 s; only redirects that skip the DB are fast.
Cause: The app and HANA Cloud sit in distant regions: ~360-400 ms per round trip against ~2 ms of DB work; ~75 sequential statements per page; a liveness 'SELECT 1 FROM DUMMY' before every call doubles the reads.
Fix: Put the app and DB in the same region first. Otherwise cut round trips: time-based connection verification, TTL caches for config/identity, per-request memoisation, batched queries (UNION ALL), parallel queries (needs a connection pool).
Workaround: A same-region store for the hot path removes the distance entirely (7.5 s to 0.6 s).
Tip: Measure with SYS.M_SQL_PLAN_CACHE snapshots before and after one request (EXECUTION_COUNT is cumulative). A Cloud Run service cannot change region in place. Without min-instances cold start is 10-12 s.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: CAP 10 outbox dequeue rejected by HANA (FOR UPDATE WAIT)
Symptom: Requests stay stuck in SUBMITTING forever although the submit call returns 200 quickly; the process service logs repeat 'queue: Failed to fetch messages ... incorrect syntax near "WAIT"' (HANA error 257).
Cause: After upgrading @sap/cds 10.0.x, the persistent outbox by default generates SELECT ... FOR UPDATE WAIT <n>, which HANA Cloud rejects; with no outbox config the default is used. A service that has not received work yet is a latent fault, not healthy.
Fix: Pin an @sap/cds / @cap-js/hana pair whose outbox SQL HANA accepts, or configure cds.requires.outbox explicitly; this is an estate-wide change and needs coordination.
Workaround: After the fix, messages that exhausted retries remain in cds_outbox_Messages and need a manual re-drive; the error disappearing does not mean the requests will run.
Tip: Pin down the regression window with the app's updated_at timestamps. 'cf logs --recent' is a short buffer swamped by router lines: filter [APP/PROC/WEB] or use the cloud-logging service.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: A missing OData service is a missing app, not an auth/routing fault
Symptom: Some /srv-* paths return 404/403/405 while sibling services on the same app return 200; it looks like an auth or proxy-mapping issue.
Cause: The CAP service was never deployed: no CF app hosts that prefix, or the host app does not contain the service. A 405 on GET means the endpoint exists and is a POST action.
Fix: Probe each service's $metadata with a valid bearer token; a 404 next to a 200 on the same app rules out auth. Fix the deployment, not the client.
Tip: A CAP app root returns 'Cannot GET /' with no service index, so read service names from the CDS model in the repo. Point integration tests at services that actually answer.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: SAP HANA Cloud SQL and LOB quirks
Symptom: Migration fails on HANA; text columns come back wrong; lookups return 500; a remote row-by-row dump runs at only 0.4-2 rows/s; lengths differ after export.
Cause: CONCAT takes only two arguments; a unique constraint is rejected on an already indexed column; NCLOB returns a LOB handle (str() gives garbage); '=' does not work on NCLOB; LOB fetch over a remote link is very slow; HANA counts UTF-16 units (an emoji is 2).
Fix: Use '||' to concatenate; drop the redundant index in a HANA-only changeset; read LOBs explicitly; compare NCLOB with an escaped LIKE; dump LOBs inline with TO_NVARCHAR(SUBSTRING(...)) and vectors with TO_VARBINARY.
Tip: Make dumps resumable and check rows written == COUNT(*) with a manifest; a dump killed by timeout looks like exit 0 when piped through tail.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: Document-shim merge over a WAN hangs for minutes
Symptom: A seed script into HANA on BTP writes one row then hangs for 10+ minutes with no output; afterwards no blocked transaction is visible.
Cause: The shim merges with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in a transaction with autocommit off; every ~360 ms WAN round trip happens while holding the row lock.
Fix: A seeder writes whole rows, so use replace (set(merge=False), a lock-free upsert); keep merge for runtime paths that must not wipe edited fields.
Workaround: Run from inside the region or reduce round trips.
Tip: In long write loops print each item with flush=True and do not pipe through tail, otherwise a hang looks like slowness.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: Lexical MAX(id) over legacy ids breaks the displayed number width
Symptom: Every ticket number across the deployment suddenly shows ~12 extra leading zeros.
Cause: Display width is computed globally from MAX(id); legacy ids like 'tkt-<epoch-ms>' sort last lexically and a lenient parser takes the 13-digit timestamp as the max.
Fix: Only canonical ids (canonical regex) may decide the width, filtered both in SQL (MAX(CASE WHEN ... LIKE ...)) and in code; filtering only in Python still lets MAX return the legacy row.
Tip: Keep the lenient parser for lookups and use a strict parser for anything that decides global state. Pin the rule in every store implementation with a source guard test.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: Choosing SAP BTP changes every architectural building block
Symptom: The design was built on a GCP pipeline, Postgres+pgvector and a separate graph DB.
Cause: The customer chose SAP BTP; the platform's services change the building blocks.
Fix: Use XSUAA for SSO/roles, CAP multitenancy with SaaS provisioning, the HANA Cloud graph + vector engine as one store, Job Scheduling for long jobs, Object Store for uploads, Generative AI Hub for model calls; wrap HANA-specific SQL behind an adapter.
Tip: CI/CD outside BTP does not carry over, so plan an MTA pipeline; check HANA Cloud pricing (the main cost) and region early.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: Running CAP / UI5 locally without a real backend
Symptom: The UI5 app sticks on the loading screen; a minimal CAP bridge will not start: better-sqlite3 cannot build offline on a new Node, and cds serve picks up a stray VCAP_SERVICES from the shell.
Cause: The UI5 manifest creates several OData models at boot and waits for user/config init; VCAP_SERVICES in the env makes cds bind to cloud services.
Fix: For a render-only dev stand-in, replay the app's mock route table behind a small Node server on the proxy port; for the CAP bridge use an in-memory custom READ handler and a wrapper that deletes VCAP_SERVICES/VCAP_APPLICATION before loading cds serve.
Workaround: Return OData v4 $count as a plain-text integer, not JSON.
Tip: Once past the render shell, stop mocking and use the real deployed backend.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: Draft data is only readable through $expand of an auto-exposed navigation
Symptom: Draft data is NULL in the event-data entity; no entity set name contains 'Draft'; a direct query returns 405 ENTITY_IS_AUTOEXPOSED.
Cause: Drafts are stored on a navigation property whose target is auto-exposed, readable only via expand.
Fix: Query the parent entity with $filter on ID and $expand the draft navigation, using an XSUAA client-credentials token.
Tip: Back up draft data field by field before testing; testing can consume a rarely reproducible draft.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP CAP & HANA]: The HDI runtime schema hides tables; fully qualify names
Symptom: Unqualified SELECTs fail, or SYS.TABLES does not show the table so it is assumed missing.
Cause: An HDI connection's default schema is the _RT runtime schema; one container's binding has no grants on another container's schema.
Fix: Always write "<SCHEMA>"."<TABLE>"; take credentials from the binding of the app that uses that container (cf env) and never print them.
Tip: hdbcli from a laptop plus VCAP credentials is enough to read M_SQL_PLAN_CACHE, M_BLOCKED_TRANSACTIONS, M_TRANSACTIONS. Delete credential copies after use.

Symptom: Mail is still sent after removing SMTP from env; a 'disabled' dev clone can still send.
Cause: The sender is chosen in order: per-workspace Graph config in the DB, then per-workspace SMTP, then env SMTP, then no-op; disabling one level just falls to the next.
Fix: Disable every level: set configured=false with a field-masked PATCH (updateMask) so secrets are not lost, remove the env SMTP host; do not copy mail config when cloning data to dev; scrub PII to example.com addresses.
Tip: Mail already handed to the provider keeps flowing after the app stops and cannot be recalled. Revoking the Graph app permission or rotating the secret is the absolute stop.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP Event Mesh & Integration]: Workflows stuck exactly ~15 minutes due to SAP Event Mesh DNS failures
Symptom: Requests stick in SUBMITTING/APPROVING for about 15 minutes (always ~900-910 s) then finish on their own; no errors or logs, the app answers in ms, HANA and the queue look healthy.
Cause: Not a code bug: SAP Event Mesh fails to resolve a hostname when pushing the webhook (the app's CF route or the XSUAA token host), then retries on a fixed, non-configurable 900 s cycle. The failing resolver is inside SAP.
Fix: Open an SAP support ticket with the subscription name, lastFailedDelivery timestamp and reason. What you can fix yourself: move the consumer from webhook push ('enterprise-messaging') to AMQP pull ('enterprise-messaging-shared').
Workaround: Find the subscription whose lastFailedDelivery is right after the stuck step and rolling-restart the consumer app; the webhook re-registers and the message is delivered immediately. Pause/resume via REST returns 500 and does not help.
Tip: A fixed delay is a retry interval, not contention. Read /messagingrest/v1/subscriptions for lastFailedDeliveryReason (it keeps only the last error). Back up subscriptions before restarting since restart wipes error history. Also check whether a 'safety net' job is silently failing.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP Event Mesh & Integration]: Graph mail polling: the read flag is not a cursor
Symptom: Log says 'could not mark read'; mark-read returns 403 ErrorAccessDenied; beyond 25 unread mails new mail is never processed.
Cause: The delegated token only has Mail.Read, and marking read is a PATCH needing Mail.ReadWrite; mark-read was used as the cursor. Requesting an unconsented scope fails the whole sign-in (AADSTS65001).
Fix: Keep a separate ledger (processed ids, cursor, rejected), fetch 'isRead eq false and receivedDateTime ge <cursor>' oldest first; use ge and dedupe the boundary by id; never move the cursor back; a fresh install sets the cursor at the newest mail.
Workaround: Request write scope as optional, fall back to read-only and store the granted scopes.
Tip: Delegated Mail.Read only reads the signed-in user's mailbox; a shared mailbox needs Mail.Read.Shared plus an Exchange grant. A refresh token can only be exchanged for the scopes it carries.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [SAP Event Mesh & Integration]: A realtime Pub/Sub bus that never worked: two overlapping causes
Symptom: Notifications are correct on page load but never update live; the WebSocket connects fine, every instance logs 'could not start the pubsub subscriber', the publish side shows no errors.
Cause: (1) Cloud Run does not set GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT so the topic path became 'projects//topics/...'; nobody checked the publisher future so the error was silent. (2) Once the project id was set, the runtime service account lacked Pub/Sub roles (403).
Fix: Set GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT from the $PROJECT_ID substitution in the deploy config; grant pubsub.publisher on the topic and pubsub.editor at project level (the subscription created at startup does not exist yet to bind to); roll a new revision.
Tip: A fix that changes the error is progress, so compare the new error with the old one. Prove success positively: the subscription exists and the 'ready' log appears.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP Event Mesh & Integration]: Local mail agent: identity, config precedence and state
Symptom: The mailbox allow-list was edited but the agent still reads the old mailbox; a copied folder behaves differently; test mails 'never arrive'; the agent silently stops.
Cause: Identity is the refresh token in the state dir, not the allow-list; real env overrides .env; config is looked up next to the exe first; ignore filters swallow silently; a process started from the agent's shell dies with that shell.
Fix: On mismatch, skip the scan and state both addresses; show the signed-in account, cursor and last scan in status; tell testers which filter is applied.
Tip: Compare counters/timestamps in state with now; a dead agent looks like a quiet mailbox. The folder contains real secrets. Back up state and stop the process before deleting queues or rebuilding.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP Event Mesh & Integration]: Graph attachments and SharePoint upload sessions
Symptom: Listing messages downloads large videos too; big bodies get 413 from the platform; the Graph token for the file store gets 401 on the site.
Cause: Graph returns contentBytes (base64) for every attachment without $select; request bodies have a size limit; the mail-sending app registration has no application role, and file storage uses a separate Sites.Selected registration.
Fix: List attachment metadata with $select, stream /$value to a temp file, use an upload session with chunks that are multiples of 320 KiB and do NOT send an auth header to the pre-authorised upload URL; decode roles in the token to confirm the registration.
Tip: Email ingest has no one to retry: keep what fits, add a line noting dropped files, do not reject the whole message. A feature flag without its backend setting is a dead flag.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP Event Mesh & Integration]: Purview-encrypted mail cannot be read via Graph
Symptom: Records created from some internal mails contain only 'protected message' boilerplate; hasAttachments=false but /attachments has an .rpmsg.
Cause: A sensitivity label with encryption enabled (OME); Graph returns only the wrapper and does not decrypt, even for an entitled delegated user.
Fix: Create an Exchange mail-flow rule 'Remove Office 365 Message Encryption and rights protection' for mail to that mailbox, or disable encryption on the label in Purview.
Workaround: Detect the wrapper + OME marker and reject; filter by label read from msip_labels in internetMessageHeaders ($select on the list call itself).
Tip: Do not reverse-engineer DRM. hasAttachments is unreliable, always query /attachments. Only strip Defender/external-sender banners at the START of the body and log what was cut.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP Event Mesh & Integration]: Webhook-to-AMQP cutover in CAP is not atomic
Symptom: After switching messaging kind to enterprise-messaging-shared, the queue piles up unacked messages; messages still aimed at the old webhook get 404 and wait 15 minutes.
Cause: Changing the profile does not delete the old webhook subscription (CAP only calls deleteWebhook on undeploy) so two transports consume one queue; the /messaging/enterprise-messaging route disappears in pull mode.
Fix: Migrate one app at a time in a maintenance window: set config, restart, delete that app's webhook subscription, verify; accept a ~15 minute tail per app.
Workaround: Test without rebuilding the image: set CDS_CONFIG (JSON merged into cds.env) via cf set-env then restart; roll back with cf unset-env + restart.
Tip: The webhook URL is built at runtime from VCAP_APPLICATION.application_uris[0] (unless cds.env.app.url overrides it) and re-registered ~5 s after each start, so no repo contains it.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP Event Mesh & Integration]: Jira REST: a wrong username looks like a missing issue
Symptom: GET issue returns 404 'does not exist or you do not have permission'; unauthenticated search returns 200 with total 0.
Cause: The basic-auth username does not match the API token's owner; Jira masks auth errors as not-found/empty.
Fix: Use the email that owns the API token; check auth with /rest/api/3/myself first.
Tip: Treat an empty 200 from Jira as unverified until /myself returns 200.

LESSON LEARNED [SAP Event Mesh & Integration]: Invite mails leave no audit trail
Symptom: Nobody knows whether invite mails were sent or delivered; many invites are never used.
Cause: The invite path calls the sender directly, bypassing the notification layer that writes audit; delivery status is discarded after the HTTP response.
Fix: Store delivery status, sent_at and provider message id on the invite record when sending, or send via the audited notification path.
Workaround: Check Sent Items of the send-as mailbox or M365 Message Trace.
Tip: Prove a Graph app may send without sending anything: sendMail with empty recipients returns 400 if permitted, 403 if not.

LESSON LEARNED [ABAP & S/4]: Write the MARM link and commit before writing classification values
Symptom: Alternative UoM/production unit data ends up in Classification instead of the UoM screen; copying a material then submitting loses the UoM part.
Cause: MARM only stores the link (material + ATINN + KZWSO + MSEHI), AUSP stores values; if the batch class (023) is not assigned and the MARM line not committed before BAPI_OBJCL_CHANGE, SAP files the value under Classification. The GUI hides this because it commits per screen.
Fix: Order: assign class, create the MARM line (including UMREZ/UMREN/MEINH), BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT with WAIT = 'X', then BAPI_OBJCL_CHANGE (OBJECTTABLE MARA); check RETURN after every BAPI; use the same routine for the copy flow.
Tip: Check CABN-ATFOR first: a NUM characteristic needs ALLOCVALUESNUMNEW; filling the CHAR table raises no error but writes empty. Prove the order with an ST05 trace.

LESSON LEARNED [ABAP & S/4]: F4/UoM spec bugs: language key, empty values, ATINN
Symptom: F4 values in the app differ from SAP, show the wrong language or miss rows; characteristics show raw numbers; the default option is missing.
Cause: The DD07T-based F4 table is keyed on VALPOS + DOMVALUE_L without DDLANGUAGE so languages collapse into one; DOMVALUE_L is empty for one valid value; DD07T holds inactive versions too; MARM-ATINN is an internal id displayed via a conversion exit.
Fix: Add DDLANGUAGE to the key, remove DOMVALUE_L from the key, filter AS4LOCAL = 'A' and AS4VERS = '0000'; convert ATINN via a CABN-ATNAM join or CONVERSION_EXIT_ATINN_OUTPUT; join AUSP fully (OBJEK, ATINN, KLART, MAFID, ATZHL).
Tip: These are spec bugs, not code bugs; review the spec against its own attached screenshots before coding. A child bug marked Done does not mean the key in the spec was fixed.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: UI5 1.136: async init and camelCase data attributes are fatal
Symptom: The UI5 app sticks on the loading screen as if the backend were missing; log shows [FUTURE FATAL] 'Event Listener init must not have a return value' or 'Property or event "propagatemodel" does not exist'.
Cause: Component.init/onInit declared async returns a Promise, which UI5 1.136 treats as FUTURE FATAL. HTML lower-cases data-propagateModel so ComponentSupport silently drops the setting; the second error masks the first. Aggregation template bindings without templateShareable:false also warn.
Fix: Make init synchronous: super.init(); void this._runInit() with the async part split out. Write data attributes in dash-case (data-propagate-model); add templateShareable:false to nested/code-built bindings.
Tip: 'Cannot reproduce' often means an earlier error is masking the bug. If the FUTURE FATAL warning also appears on a healthy environment it is not the cause; apply the fix to every copy of the app.

LESSON LEARNED [ABAP & S/4]: Working safely on a customer's SAP DEV system
Symptom: Reference data 'does not exist'; SE80 has no Versions menu; CDS/RAP cannot be edited in SAP GUI; OData probes 404 on every path.
Cause: Master data is client-dependent; SE80's Utilities menu needs an open object; the object list lives in the transport's child tasks; CDS/behaviour definitions are only editable in ADT and SAP only auto-versions on transport release; the system has not activated the SICF service.
Fix: Confirm the client before reading data; open the object then Utilities > Versions > Generate version before editing; open every task of the transport; use Eclipse ADT; ask Basis to activate SICF or use a CAP bridge for HTTP tests.
Workaround: Copy the source to a local file as a backup before editing and add the fix to a modifiable transport.
Tip: If SAP asks for an SSCR access key, stop: you are about to modify SAP standard code. Version Management > Compare gives a diff usable in place of peer review.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: A shared UI library calls a backend action this product lacks
Symptom: A generic system error on Submit (sometimes on form load); Submit and Save Draft are blocked, all field errors hidden; network shows a POST to an action returning 404.
Cause: Drift between products: the shared UI library added a call to an action that exists only in another product, or exists on the dev branch but was not promoted to QAS. The UI wrapper returns without calling the submit handler when an optional rule errors.
Fix: Add the backend action or cherry-pick it to every environment branch that shipped the UI call. In the UI, an optional rule failure should only warn and still call the handler, in every copy of the wrapper.
Tip: Confirm the missing action by reading the service $metadata; a hand-made POST returns 403 for lack of a CSRF token and proves nothing. Watch for two independent faults happening at once.

LESSON LEARNED [ABAP & S/4]: Deduplicating the load file is not enough for S/4
Symptom: The customer cleaned the import file, yet loading it still creates duplicates.
Cause: New records are not matched against master data already in S/4; the target object's keys and rules decide part of what 'duplicate' means.
Fix: Match against live master data (OData/CDS/Integration Suite) and validate against the target object's keys/constraints; clarify one-off migration versus recurring load.
Tip: Check for an SAP MDG licence; MDG already has duplicate checks and match-and-merge.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: An abandoned page build or stale local model leaks into the next page
Symptom: Leaving a slow-loading CREATE page and opening an UPDATE page makes the UPDATE form enforce CREATE's mandatory fields; F5 clears it.
Cause: Two routes share one controller instance and the async page build does not check the route is still current; the shared 'local' model is last-response-wins with no template ID check; the old template structure is reused.
Fix: Add a page-request token incremented on every route match and check staleness after every await in route handlers and page builders; guard shared-model writes by template ID; reuse cache only when the template ID matches.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Radix ScrollArea breaks truncation and paints a background patch
Symptom: A long title pushes the sidebar wider and 'truncate' stops working; later a light rounded background patch appears under the cursor across several cards, mistaken for a hover highlight.
Cause: The Radix Viewport wraps content in a display:table div sized to content. The first fix used [&>div]:!w-full on the ROOT, which also hit the scrollbar sibling and stretched the thumb full width.
Fix: Fix it in the primitive: [&>div]:block! on the Viewport (Tailwind v4 puts ! at the end). Never target every direct child div of the root.
Tip: A shape extending beyond a component's bounds signals a sibling overlay (scrollbar, portal); list the root's children before blaming the OS or the bundle cache.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Flet 0.8x changes its API silently
Symptom: Startup fails at FilePicker(on_result=...); a red 'Unknown control: FilePicker' block with no exception; Dropdown ignores on_change; focus() does nothing with 'coroutine was never awaited'; DeprecationWarnings everywhere.
Cause: Flet 0.86 changed the API: FilePicker is a service (page.services), pick_files returns files; Dropdown uses on_select; focus/scroll_to are coroutines; ElevatedButton is deprecated in favour of Button.
Fix: Use the new API; call coroutines via page.run_task; add tests that BUILD the real shell and EVERY dialog with a fake page; promote Flet deprecations to errors in pytest.ini.
Tip: Unit tests on instances made with __new__ do not see wiring errors.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: A shipped feature hidden behind a preview flag with no default
Symptom: Users install the build and the new sidebar item is missing, looking as if the feature was never built.
Cause: The item is wrapped in a feature gate; the preview-feature entry lacks defaultEnabled and the resolver treats missing as false.
Fix: Set defaultEnabled true for features the requirement says must be visible, or state clearly in the report that users must enable it in Settings.
Workaround: Enable the preview feature in Settings.
Tip: Copying the neighbouring pattern (gate everything) can violate the actual requirement; verify the build from the user's point of view, not only in tests with the flag on.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Black window because clean() runs before build()
Symptom: After a successful login, the packaged app shows a completely black window with no error.
Cause: page.clean() runs before page.add(shell.build()); an exception in build() leaves an empty page, and the windowed build has no console so the traceback vanishes.
Fix: Build the new view before clearing the page so a failure keeps the old screen and shows a message; draw the empty state before reporting a load failure; write a rotating log file next to the executable.
Tip: Apply the build-before-clean guard everywhere this pattern appears.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Submit-time validation skips table rows inserted by rules
Symptom: A form submits with mandatory fields empty in table rows inserted by rules; the request is created then fails in the backend's async validation.
Cause: Submit-time validation skips every repeatable section, so the only guard for table rows is the add/edit row dialog; machine-inserted rows never pass through that dialog.
Fix: On submit, validate every row of every visible repeatable section with the same rules as the dialog, skipping deleted rows; skip fields targeted by SHOW/HIDE/EDITABLE/MANDATORY rules so users are not blocked by fields they cannot see.
Tip: Keep the 'blank' rule consistent between frontend (trim whitespace) and backend (falsy rejects 0). A TODO in the code can be a constraint still in force.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Testers see the old UI after deploy because of browser cache
Symptom: After a successful deploy, users and agents still run the old behaviour; Ctrl+Shift+R does not help.
Cause: Component-preload.js is cached (max-age=3600) or index.html has no cache-control so the browser uses old hashed chunks; an open SPA tab keeps old code in memory.
Fix: Serve index.html with no-cache and version the preload.
Workaround: In the tab, fetch Component-preload.js with {cache:'reload'} then location.reload(), or reopen the tab; tell QA they may need Ctrl+F5 for up to an hour.
Tip: Before testing a deploy, assert the running code contains a new symbol. Navigating to the same URL only changes the hash, it does not reload.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: CSS utility conflicts, overflow and dark-theme dropdowns
Symptom: A name cell stretches the row and the value cell disappears; a long URL pushes the whole column; a date column wraps on non-English machines; a dark-theme <select> list is unreadable when open; a dialog title drops below the X button.
Cause: Concatenating 'w-full' with 'w-56' lets stylesheet order decide; break-word does not affect intrinsic width; locale month names are longer; the OS draws select popups with a light palette without color-scheme; an unlayered global h2 rule beats Tailwind utilities.
Fix: Use tailwind-merge (cn) or size from the container grid; overflow-wrap:anywhere with min-w-0; locale-independent date format; set color-scheme: dark at the dark-theme root and give select/option an opaque background; a margin-reset class on the shared DialogTitle.
Tip: Verify with computed style and bounding rect, not screenshots, when the OS draws the element. Fix sibling apps using the same pattern too.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: pnpm/biome/vite monorepo tooling traps
Symptom: 'pnpm run check' reformats hundreds of unrelated files; workspace typecheck fails on missing modules; pnpm demands purging node_modules; vite.config fails to import shared TS; the TS build rejects enums and parameter properties.
Cause: The check script runs biome --write on the whole repo while the base branch is not clean; 'pnpm add -Dw' can unlink sibling projects; corepack's default pnpm major differs from the lockfile; vite.config is Node ESM; erasableSyntaxOnly forbids enums (TS1294).
Fix: Run only 'biome check --write <your files>' and stage only your files; run a full 'pnpm install' after 'pnpm add -Dw'; pin pnpm via corepack; import shared code in vite.config via a relative '.js' path; use a const object + union instead of enums.
Tip: Before accepting blame for a red gate, prove it pre-exists: rerun on a clean base and check 'git diff --name-only' does not touch the failing area.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: UI5 web components are invisible to jsdom role queries
Symptom: Role+name journeys find 0 textboxes under jsdom although the page renders inputs; in the real app the fields have no accessible name either.
Cause: @ui5/webcomponents-react custom elements never upgrade in jsdom; form Field labels are bare spans without an htmlFor/id pair, which getByText tests do not catch.
Fix: Run role-based acceptance tests in a real browser (Playwright/Chromium); give each control an explicit accessibleName and add tests asserting fields are reachable by role+name.
Tip: To tell a React page from old UI5 use a positive probe (#root has a React fiber) and a negative probe (no window.sap.ui); ui5-* tags prove nothing.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Desktop window sizes are logical pixels
Symptom: On a laptop the composer at the bottom of the app is off-screen and cannot be clicked, although an identical earlier report was a false alarm.

Fix: Pick the default size for the smallest expected screen and scale factor (e.g. 700 logical height); record the reason in a comment.
Tip: Same symptom, different cause: do not dismiss a repeat report just because the last one was an artifact.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: React effect and state patterns that often cause bugs
Symptom: A worker is killed at its first message; lint flags setState-in-effect or ref-during-render; a skip-first flag does not skip; the first dragover is ignored; an optional parameter receives a MouseEvent.
Cause: Unmount cleanup runs on every re-render; syncing props into state in an effect; StrictMode double mount consumes a one-shot flag; a handler reads state before React re-renders; onClick={fn} passes the event as the first argument.
Fix: Tear down on pagehide instead of effect cleanup; key the component by the record being edited instead of syncing props; compare with a last-saved ref instead of counting runs; read hot values from a ref; wrap handlers (() => fn()).
Tip: Distinguish a missing key ('use defaults') from an empty array ('user removed everything'); always persisting defaults freezes the list against later additions.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: React Query prefix invalidation refetches active queries
Symptom: Clicking Create fires several extra full-list requests whose results are discarded; fixing the create handler removed only one.
Cause: Invalidating a broad key prefix also matches the create page's active queries and React Query refetches every active match; the WebSocket handler also invalidates the same prefix on every push.
Fix: Define in one module which keys go stale when an entity changes and use it at every invalidation site (socket, create, reply). Test with a real QueryClient, not spies.
Tip: Count requests in a real browser via CDP; monkey-patch invalidateQueries with a stack trace to find callers. Check POST status, since 429 rate limits can fake a 'fixed' count.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Vite web worker traps
Symptom: The worker 404s at runtime, or never answers with no error, or grows from 8 KB to 2.3 MB.
Cause: new URL() for a worker must be a relative literal (the '@' alias does not resolve); a worker importing import.meta.env dies at module evaluation before onmessage exists; dynamic imports of large data are inlined into the worker chunk.
Fix: Use a relative literal URL; pass config into the worker as data in an init message; serve large tables as static files and fetch them.
Tip: An error-reporting channel that itself drops unknown sessions is not a diagnostic tool.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Admin list screens not designed for scale
Symptom: The editor shows exactly 50 rows and row 51 is unreachable; the local demo with 3 rows was fine.
Cause: The service fetches $top=50 with no $skip/$filter/$count; the table renders rows.map with no paging/filter/virtualisation; the engine picks rules by linear scan.
Fix: Add server-side paging/filtering ($top/$skip/$filter/$count) and a shared data grid, index rules in the engine; test with realistic data volumes.
Tip: The old system is not a safe oracle for volume behaviour. 'N/N routes live' may be one component with a variant prop, so check ported behaviour rather than counting routes.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: input+datalist is autocomplete, not a dropdown
Symptom: The choice editor shows only the selected option; a placeholder workaround fixes it once then breaks after the next pick.
Cause: A datalist filters suggestions by the input's text; any prefilled valid label filters the list down to one entry.
Fix: Replace it with a self-drawn option list re-rendered from state on each open, plus a separate free-text field for an 'other' answer.
Tip: When a widget misbehaves, check its contract matches the need before patching how data is fed to it.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Conditional forms: hidden fields still required, stale answers still shown
Symptom: The Next button stays disabled waiting for a question not on screen; dependent questions still show after their parent has been hidden.
Cause: The required check counts hidden fields; visibility only considers the parent's saved ANSWER, not whether the parent is visible.
Fix: Required/filled/review logic skips hidden parts; compute visibility as reachability (parent visible AND answered), iterating to a fixed point so cycles terminate.
Tip: Keep answers while hidden so re-showing restores them, but exclude hidden parts from review and export.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Status colours and warnings must be orthogonal
Symptom: A warning node hides in-progress status; after separating warnings from the colour scale, a parent turns green when one child finishes and a blocked parent loses its red.
Cause: Warnings were modelled on the same severity scale as progress; the rewritten rollup rule weakened a neighbouring rule.
Fix: Status colour with blockers overriding everything below (itself or descendants); done only when every child is done; warnings are a separate badge (owned vs inherited) with the reason on hover.
Tip: Colour semantics are a linked system: change one rule and retest the others, including the hardest case (one blocked leaf under all-green).

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: TanStack Router does not discover routes when using a virtual config
Symptom: A new route file in the routes folder has no effect; tsc says the path is not assignable to keyof FileRoutesByPath, rebuilding does not help.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Patching a running UI5 controller requires rebinding events
Symptom: A controller method patched in the page seems not to run, or a dialog seems stuck.
Cause: Press handlers in an XML view are bound at view creation, so replacing the controller method does not change the bound handler; a DOM click on a MessageBox button may not close it.
Fix: Rebind via the control's event registry (btn.mEventRegistry.press[i].fFunction) and close dialogs via the UI5 API.
Tip: For standalone test pages: load lodash/deepdash as UMD and sap.ui.predefine; do not stub 'async' as a no-op, it silently skips loops and tests pass for the wrong reason.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: A CORS allowlist blocks fetches from a desktop renderer
Symptom: Fetching from a Tauri renderer to a backend API fails although the API works from its own web console.
Cause: The API's CORS only allowlists its own frontend origin; the tauri.localhost/localhost origin gets no access-control-allow-origin header.
Fix: Proxy the call through the Rust backend (a Tauri command) instead of fetching from the renderer.
Tip: Test with curl sending a real Origin header to see whether access-control-allow-origin comes back.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Layout regressions only visible when rendered
Symptom: Toolbar buttons pushed off the right edge; the leftmost node clipped; stray page scrollbars; a 100-node tree unreadable.
Cause: A flex-1 input takes the whole row; offsets computed by centring (negative x); canvas height based on a guessed header height; a fully horizontal tree layout grows without bound in width.
Fix: Fixed input width, real padding and sizing by content extent, full-height flex columns; wide fixed-depth trees use vertical tiers with only the leaf tier horizontal.
Tip: Type-checks and builds do not catch these; verify element rects against innerWidth from the DOM. Layout constants tuned for one page shape go wrong when the page changes shape.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Inline editing and re-render details
Symptom: Spaces vanish while typing; moving between editable table rows takes two clicks; a newly created input loses focus; the 'next' screen keeps the old scroll position.
Cause: Re-render writes the trimmed value into the focused input; the table rebuilds on blur before the click fires; default mousedown blurs the new input; the scroll reset targets one pane but a responsive breakpoint moves scrolling to the window.
Fix: Skip the focused element when repainting; use one document-level mousedown handler with preventDefault; reset every possible scroller and call focus({preventScroll:true}).
Tip: A scroll reset aimed at one container is only right when the layout has a single scroller.

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Limits of local HTML files (file://)
Symptom: A form opened from file:// cannot save the answer file; the page cannot fetch the status file next to it; saving uploads in localStorage exceeds quota.
Cause: Browser sandbox rules for file:// pages and localStorage size limits.
Fix: Serve it through a small local server bound only to loopback that writes output and shuts down on submit; store file bytes server-side (disk/SQLite), not base64 in localStorage.
Tip: Bind local tool servers to the loopback interface only.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Shared Firebase project: bulk identity deletes hit other apps; parameterless clients stick to (default)
Symptom: One app's 'purge test users' also deletes another app's users and Firebase Auth accounts; a dev service reads and writes production data; the app writes to (default) though it meant to use a named database.
Cause: Firebase Auth is project-scoped and Firestore database-scoped; many services share (default) and the user collection. A Firestore client created with no parameter is hard-bound to (default).
Fix: One Firestore database per app/environment, pass the database id explicitly and pin it in deploy config with a guard. Put an app filter in front of every bulk identity delete.
Workaround: If the database cannot be split yet, use a collection prefix inside (default).
Tip: Before a bulk delete, list every service sharing the project and their database env vars. Treat 'database id not set' as production.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Small Flet layout and input traps
Symptom: The composer is only ~370px wide in a wide window; a long modal form runs past its buttons; a picker dialog does not close after choosing; Enter inserts a newline instead of sending.
Cause: A TextField in a Row without expand keeps its intrinsic width; the dialog body is unbounded and does not scroll; the caller popping the dialog races with a shell rebuild; the field lacks shift_enter.
Fix: expand=True for the composer; scroll the dialog body with height = min(content estimate, ~62% of the window); the picker closes itself before calling the callback; opt into TextField shift_enter per field.
Tip: Do not handle the Enter key yourself for IME users (e.g. Vietnamese telex).

LESSON LEARNED [Fiori / UI5 & Frontend]: Embedding a remote web console in a Tauri app
Symptom: An external web UI needs to be embedded in a desktop app view.
Cause: An iframe only works when the target sends no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors; Tauri capabilities limited to the main window keep the remote frame away from the IPC bridge.
Fix: Check response headers first; only allow http/https iframe src (reject javascript:/data:), report invalid URLs; sandbox the iframe.
Tip: Mock fixtures named like the real menu can mislead; find the component that actually renders the menu.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Per-host SSO callbacks require registering every hostname at every IdP
Symptom: Login from a new custom domain returns to the old host or fails with redirect_uri_mismatch. One of Cloud Run's two default hostnames fails although it is in the allowlist.
Cause: The callback is derived from the request host so each hostname sends a different redirect_uri, and Google matches URIs exactly (including a trailing /). SSO_REDIRECT_BASE, when set, wins over the request host; removing it also empties the post-login redirect allowlist built from it.
Fix: Register each hostname's callback at each provider BEFORE changing config and set the allowed-redirect-hosts list explicitly. Or pin SSO_REDIRECT_BASE to one canonical hostname in deployed environments, leaving it empty only locally (register both 127.0.0.1 and localhost).
Workaround: Pin one canonical callback base (users always land on the canonical host) or register callbacks for every hostname.
Tip: Compare the redirect_uri the app actually sends with what is registered before blaming the app. The post-login allowlist only controls next=, it registers nothing with the IdP.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Moving where permissions are read without moving where they are written
Symptom: Add user says 'user already exists' for someone not in the new roster; an invited staff member gets 403 on every workspace call although listed on the People screen.
Cause: The screen reads the new roster but the duplicate check still reads the old collection and invites still write to the old place. The membership helper returns silently (wrapped in except: pass) when no company is selected.
Fix: Give the new store a complete write side (invite, edit, remove, adopt on first login); adopt people who already have a grant instead of refusing. The membership helper returns a bool and logs the reason on every early return.
Tip: When the read side moves, grep every writer and every duplicate/existence check against the old source. A correct but useless refusal is still a bug.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Secrets leaked via chat, tickets, git remotes, cf env and transcripts
Symptom: Plaintext OAuth tokens in clones' origin URLs; one 'cf env' wrote several client secrets to disk; an admin password in a ticket description; secrets and private keys pasted or printed into chat/transcripts.
Cause: Cloning with token-in-URL; cf env dumps credentials of every bound service; sharing plaintext credentials for convenience; a redaction regex that did not match so keys were printed.
Fix: Move git auth to a credential helper or SSH and rotate the token; never save cf env output; rotate every credential that appeared in chat or tickets and remove it from the ticket. In CI store client bindings as masked variables and mint short-lived tokens per job.
Tip: Mask secrets in all command output, record only length and hash; test redaction before relying on it. Agents must not submit login forms or type passcodes for the user; deleting a local copy is not rotating.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: A multi-user retrofit leaks through shared stores
Symptom: A two-person e2e shows members seeing other people's project names, seeing projects they were removed from, and ordinary members creating accounts for arbitrary emails.
Cause: Registry rows live in a collection every member can read; creating a project grants owner and the right to invite unknown emails to everyone; tokens issued before removal stay valid until expiry.
Fix: Filter every cross-project read by visibility, put account creation behind an explicit permission, read grants live or keep access tokens short (~5 minutes). Run a multi-user e2e (create, share, revoke, delete) on every auth change.
Tip: Deny by default. Never make an endpoint that exchanges an email for a token.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Plaintext secrets in env vars and shared keys give false security
Symptom: API keys and DB passwords visible in Cloud Run revision config; one API key shared in a settings file; a proposed design hard-codes half a key in the binary.
Cause: The deploy pipeline passes every value, secrets included, as plain env vars instead of Secret Manager references; one key for all users for convenience; believing a compiled binary hides a key.
Fix: Move sensitive values into Secret Manager and reference them with --set-secrets; use per-user identity (SSO) instead of shared keys. State plainly that a key in a binary can always be extracted; the real secret must live with what the user holds.
Workaround: Limit who has run.services.get on the project; if a shared key is unavoidable, document that revoking means rotating for everyone.
Tip: Anyone who can read the service sees the values, so do not copy them into notes or logs. Delete temporary admin clients right after use.
