LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: An agent silent in a new channel/community: missing membership and directory record
Symptom: Tagging the agent gets no reply; the seat log says 'agent invocation refused' with 403 at the lease endpoint, or 'restricted: not a relay member' and exits.
Cause: Claiming an invite only admits the person's key, not the agent's. The agent also needs bot membership in the channel and a directory record (kind:10100) on THAT relay listing the channel id; the UI shows none of these gaps, and clients may skip updates when 'profile unchanged'.
Fix: Add a relay membership row for the agent key (admin), add it to the channel as a bot, republish the directory record signed by the seat key keeping status/respond_to/skills and adding the channel id, then read it back. Then send a NEW mention since refused events are not retried.
Tip: Grep the agent log by seat/relay for 'agent invocation refused' vs 'admitted by relay-issued lease'. Two hostnames for one relay are two different relays with separate logs; keep an agent onboarding checklist.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Community move/mount forks agent identity
Symptom: After re-keying/moving a relay or running mount, an agent seat goes silent, is absent from the relay roster and cannot authenticate; the log says a NEW key was minted.
Cause: The keyring is stored per community id; mounting a new community id without the old keyring, or a mount minting keys for every seat missing locally, creates a forked identity. Mount also changes the locally active community.
Fix: Copy the whole keyring folder to the new community id before mounting and verify the pubkey matches the identity file. Mint only needed seats via the keyring API; move existing keys to another host, never mint a second key.
Workaround: If a new key was already minted, delete the new key folder and copy again.
Tip: A seat's private key belongs to one host; record which host holds which key.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: A GDPR-erased user loops back to the login page with no error
Symptom: SSO 'broken for one person': after signing in they are sent back to the login page, no error, no sso_error; re-inviting does nothing.
Cause: Two gates read two different fields: the login gate reads app_access (left intact by erasure) and grants a session, the request gate reads status (now inactive) and rejects every request. Erasure blanked the record (merge=True) instead of deleting it, so the invite was never used.
Fix: Delete the record outright or keep a tombstone with no role/access; derive 'may log in' and 'may keep a session' from the same field. To restore a person, reactivate rather than delete the tombstone.
Workaround: Reactivate via the admin endpoint or a masked Firestore PATCH.
Tip: Search by status==inactive + erased_at, not by email (it was blanked). An unused invite is a diagnostic clue.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Erasure misses reference fields so erased people still get mail
Symptom: An erased person still receives customer emails about several tickets.
Cause: Erasure only cleared contact fields; the followers array (CC on all mail) and requester fields were not searched and cleared. Two deletion paths (erasure and offboarding) keep different field lists; autolink/invite re-adds erased addresses.
Fix: Keep one shared list of person-bearing fields (including followers, requester*), search places where the person is only referenced, block autolink/invite for erased addresses. Run a data repair for records already written.
Tip: Separate 'where the person is a contact' from 'where the person is referenced'. Fixing code does not fix data already written.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Verifying Firebase tokens outside GCP and the login redirect loop
Symptom: On a non-GCP host every login returns 401 and the login page refreshes endlessly with nested /login?next=/login?next=...
Cause: firebase_admin.verify_id_token needs google.auth.default() and raises DefaultCredentialsError without ADC/metadata server; the SPA's 401 handler uses the login page itself as next.
Fix: Fall back to public-key verification (google.oauth2.id_token with the securetoken certs), checking aud, iss, sub; do not carry a service-account key to another cloud for something that only needs a public key. Do not redirect while on /login and reject next starting with /login.
Tip: Firebase authorizedDomains only guards popup/redirect sign-in, not email/password. REST identitytoolkit needs the x-goog-user-project header.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Removing a back-compat auth fallback requires a backfill first
Symptom: Users of another product show on the Users screen and get deleted by mistake; adding a filter changes nothing; removing the fallback causes AttributeError or locks users out.
Cause: A bridge rule treats users with no per-app access map as implicit members, and the backfill was never done. A second copy of the legacy rule sits in the login controller; deleting the '(not has_map) or ...' clause also removes the short-circuit protecting '.get' on a None map.
Fix: Backfill explicit grants from the canonical source first, then add the filter, then remove the fallback in every file and normalise the map to a dict. The wrong order is either a no-op or a mass lockout.
Tip: grep every copy of the legacy rule before removing it. Expect a one-time mass logout if session cookies carry claims resolved through the old rule.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Silent identity refusals and dangerous defaults
Symptom: Users sign in but see nothing (403 'not a member'); after an admin 'fix' they cannot sign in with no message; a personal account is granted production admin on every start.
Cause: Boot-time seeding grants admin without attaching a workspace; tombstones are checked first and return silently; a hard-coded seed-admin list applies when the env var is unset; empty/unknown roles are normalised to the customer role.
Fix: Every deny branch must log the reason and where to look; seeded admins need a workspace and skip erased addresses. Set the seed-admin env explicitly in every environment and review existing allow entries (setting env does not revoke).
Tip: The common pattern is two subsystems disagreeing without saying so: check tombstone, allow entry and membership together. New intake paths must share the server-side company derivation logic.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Restoring deleted Firebase Auth accounts from an export
Symptom: accounts:batchCreate fails for every federated account with 'invalid federate identifier'; restored password hashes may be unusable; replaying the backup collides with accounts users have recreated.
Cause: The export writes the provider's raw GUID into federatedId; password hashes only work with the project's hash config; users who signed in again already have a new uid with an empty profile that looks normal.
Fix: Drop federatedId (providerId + rawId is enough); fetch signerKey, saltSeparator, rounds, memoryCost from the identitytoolkit admin config and pass them with the hashes. Split the backup into missing accounts (recreate under the original uid) and returning accounts (merge lost fields into the current uid).
Tip: Verify the restore by email coverage (nobody missing a doc or account), not by counts. Keep the backup in a dated archive with a README of these traps.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: An OAuth state check that compares a value with itself
Symptom: Login works and looks CSRF-protected, but the state check never fails.
Cause: verify_state(x, x) is called with the same value twice; a signed state only proves the server created it, not that this browser started the flow (login CSRF).
Fix: Bind state to a short-lived signed cookie set when login starts, compare at callback and clear it on every callback; make comparison parameters keyword-only.
Tip: Two positional string parameters of the same type are an easy place for self-comparison to hide. Add a test: same state, different browser, no cookie must fail.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Containment rules for tool-running agents
Symptom: Risk of prompt injection escalating tool rights, confused deputy, or secrets leaking into tool processes.
Cause: The model reads messages anyone can write; child processes inherit the parent environment; a shared agent may run with owner rights.
Fix: Check grants at CALL time, not planning time; effective rights = agent AND invoker; unclassified tools default to most restricted; child processes get a minimal allowlisted env, never os.environ. Check path traversal after resolving the path; never accept launch commands or server paths from messages.
Tip: Treat prompt injection as normal input; the real proof is a test where the model follows the injection and the call is still refused.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: A dot folder nearly pushed a whole browser profile
Symptom: The first push of an unversioned workspace nearly included saved passwords, cookies and history.
Cause: A scratch folder starting with a dot held a full Chromium profile used for automation and a dev DB with real users; plain ls skips it.
Fix: Write .gitignore before the first commit (venv, dev DB, local config, browser profiles, .env), grep for secret patterns, then verify the pushed tree with git ls-tree on the remote.
Tip: Ignore rules only protect git; move credential-bearing folders out of the workspace. Check repo visibility before committing environment identifiers.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: google-auth cannot verify ID tokens without requests
Symptom: Google sign-in reaches the last step then fails: 'The requests library is not installed'.
Cause: Only google-auth was pinned; id_token verification uses google.auth.transport.requests which needs requests/urllib3. The import is lazy and no test calls Google so boot and tests stay green.
Fix: Pin requests and urllib3 explicitly; add an offline test that imports the transport and asserts a broken token fails with a token error, not a library error.
Tip: A lazily imported dependency on a path no test exercises is invisible to every check; a debug page that does the real work and prints the real error finds it at once.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: A git push gate that cannot see commits; bots counted as members
Symptom: Rules like 'agents do not write main', path-based rules or commit signature checks cannot be expressed on the relay's git host.
Cause: The pre-receive hook only sends HMAC'd ref updates (old/new oid, ref), no commit/path content; on push the Bot role is promoted to Member.
Fix: Add an agent identity check in the push gate (fail closed on lookup errors) and have the hook send commits and changed paths per ref bound into the HMAC. Merge controls (required checks, review, CODEOWNERS) belong on a real forge.
Tip: Old relays ignore unknown rule names; verify enforcement end to end with a real push.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Roles stored in the wrong place leak admin rights
Symptom: An admin of one org invited to another org as a member can administer that org; after one change every member can open the admin page.
Cause: One installation-wide role on the user row; later a convenience grant made everyone org_admin of their personal org.
Fix: Two axes: system role on the user, org role on the membership, nobody grants above their own level; invites/grants never confer system roles. Clients get is_admin from the server instead of computing it from role strings.
Tip: A convenience grant on an object every account owns is effectively an installation-wide grant.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Physical controls beat model refusals
Symptom: An exfiltration prompt is refused by the model, which looks like a working control.
Cause: Model refusals and intake command filtering are procedure, not a physical wall. The real walls are the server-side push gate and network egress (internal Docker network + allow-list proxy).
Fix: Prove controls with hard walls (proxy 403, pre-receive deny). Repos outside the relay are protected via a credential-holding bridge and host-side branch protection; agents run only in the sandbox.
Tip: An agent running outside the sandbox with the user's token cannot be controlled by the relay; only a server-side runner gives full control.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Isolate sensitive PII and keep it out of logs
Symptom: Personal identifiers risk leaking into work projects, the orchestrator or logs.
Cause: Logs and cross-project notes naturally repeat the values being processed.
Fix: Store PII only in a dedicated isolated project; never repeat full identifiers in logs or other projects, refer by a short non-identifying suffix. Do not store third-party identifying data seen incidentally (e.g. in sample images).

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Checking redirect_uri registration without a human: works for Google, not Entra
Symptom: SSO setup errors seem to need someone clicking through consent to diagnose. Probing the Microsoft authorize endpoint with a made-up redirect_uri still returns HTTP 200 as if valid.
Cause: Google validates redirect_uri before authenticating anyone, while an Entra tenant only validates redirect_uri after sign-in.
Fix: For Google, fetch the authorization URL server-side (curl -L or follow the Location from /login): a valid URI reaches the sign-in page, an invalid one stops at redirect_uri_mismatch; change the Host header to test each hostname. For Entra, check in the portal or have a real person sign in from that host.
Tip: No AADSTS error at the authorize step does not prove the URI is registered. Classic OAuth clients cannot be edited with gcloud; register URIs in the console.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Azure client secret 'invalid' because copying lost characters
Symptom: AADSTS7000215 'Invalid client secret' for days although app id and tenant are right.
Cause: The pasted secret value lost its '~' characters (38 instead of 40). The portal's 'Secret ID' GUID can never be used to authenticate.
Fix: Compare the length with the canonical copy and ask about '~' before requesting a new secret. Take the running copy from the deployment's secret store (e.g. 'gcloud secrets versions access latest').
Tip: When a credential is missing locally, check the running service's secret store first. Strip gcloud's trailing newline when saving to a file; a secret's Value is shown in full only once at creation.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Device-code flow fails silently: Conditional Access or Keycloak consent
Symptom: Device codes keep expiring 'unused' although the user says they signed in; the CLI never gets a token.
Cause: Tenant Conditional Access blocks device-code flow (AADSTS53003 shows only in the browser) and the polling client only sees authorization_pending. Keycloak hard-codes a consent screen for the device grant (RFC 8628); users think they are done after the IdP page and miss the 'Yes' button.
Fix: Use authorization-code flow + PKCE with a loopback redirect (like gh/gcloud); keep device flow only as a fallback when there is no browser.
Tip: An expired code does not mean the user ignored it; ask them. On Keycloak, a browser session with no offline session for the client means consent was not completed; run interactive scripts in the background with 'python -u' so the code prints immediately.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: SPA vs Web redirect platform changes secret requirements and token lifetime
Symptom: AADSTS700025, then AADSTS9002327, refresh tokens dying exactly after 24h (AADSTS700084), then AADSTS7000218 after switching to Web.
Cause: A redirect URI registered under Single-page application makes the client public, requires an Origin header and caps refresh tokens at 24h. The Web platform is confidential: secret required, long-lived refresh tokens.
Fix: Desktop/unattended tools should register under 'Mobile and desktop applications' (PKCE, no secret, long-lived tokens) or Web (with a secret that must be rotated).
Workaround: For SPA, send an Origin header matching the redirect and log in again daily.
Tip: AADSTS7000215 is checked before the platform so it says nothing about URI registration. Refresh tokens rotate; always store the newest.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Storing secrets in a local app
Symptom: Risk of tokens leaking to the page, being overwritten by their own masked value, or 'encrypting' secrets with a key file next to the database; a stored key turns out to look like another provider's token.
Cause: Bulk config reads push everything to the page; masked values can be saved back; removing a provider keeps the old key. A key next to the ciphertext protects nothing.
Fix: Keep secrets in a separate table that is never read back out, nodes store only the secret NAME, only the server engine reads it; show a masked tail and have the server refuse to write masked-looking values; delete keys when a provider is removed. Encrypt at rest with the OS keystore (DPAPI/Credential Manager) and refuse to store plaintext without it.
Workaround: Instrument the page (fetch, paste events) and watch the DB to prove where a wrong value came from.
Tip: Reject keys that duplicate another provider's secret and check vendor prefixes. Accept secret values via stdin; no API/CLI route returns the value.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Entra mailbox permissions: the account that created the app confers nothing
Symptom: The app is assumed to read its creator's mailbox, but an app-only token with a valid secret still gets 403 on every mailbox.
Cause: Rights depend on the permission TYPE: delegated Mail.Read reads only the signed-in user's mailbox; application Mail.Read reads EVERY mailbox unless an Exchange application access policy restricts it. An app with a mail-sounding name may have no mail permission at all.
Fix: Shared mailbox run unattended: application Mail.Read + New-ApplicationAccessPolicy restricted to a mail-enabled group containing only that mailbox, verified with Test-ApplicationAccessPolicy (propagation up to 1 hour). Per-user tools: delegated with refresh tokens.
Tip: Read the token's roles/scp claims to see what was really consented. After the policy the token still has Mail.Read; only a real 403 on another mailbox proves the fence.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Accepting a new attachment reference form safely
Symptom: Adding a 'reference' form for a field the client renders as an href risks reopening XSS via javascript: URLs.
Cause: A client-supplied string flows straight into an href attribute.
Fix: Accept only relative paths with no scheme/host, take only the filename, take the workspace from the authenticated route. Confirm the file exists with store.stat (fail closed), use the store's size and rebuild the stored value server-side.
Tip: Issue upload sessions only after the same allow-list checks as inline files. Check identity before file type so errors do not reveal accepted file types.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Accepting a new attachment reference form safely
Symptom: Adding a 'reference' form for a field the client renders as an href risks reopening XSS via javascript: URLs.
Cause: A client-supplied string flows straight into an href attribute.
Fix: Accept only relative paths with no scheme/host, take only the filename, take the workspace from the authenticated route. Confirm the file exists with store.stat (fail closed), use the store's size and rebuild the stored value server-side.
Tip: Issue upload sessions only after the same allow-list checks as inline files. Check identity before file type so errors do not reveal accepted file types.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Graph Sites.Selected grants nothing without a per-site grant
Symptom: The app-only token is issued fine but GET /sites/... returns 403 accessDenied.
Cause: Sites.Selected only permits per-site grants; until an admin POSTs /sites/{id}/permissions the site is invisible.
Fix: Have an admin grant a per-site role (Graph POST with a Sites.FullControl.All token, Graph Explorer or Grant-PnPAzureADAppSitePermission). Do not grant tenant-wide Sites.ReadWrite/FullControl.All.
Tip: Probe end to end (resolve, list, upload, download with byte compare, delete) and exit 0 only when both read and write pass.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Microsoft SSO pinned to one tenant blocks outside customers
Symptom: Invited customers get 'Selected user account does not exist in tenant' and no invite is used; some outside users can sign in though.
Cause: The Microsoft SSO authority is set to the vendor's tenant GUID instead of 'common'/'organizations'; the outside users who succeed are B2B guests in that tenant.
Fix: Invite customers as B2B guests, or make the app registration multi-tenant with the 'organizations' tenant, or use Google SSO/federation. Long term: per-company IdP config resolved from the email domain.
Workaround: Add the user as a B2B guest and grant access to the app.
Tip: Find which tenant a domain belongs to via the public OIDC discovery document. The IdP gate and the app's allow-list are independent; both must let the user through.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Rolling out an app-owned permission roster safely
Symptom: Switching login to a new roster could lock out dozens of real users, cause logout loops or blank screens in unseeded environments.
Cause: The new roster is partly seeded; login and the per-request session check read different sources; an empty collection is treated as 'nobody may enter'; one person has several uids; a missing env var defaults to the prod roster.
Fix: Ship in observe mode (log who strict mode would refuse) then switch to strict via a committed config. Treat an empty roster as 'not seeded' and fall back; login and session share one overlay; declare the environment name explicitly in each deployment's vars file.
Tip: Read the observe log for newly onboarded outside users before enabling strict. Keep the mode flag in deploy config because --update-env-vars reapplies and silently overwrites manual edits.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Okta refuses login: custom authorization server without an access policy
Symptom: The Okta page says 'You are not allowed to access this application' before the callback, although assignment and sign-on policy allow it.
Cause: The 'default' custom authorization server (/oauth2/default) needs an access policy that a new Integrator org lacks, so /authorize fails with no_matching_policy. Signing up via the default developer page creates an Auth0 tenant with different paths.
Fix: Point the issuer at the org authorization server (/oauth2, endpoints /oauth2/v1/...) or add an access policy for the client id. Sign up for the 'Integrator Free Plan' to get a real *.okta.com org.
Tip: Read the Okta System Log filtered by app first; the error text names the wrong gate. Register callback URLs for every environment or get 400 redirect_uri.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Metered AI API keys need spend limits and per-feature switches
Symptom: Setting one provider API key silently moves three features to the new provider and enables a paid translation feature; AI routes only need login so any customer can call them repeatedly.
Cause: Every feature's is_enabled() only checks that the key has a value; AI routes have no rate limiter, no cache, and the default model id was never called for real.
Fix: Each costly feature gets its own switch, off by default; a rate limit shared across instances per caller and workspace. Default model ids proven by a real call; deploy code before setting the key.
Workaround: Disable the feature in workspace settings and set tight limits in dev.
Tip: Before adding a key, inventory every caller of the provider module. A wrong model id on a best-effort path that swallows errors fails silently.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Google OAuth sign-in for a local web app
Symptom: Sign-in fails with 403 org_internal; later the user reports done but the app received nothing.
Cause: The OAuth app audience is 'Internal', allowing only the owning Workspace org, so personal Gmail is refused before reaching the app. The 'done' report was premature.
Fix: Set the audience to External; use a server-side code flow with only openid/email/profile scopes; check aud, iss, exp, nonce, email_verified claims. Verify completion in the database, not by report.
Tip: Keep the sign-in wall OFF by default until one successful sign-in, or you lock yourself out. Cookies issued for 127.0.0.1 are not sent to 'localhost'.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Imperative legacy CAP authorization and non-preventive SoD
Symptom: A legacy backend audit: roles are app-managed seed data, not XSUAA; a client-credentials token with only the uaa.resource scope can still read CAP service data.
Cause: Authorization is scattered as imperative checks in handlers with bypasses for system users, only one @restrict is effective, no field-level authz. Maker/checker only applies if the flow is configured correctly.
Fix: Enforce SoD on the server (reject maker == checker), move checks to declarative @restrict/role scopes, validate scopes on technical tokens.
Tip: When porting to a new stack, describe the legacy authz first (with file:line citations) as the baseline to reproduce or deliberately tighten.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: A CSRF helper sending fake tokens
Symptom: Mutating requests fail erratically or pass with invalid tokens; tests asserting on the first response are flaky.
Cause: The helper caches the string 'local' as the CSRF token when the fetch returns nothing, fetches from a hard-coded /index.html instead of the service root, compares 'Required' case-sensitively and ignores tokens returned on non-2xx responses.
Fix: Leave the token undefined when absent; fetch from the request URL, then $metadata, then the service root. Compare case-insensitively, send no-cache headers and accept tokens from non-2xx responses.
Tip: E2E tests must wait for the full condition (every call finished 2xx) so they wait out the 403 -> fetch -> replay sequence instead of racing it.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Roles taken only from the token; IdP realm shared between environments
Symptom: Users see no data ('No workspace-wide editing role'); brokered SSO users do not show in the IdP admin user list.
Cause: The app resolves roles only from the token's roles claim; dev and prod share one Keycloak realm and client so grants apply to both; brokered usernames are not people's names.
Fix: Assign client roles (not realm roles) in Role mapping, filtered by client; find users by email.
Tip: Do not loosen auth or edit app code to fake rights. A wrong Basic-auth username on Jira gives 401 at /myself but a misleading 404 on issues.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Credential handling in an HTTP node
Symptom: Risk of leaking tokens on redirect, empty credentials causing confusing 401s, or a hidden body still being sent.
Cause: urllib copies every header (Authorization included) to the redirected request; a missing secret silently becomes an empty header; an old body config remains after switching the method to GET.
Fix: Drop Authorization when redirecting to another host (netloc including port); fail before the call naming the missing secret; refuse when both a header and a secret set Authorization; only send a body for POST/PUT/PATCH.
Tip: Pass user-entered text to shell commands via environment variables, never interpolated into the script.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Audit trail vs erasure, and separating logs
Symptom: A matching/dedup product creates an audit trail with names, addresses and tax ids: a second copy of personal data that must be both immutable and erasable.
Cause: Storing values instead of references; mixing technical logs with business audit.
Fix: Technical logs carry no payload and live in the platform's log service; business audit lives inside the tenant boundary, stores references (id, rule version, actor, time, hash) resolved at read time, append-only with a hash chain.
Tip: Needs legal sign-off, not engineers' assumptions.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Client-side uninstall does not end access
Symptom: 'setup --remove' removes hooks but the 90-day login remains; running setup again has full access without signing in.
Cause: The removal does not revoke the refresh token.
Fix: On remove/uninstall, revoke every stored refresh token (per issuer) and delete the helper folder; verify the old token returns invalid_grant.
Tip: Client-side removal is only cleanup; the real lock is disabling the user at the IdP. A borrowed machine also keeps the browser's IdP session and chat history.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Prefer email-based grants over bearer invite codes
Symptom: Invite codes need expiry, revocation, use counts and hashing, and recipients are still confused.
Cause: An invite code is a forwardable bearer token.
Fix: Grant by email in the admin panel, materialised into a membership on each SSO login; revocation deletes grant, membership and sessions in one transaction; require email_verified; the refusal page states exactly which address was checked.
Tip: Exact email matching (dots, + suffixes) causes 'granted to nobody' mistakes; showing the checked address lets it be fixed in 10 seconds.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Login loses the way back
Symptom: After a successful SSO the user lands on a dead-end root page instead of the admin page; reported as 'callback broken'.
Cause: The unauthenticated handler redirects to a bare login URL so the next chain carries no value; next is HTML-escaped but not URL-encoded so a query inside it breaks the href.
Fix: Pass next (path+query only, validated as relative) on redirect; URL-encode it in links; skip /auth/ paths to avoid loops; the root page branches on the user's rights.
Tip: HTML-escaping protects markup, URL-encoding protects values. A complete mechanism fed no input looks like correct code in every single file.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Keep credentials out of URLs and redirects
Symptom: Risk of sessions or one-time codes sitting in browser history and access logs.
Cause: A naive desktop handoff puts the session in the callback query string; post-redirect-get writes a freshly issued code into the URL.
Fix: Use a one-time, short-TTL, hashed handoff code redeemed by a conditional UPDATE in exchange for Set-Cookie; accept only literal http loopback callbacks; render issued codes with a 200 instead of redirecting.
Tip: Use the system browser (RFC 8252) for desktop login, not an embedded webview. HTTP clients should not follow 303-to-login since it masks auth failures as 200 HTML.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Do not let agents borrow the browser's login session
Symptom: A request to let an agent tool use a browser already signed in to a SaaS.
Cause: Reading the browser's cookie store is credential harvesting whatever the purpose.
Fix: Build a narrow tool/MCP server using an API key and tokens from environment variables, never written to config or error messages, with a test asserting the allowed tool list.
Tip: Let the user create and install API credentials themselves.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Scrubbing env credentials breaks the agent's git auth
Symptom: After adding env scrubbing for agent processes, the agent can no longer authenticate to git.
Cause: The scrub removes every *_PRIVATE_KEY variable, including the one the git credential helper reads for the agent's own identity.
Fix: Allow-list the identity variables and set them explicitly from the harness's own key; drop everything else inherited.
Tip: The demo 'worked' because the agent re-exported the key, which hid the bug; test inside the real harness.

LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: An internal control-plane API readable without authentication
Symptom: Workflow catalogue and agent registry endpoints return 200 with no credentials; the OpenAPI declares no security scheme (or only on some routes).
Cause: The dev control-plane service was deployed with no auth on read routes (and possibly start-run).
Fix: Report it as a security finding and require auth on the service. Do not rely on this open state when designing clients.
Tip: When a service hostname cannot be guessed (CF router says 'Requested route does not exist'), grep the frontend JS bundle for sibling service hostnames.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: A single self-hosted runner: jobs QUEUED forever with no error
Symptom: Deploy, CI and rollback all hang in QUEUED for nearly an hour with no error.
Cause: Every workflow pins runs-on to the label of one self-hosted VM that was stopped (or a label no runner carries); GitHub queues rather than failing fast.
Fix: Restart the VM (the runner re-registers), then add a second runner or a hosted fallback so there is no single point of failure.
Workaround: Keep gcloud rollback/deploy scripts that run without a runner.
Tip: A VM's ephemeral external IP changes on every stop/start, breaking hard-coded allow-lists; reserve a static IP if needed. Read labels from the runner registration instead of guessing.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Creating invites: 403 vs 401 reveals a missing role
Symptom: A user cannot find how to invite people; the CLI has no invite command; owning the channel does not help.
Cause: Invites are a relay-side HTTP API using NIP-98 signed auth. 403 'only owners/admins' (unlike 401 missing auth) means the signature is valid but the relay ROLE is missing; a channel owner is not a relay admin.
Fix: Ask a relay owner/admin to create the invite or raise the user's role; an admin can insert a membership row into the relay DB.
Tip: 401 = authentication failure, 403 = authorization/role failure; use it to diagnose roles without changing anything.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Hosted runners disabled by Enterprise/org policy
Symptom: Switching runs-on to ubuntu-latest makes the job die within seconds with no log ('log not found'), saying hosted runners are disabled.
Cause: A GitHub Enterprise/org policy forbids hosted runners; a wrong runs-on is still valid YAML so no local gate catches it.
Fix: Return runs-on to the self-hosted label; before changing, check existing runners with 'gh api repos/<o>/<r>/actions/runners'. Hosted runners must be enabled by an Enterprise admin.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: gcloud --set-env-vars / --env-vars-file replace the whole env
Symptom: After updating one variable, the production service has only a few env entries left; env edited by hand in the console vanishes on the next deploy.
Cause: --set-env-vars, --set-secrets and --env-vars-file REPLACE the entire env (only valueFrom entries survive); --update-* MERGES but still rewrites the listed names on every deploy.
Fix: Use --update-env-vars/--update-secrets and put important values in the build config (or repo Variables/Secrets as the single source of truth). To repair: export the service YAML, replace the env block with the last good revision's env and run 'gcloud run services replace'.
Tip: After every env change, read back the env count and key variables and compare with the previous revision. Hand-set env is not in git and a traffic rollback does not undo it. An 'absent' variable differs from 'present-but-empty'.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Commas and delimiters in gcloud env values
Symptom: '--update-env-vars=KEY=a,b' fails with a usage dump; a 128-character password is stored as 11 characters and a junk variable named after a password fragment appears.
Cause: Commas in values are parsed as delimiters; the ^X^ form splits at X if X appears in the value.
Fix: Use the alternate delimiter form '^@^KEY=a,b,c' with a character absent from the value, or a temporary --env-vars-file (YAML, deleted in finally). Check secrets by LENGTH after writing.
Tip: Move plaintext secrets in Cloud Run env to Secret Manager refs; anyone who can describe the service can read them. Pass credentials via env/temp files, not argv (visible in the process list); redact by each secret name.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: A green deploy (or merge) does not prove the code is live
Symptom: The fix was pushed/merged and the deploy run is green but the bug remains; or the run reports failure though the deploy is fine; or prod deploys fail for days unnoticed.
Cause: The run built the commit BEFORE the fix (workflow_dispatch only, actions/checkout pinned to its own ref), failed on an unrelated step (e.g. artifact quota), or the fix was deployed to a different front door than users use.
Fix: Check on the target: the run's headSha ('gh run view <id> --json headSha'), the serving revision/'last uploaded', the bundle hash, or probe a route that exists only in the new code. Before dispatching, confirm the pinned branch contains the expected commit and config.
Workaround: Set continue-on-error on utility steps (log/artifact upload) so they do not make a good deploy look broken.
Tip: Name revisions after the commit SHA (--revision-suffix). Bundle hashes are only comparable with the same build path. Code that runs fine in one deployment (RAM, response caps) may not run in another.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: A workflow guard only protects the branch that contains it
Symptom: A guard 'on every branch' never runs; a deploy dispatched from the wrong branch silently switches prod to another DB while every check is green.
Cause: GitHub runs the workflow copy on the dispatched ref; other branches carry old copies and their own deploy config.
Fix: Keep one deploy workflow on the default branch and pin the ref in actions/checkout; after build, read the env back from the new revision before moving traffic.
Tip: grep every branch for the guard before trusting a comment. A health probe (/readyz) only proves the app reaches ONE store, not the RIGHT store.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Windows self-hosted runner: shell, encoding, PATH and the Python stub
Symptom: Every step fails before running ('running scripts is disabled', parser errors, 'pwsh: command not found'); tools reported missing though installed; 'Python was not found; ... Microsoft Store'.
Cause: Execution policy Restricted and GitHub's shell does not pass -ExecutionPolicy; Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads BOM-less UTF-8 as ANSI; 'bash' points to WSL; the runner service reads PATH once at start; 'python' is the Store stub alias; winget installs per-user by default, and a wrong package id installs nothing silently.
Fix: Invoke shells explicitly with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass; keep run blocks ASCII-only; call Git Bash by full path (or prepend Git's bin); find the real python by test-running each candidate then write it to GITHUB_PATH; restart the runner service after installs; winget --scope machine with a verified id.
Tip: A preflight must not depend on what it checks, and a probe must not call the tool being diagnosed (npm config get once hung a job 10+ minutes); read the config file instead. Shell paths with spaces can be split wrongly by the runner.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Pinning a package manager is one decision spread over many places
Symptom: Weeks after switching npm to pnpm 11, three build paths fail on first use: the Docker build (ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE, ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH) and the runner ('pnpm is not recognized').
Cause: pnpm 11 needs Node >= 22 but the Docker base is node:20; pnpm >= 10 reads overrides from pnpm-workspace.yaml which the Dockerfile does not COPY; the runner has no pnpm install step; the fix was made on one branch only.
Fix: Treat the packageManager pin, Docker base image, COPY list and runner setup (pnpm/action-setup) as one change; port build fixes to every branch that deploys.
Workaround: Reproduce a Docker stage locally in an empty folder with only the COPYed files before spending more cloud builds.
Tip: After a toolchain change, delete the old lockfile (two lockfiles = drift) and add the new tool to preflight. Do not switch to bun: it ignores pnpm-lock.yaml and overrides.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Cloud Run: land revisions dark, do not use services update
Symptom: Changing env with 'gcloud run services update' took prod down (requests hang to timeout), and rolling the variable back also hung; creating a new service fails with '--no-traffic not supported when creating a new service'.
Cause: services update builds a revision from the service TEMPLATE (which may hold a different image from the serving revision) and sends 100% traffic straight to it. --no-traffic/--tag are refused when the service does not exist yet.
Fix: Every change (env included) goes through a build config that lands the revision dark (--no-traffic --tag=candidate), probe/measure on the candidate URL, then update-traffic. For a new service, create it first with a placeholder image.
Workaround: Recover with update-traffic --to-revisions=<last good revision>=100.
Tip: 'gcloud run services describe' returns the template (the next deploy), not what is serving; compare revision specs field by field (image digest). Warm instances before measuring. Keep service/image names short because Cloud Run appends revision suffixes.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: GitHub repository rulesets do not show in branch protection
Symptom: GET /branches/<b>/protection returns 404 'Branch not protected' but pushes are still refused; 'gh pr merge --admin' fails because someone else must approve.
Cause: The protection is a repository RULESET with empty bypass_actors (admins cannot bypass either); require_last_push_approval means the pusher cannot self-approve.
Fix: Read /rulesets and 'gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision'; get a second person to approve, or temporarily set enforcement=disabled after backing up the JSON.
Tip: PUT the ruleset back with only writable keys (name, target, enforcement, bypass_actors, conditions, rules). Re-enable right after the incident and port needed fixes BEFORE re-enabling.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Branch hygiene: stale bases, phantom backlogs, silent data loss
Symptom: An MR shows '19 commits behind'; merging an old branch would revert thousands of lines; 'git log --branches --not --remotes' lists 'unpushed' work that already landed; a file vanishes from staging.
Cause: The branch was cut from a stale local staging; the target branch was deleted; the upstream branch was deleted after merge so its commits show as unpushed; a commit on a long-lived branch never landed.
Fix: Always fetch and branch from origin/<target>; cherry-pick onto a new branch instead of reusing a very old MR branch; for pushed branches merge the target in instead of force-pushing a rebase; confirm 'unpushed' with git cherry + per-path diff.
Tip: Fetch before answering 'has it been pushed/merged'; local refs can be days old. Use 'git merge --ff-only' after fetch so divergence fails loudly.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: A pending pipeline may have no eligible runner
Symptom: A GitLab pipeline sits PENDING, jobs 'created / not started' although runners are online and idle; an old report saying 'runner dead' gets repeated.
Cause: Project-type runners are registered only for some projects; another project has 0 runners so jobs never run. Some projects build with Jenkins so having no GitLab pipeline is correct; the 'infra' failure was really a governed-paths tripwire.
Fix: Check 'glab api projects/:id/runners' (0 means stop waiting) and recent pipeline status before concluding; register a runner or merge per policy; for governed paths let the owner re-run.
Tip: With no runner, a green MR says nothing; record evidence of gates run locally in the MR description. Check runner heartbeat before declaring a job hung. Remove old claims from docs once disproven.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: PyInstaller packaging traps
Symptom: A new route works from source but 500s in the exe; the packaged app dies on a missing data file; a shared package is missing from every exe; a windowed exe says 'Unhandled exception' with no log; the app looks dead for ~2 minutes after deploy.
Cause: PyInstaller follows imports, not data files, and drops modules imported only inside functions; one-dir builds put _MEIPASS in _internal so __file__-based lookups miss; robocopy /MIR deletes files absent from the new build; antivirus scans large files slowly on first read; crashes happen before logging is configured.
Fix: Import at module level and add hiddenimports/--collect-submodules; --collect-data for packages reading their own data; add a build-time check refusing bundles with missing files; locate model folders by a sentinel file with an env override; deploy with robocopy /E excluding data folders.
Workaround: Build a console variant to see the traceback.
Tip: --hidden-import fixes imports, --collect-data fixes files. Wait ~3 minutes before calling it a crash; check the process list and stdout log.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Building a Tauri app on Windows: toolchain and sidecars
Symptom: 'pnpm tauri build' dies at audiopus_sys ('is cmake not installed?'), then 'resource path binaries\...exe doesn't exist'; the installer contains an old or 0-byte sidecar so nothing spawns.
Cause: cmake/cargo are not on PATH (cmake ships with VS Build Tools); tauri build does not usually rebuild sidecars; externalBin on Windows needs <name>-<target-triple>.exe, and a 'touch' sidecar recipe creates a 0-byte file.
Fix: Use the repo's canonical rebuild script via a cmd wrapper that calls vcvars64 and prepends rustup bin + bundled cmake (CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5); build the sidecar in release for the target triple, copy to binaries/<name>-<triple>.exe, check its size, then 'tauri build --bundles nsis'.
Workaround: For dev checks, create an empty stub with the .exe extension.
Tip: The bundle version comes from the Tauri config, not package.json. A cold release build takes 45-60 minutes. Build in a detached git worktree; back up keys/state before uninstalling the old app. Unsigned installers trigger SmartScreen.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: gcloud's active config is machine-wide
Symptom: Every gcloud command without --project targets the wrong project because another session changed the default config.
Cause: One active_config file decides account and project for every terminal; auth login and config set write into the active config; 'gcloud auth application-default login' overwrites the machine-wide ADC file.
Fix: Isolate with a dedicated CLOUDSDK_CONFIG folder holding only the needed credentials; run deploys through a wrapper asserting account, project id AND the server-returned project number; negative-test with a decoy config.
Workaround: Pass --account and --project on every command.
Tip: A wrapper only protects commands that go through it. Read config back after 'gcloud config set'; it can silently not take effect.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: An unpinned transitive dependency breaks a rebuild of the same commit
Symptom: A Cloud Run candidate revision never becomes ready, /readyz returns 503 InvalidArgument; the serving revision built from the same commit is healthy.
Cause: A transitive library with a floating version range (e.g. google-api-core) changed behaviour (percent-encoding the '(default)' database id), so two builds of the same commit installed different versions.
Fix: Pin the transitive package explicitly in requirements.txt with a test that fails if the pin is dropped/loosened. Have the readiness probe log the error message, not just the class.
Workaround: Keep traffic on the old revision; the candidate was deployed dark so users are unaffected.
Tip: With identical code and env, compare images: diff the layer manifest (the pip install step) and site-packages/*.dist-info/METADATA. Diff env with 'gcloud run revisions describe' per revision. A warning printed next to an error is not evidence about that error.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: A 'describe || create' step fails every deploy after the first
Symptom: Every deploy fails at the Pub/Sub topic creation step; the very first deploy succeeded so the step looked harmless.
Cause: 'describe' fails (missing permission, output hidden) so it falls through to 'create', which refuses because the topic exists.
Fix: Call create directly and treat 'already exists' as success (grep the output), other errors still fail the build. Test all 3 cases: created, exists, permission denied.
Tip: Idempotency built on a 'check' command is only correct if the check distinguishes 'absent' from 'cannot see'. In cloudbuild.yaml Cloud Build expands $VAR itself, so shell variables must be written $$VAR.

Fix: Call create directly and treat 'already exists' as success (grep the output), other errors still fail the build. Test all 3 cases: created, exists, permission denied.
Tip: Idempotency built on a 'check' command is only correct if the check distinguishes 'absent' from 'cannot see'. In cloudbuild.yaml Cloud Build expands $VAR itself, so shell variables must be written $$VAR.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Self-hosted runner VM: setup, memory and access scopes
Symptom: Runner registration fails when run as root; a small VM is OOM-killed during builds; gcloud on the VM gives permission errors although the service account has the roles.
Cause: The runner config script refuses to run as root; a 1 GB VM (e2-micro) has too little RAM for heavy CI (Playwright, global npm installs); the VM was created without --scopes=cloud-platform so access scopes limit the token.
Fix: Create an unprivileged runner user and configure unattended (possibly via a startup script reading the token from metadata); add a ~2 GB swapfile; create the VM with --scopes=cloud-platform (or change scopes while the VM is stopped).
Tip: IAM roles that look right can still be blocked by the VM's access scopes, so check the scopes.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: A Cloud Run 504 does not stop the handler
Symptom: The request returned 504 and the scheduler job was paused, yet emails and writes continued for another 30 minutes.
Cause: Cloud Run returns a timeout to the caller but the handler keeps running in the instance; pausing Cloud Scheduler only blocks the next trigger; an env var named like a kill switch is read by no code.
Fix: Force a new revision (update any env) or scale to 0 to end the instance, verify by counting writes twice some time apart. Long batch work should be a job with its own cancel mechanism.
Tip: A paused scheduler job keeps no backlog; missed runs are not replayed. grep the code for a 'halt' variable before trusting it.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: A deploy guard must compare state, not demand a fixed value
Symptom: A guard requiring 'DB=hana' nearly emptied prod data on a routine deploy; later it blocked a correct deploy with a wrong 'store migration' message.
Cause: Pinning the guard to an expected value turns every code deploy into a store migration when value and reality diverge; parsing config with sed|head -1 caught a value inside a comment.
Fix: The guard reads the value prod is serving and the value this tree would apply, and refuses any CHANGE unless an explicit override input is given; the post-build check compares against the same value. Strip comment lines before parsing config.
Tip: Check the override really passes every later check, or it only wastes one build.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: A new app in a shared GCP project: isolating Firestore
Symptom: A new app deploys to Cloud Run in the same project as a live system using Firestore; the deploy is green but can silently damage the other system's data.
Cause: A parameterless Firestore client binds to the (default) database; deploying firestore:rules replaces the whole ruleset, firestore:indexes deletes indexes not in the file; import/export and bulk delete are database-level; a seed script in the boot path runs on every cold start; the compute service account is shared with every database.
Fix: Create a separate Firestore database, pass the database id explicitly and pin it in firebase.json, move migrations out of the boot path; snapshot (default)'s index/field config before and after, the diff must be empty; real isolation needs a dedicated service account with IAM conditions.
Tip: A collection prefix is a naming convention, not an isolation boundary. Named Firestore DB ids are at most 63 characters.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: SQLite on Cloud Run loses data on every revision
Symptom: Users and data vanish after every redeploy.
Cause: The database file is in /tmp (in-memory on Cloud Run); SQLite on a network filesystem is unsafe and several instances are several different DBs.
Fix: Move to hosted Postgres; the deploy script refuses a missing or SQLite database URL (with an explicit --ephemeral-db flag for demos that forces max-instances=1).
Workaround: max-instances=1 for a temporary demo.
Tip: Prove persistence without logging in: check that a row the service writes on first boot survives a new revision.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: An undeployed companion service and a missing paired secret
Symptom: The deployed system does not respond; the create flow looks fine; log shows 'worker dispatch failed ... All connection attempts failed'.
Cause: The worker service was never deployed and its default URL points at localhost inside the same container.
Fix: Deploy the worker; the deploy script refuses half a pair of config (a URL without its secret or vice versa); read the existing shared secret and session secret from the running service instead of generating new ones.
Tip: A new session secret logs everyone out. Check both directions of the shared secret with a harmless request (202 with the secret, 403 without).

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Cloud Run intercepts /healthz
Symptom: /healthz returns 404 on the deployed service while /readyz next to it returns 200.
Cause: Google Frontend answers /healthz itself with its own HTML 404 page; the request never reaches the container (no x-cloud-trace-context header).
Fix: Use another liveness path, e.g. /livez.
Tip: Classify 404s by headers and body (Google's HTML vs the framework's JSON).

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: GitHub Actions logs hide the real Cloud Build error
Symptom: A deploy fails with only 'build step 0 gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker failed: exit status 2', which looks like an infra/Docker fault.
Cause: The real error (e.g. a TypeScript error in 'npm run build') is only in the Cloud Build log; Actions just waits on 'gcloud builds submit'.
Fix: Get the build id from 'gh run view <id> --log-failed', then 'gcloud builds log <BUILD-ID>' to read the real output and fix the source.
Tip: Always read the Cloud Build log before concluding it is an infra fault.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Repo comments misstate CI status; only the API is authoritative
Symptom: The YAML says 'RE-ENABLED' but nothing runs lint/test on push; pushing a workflow file is refused.
Cause: The workflow was set disabled_manually on GitHub independent of the file content; workflows whose file was deleted stay registered; the gh token lacks the workflow scope.
Fix: Check real status with 'gh workflow list --all' and 'gh run list'; fix the comment; add the workflow scope to the gh token before pushing workflow files.
Tip: 'Active' does not mean 'automatic': a workflow with only workflow_dispatch never runs on push, so pushing to main is not a release.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Environment names and old comments misstate what is prod
Symptom: A service named '-qa' is assumed to be staging; docs name another platform as production; a workflow header naming an old DB nearly blocked a safe deploy.
Cause: Services were repurposed without renaming; comments and docs were not updated when the architecture changed.
Fix: Determine the environment from live facts: domain mappings, env on the serving revision, actual data; confirm with the owner; fix or delete the old comment.
Tip: A comment contradicting the config below it can block a correct action or let a wrong one through.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Endpoint security blocks node.exe outbound by binary
Symptom: On a CI runner corepack/npm fails with 'connect EACCES' to the npm registry while curl gets through; no proxy or firewall rule exists.
Cause: Endpoint security blocks outbound connections of that specific node.exe binary; a Node installed at another path and bun can connect. It had been diagnosed and worked around before, but nobody linked it.
Fix: Ask the machine admin for an outbound exception for node.exe; meanwhile have CI pick the first Node that can actually fetch from the registry.
Workaround: Use a second Node binary at another path, or a loopback registry mirror.
Tip: Before re-diagnosing an environment problem, grep the repo for the symptom ('EACCES', 'registry', 'mirror').

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Commit hygiene: child repos, stray files and out-of-scope diffs
Symptom: Risk of nested repos, unrelated files in commits, losing work when splitting commits, whole-file CRLF diffs, 'git add -A' nearly pushing 4 GB of build output.
Cause: The app folder sits inside a larger repo; git add -A sweeps files others are working on; 'git checkout -- file' discards changes; 'git stash push <paths>' records the whole tree; an edit script converts CRLF to LF; formatters/generators touch unrelated files; build artefacts are missing from .gitignore.
Fix: Check 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' before git init; read whole-repo status then stage specific paths; measure untracked size before staging; copy files out before rewinding; preserve line endings; revert out-of-scope files before committing.
Workaround: If one commit merged two features, 'git reset --soft HEAD~1' and recommit before pushing.
Tip: Prove a move by comparing line multisets; use git check-ignore. A fork that keeps upstream workflows and Dependabot can burn Actions quota; remove them or disable Actions on the fork.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: GitLab / glab quirks on a self-hosted instance
Symptom: Merging an MR returns 405 or 'conflict' right after a push; adding a second reviewer returns 200 but reviewers: []; 'glab api --input -' returns 415; 'glab repo view' 404s.
Cause: GitLab recomputes mergeability right after push/merge; multiple reviewers/assignees are a paid-tier feature; glab sends no JSON content-type for stdin bodies; a remote URL with a token confuses glab; flaky VPN/DNS.
Fix: Retry after recomputation; set one reviewer and tag the second in a comment; use 'glab mr create -R <path>' or the numeric project id; send JSON bodies via --input with Content-Type application/json.
Tip: Always read the MR back after setting fields. Protected branches may be maintainer-merge only. Before pushing, confirm the right code group, not a group with a similar repo name.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: A background build wrapper reports false success
Symptom: The build fails but the background job/task notification reports exit 0.
Cause: The wrapper prints 'EXIT 0' from its own echo/subshell, not the build's exit code; the real error was a Python text patch that corrupted the source.
Fix: Capture and print the real exit code; read the EXIT line and errors in the build log. Edit source with a real editor, not by patching escaped strings with an ad hoc script.
Tip: Read the exit marker in the build log; never trust the task notification.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: The built front end differs from what the server serves
Symptom: After a pull or fix the UI looks unchanged; a 'fixed' bug persists for users.
Cause: The server serves the built dist, not the source; dist is gitignored; browser tabs keep old worker chunks until a hard reload; 'tsc --noEmit' on a solution-style tsconfig checks nothing.
Fix: Run a production build after editing src; verify by grepping the new asset hash in the served HTML and the new string in the bundle; ask for a hard reload.
Tip: When tsconfig.json only contains project references, only a real build catches type errors.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Remote SQL via gcloud ssh on Windows returns nothing
Symptom: Inline SQL passed through 'gcloud compute ssh' into a DB container returns nothing or gets mangled.
Cause: Nested quoting through the Windows shell + ssh + docker exec corrupts the command.
Fix: scp the SQL file to the VM then 'psql -f' with ON_ERROR_STOP in one transaction (or pipe base64 SQL from Git Bash); keep container env variables in single quotes so they expand inside the container.
Tip: Raw DB inserts emit no application events so clients may not see changes immediately. Record the undo statements.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Cancelling a GitHub job does not stop a running Cloud Build
Symptom: The deploy job says 'cancelled' but minutes later a new Cloud Run revision appears with 0% traffic.
Cause: The workflow only calls 'gcloud builds submit' and waits; killing the waiting process does not stop the remote build. The build still lands the revision dark, while the promote step lives in the GitHub step that was skipped.
Fix: Cancel the Cloud Build too ('gcloud builds cancel'), or finish by probing the candidate then 'gcloud run services update-traffic --to-latest'.
Tip: In 'gcloud run revisions list', ACTIVE=yes includes tagged 0%-traffic revisions; only status.traffic percent shows what users get. Check which commit the candidate was built from.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Required status checks need a pull_request trigger
Symptom: CI is red for days yet PRs still merge; the team thinks main is protected but there is no protection.
Cause: Prod CI only runs on push to main (after merge) so it cannot gate PRs; a required check must be reported on the PR's head commit.
Fix: Add a pull_request trigger, pass github.event.pull_request.head.sha to the reusable CI (github.sha is the temporary merge commit), confirm the check shows on the PR, then enable branch protection with that check and strict up-to-date.
Tip: Read protection back via the API (404 means none). A single-job self-hosted runner queues PR checks behind other jobs.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Traps in workflow_dispatch, push triggers and reusable workflows
Symptom: Dispatching a new workflow from a feature branch gives 404 'workflow not found on the default branch'; a push-triggered run is green but does not move traffic; a staging deploy cancels a prod deploy; a called workflow logs in with empty credentials.
Cause: workflow_dispatch only registers files present on the default branch; on push the inputs context is empty; a shared concurrency group with cancel-in-progress spans environments; called workflows get no secrets unless passed.
Fix: Add on: push for branch-based deploys; resolve inputs once at job level with defaults (inputs.x || 'default') and guard with github.event_name; concurrency groups per target; use secrets: inherit.
Tip: To trial on the runner without touching main, push a temporary branch with a push-triggered workflow.

Cause: workflow_dispatch only registers files present on the default branch; on push the inputs context is empty; a shared concurrency group with cancel-in-progress spans environments; called workflows get no secrets unless passed.
Fix: Add on: push for branch-based deploys; resolve inputs once at job level with defaults (inputs.x || 'default') and guard with github.event_name; concurrency groups per target; use secrets: inherit.
Tip: To trial on the runner without touching main, push a temporary branch with a push-triggered workflow.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Cloud Run defaults cannot run heavy jobs
Symptom: A job processing hundreds of thousands of rows will exceed service limits.
Cause: The reference service runs 1 vCPU, 1 GiB, 300 s request timeout.
Fix: Design heavy processing as asynchronous jobs with a queue, chunking, idempotency keys and a status endpoint; upload large files straight to object storage via signed URLs.
Tip: Read the actual deployed config and treat its limits as design constraints.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Verifying a packaged desktop app properly
Symptom: A bundled fallback is thought to work; the app is thought to have exited; a .env next to the exe is thought to be ignored.
Cause: An existing cache on the dev machine satisfied the fallback; the window belongs to a child process, not the parent exe; a one-file build unpacks to a temp folder so it cannot see the .env next to the exe; config defaults are read from os.environ at import, before .env loads.
Fix: Test with HOME/USERPROFILE pointing at an empty folder; inspect the process tree; use a one-dir build and resolve config from sys.executable's parent folder; read defaults inside a function after loading .env; each build goes to a new timestamped folder.
Tip: A fallback tested on a machine that does not need it has not been tested.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Build-context ignore files for Cloud Build
Symptom: The second image fails 'COPY ... file does not exist'; the build uploads thousands of files including the virtualenv.
Cause: .dockerignore excludes a folder the second image needs; with no .gcloudignore, 'gcloud builds submit' uploads everything (falling back to .gitignore) and the tarball remains in the bucket.
Fix: Let each Dockerfile's COPY lines decide the image scope; add a .gcloudignore excluding .env, venv, DBs, tests; use a cloudbuild config selecting a non-root Dockerfile with -f.
Tip: A repo with a good .gitignore only protects the upload by accident.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Recovering a lost .env from the running service
Symptom: The deploy script exits because .env is missing on a fresh clone.
Cause: The file is git-ignored; GitHub Actions secrets are write-only (the API returns only names); a 404 from gh under another account means 'cannot see', not 'empty'.
Fix: Rebuild it from 'gcloud run services describe' (names printed only), reverse the key renames the deploy script applies, refuse to overwrite an existing file; dry-run first.
Tip: If the session secret is not in the file, redeploying generates a new one and logs users out; decide that explicitly.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: The git credential helper needs a newer git; fetch hangs on a prompt
Symptom: git via the credential helper fails in the container, or git fetch hangs forever.
Cause: The helper needs git >= 2.46 (authtype capability; Debian bookworm has only 2.39); fetch without the helper waits on a password prompt.
Fix: Use a distro with git >= 2.46 (e.g. Debian trixie); configure the helper for fetch too; set GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 in automation.
Tip: Use the run id in E2E test resource names to avoid collisions.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: git push over SSH hangs on port 22
Symptom: 'git push' hangs with no error on some networks.
Cause: Outbound port 22 is blocked on some networks (intermittent, network dependent).
Fix: Try a normal push first; if it hangs, use GIT_SSH_COMMAND with HostName=ssh.github.com, Port=443, name the key explicitly (-i, IdentitiesOnly) and set ConnectTimeout.
Workaround: Put the 443 override in a permanent ssh config alias.
Tip: Overriding HostName bypasses the alias's IdentityFile so the key must be named. Pushing to an explicit URL instead of 'origin' does not update the tracking ref; run git fetch afterwards.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: The local Rust toolchain differs from CI
Symptom: Local lacks rustfmt/clippy and rustc is older than the pinned version; CI will fail format/lint.
Cause: The toolchain was installed by hand, not via rustup, so rust-toolchain.toml is ignored.
Fix: Install rustup (e.g. via winget) to use the pinned version with the default profile (rustfmt, clippy); run the exact fmt and 'clippy -D warnings' commands CI runs.
Tip: Clippy on Windows reports cfg(unix) code as unused, which is pre-existing noise; confirm the flagged files are outside your diff.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Verify git push against the remote, not the exit code
Symptom: A script reports the push done but the branch is not on the remote; a push once exited 0 while writing nothing.
Cause: A transient DNS error ('Could not resolve host') plus a script that echoes success regardless of exit code; a pre-push hook may cache pass results by sha.
Fix: After every push, compare the local SHA with the remote via git ls-remote and retry if missing.
Tip: Do not merge into environment branches without the rights or review; merging is deploying and someone else owns that step.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: The Cloud Run request timeout must exceed the app timeout
Symptom: Users get the platform's generic 504 instead of the app's friendly timeout message.
Cause: Cloud Run's clock starts earlier (at the load balancer); with equal timeouts the platform wins.
Fix: Set the Cloud Run timeout above the app timeout (e.g. 330 s vs 300 s) and always raise both together.
Tip: Defaults to know: without a livenessProbe a broken revision is not restarted after cutover; CPU is throttled outside requests so background threads stall; min-instances=0 wipes /tmp and in-process state, and /tmp is RAM.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: Docker compose: migration timeouts and unpublished ports
Symptom: The first compose up fails migration with 'pool timed out' although Postgres is healthy; later the service is healthy but its port is unreachable from the host.
Cause: Postgres was still doing its first init; 'up -d' of a single service does not apply port mappings.
Fix: Rerun compose up for the migration; use 'up -d --force-recreate <service>' to republish ports.
Workaround: When Docker Hub pulls are blocked, use locally tagged images.
Tip: Check host port mappings in 'docker compose ps', not just health.

LESSON LEARNED [CI/CD & Deploy]: The cloud free tier is not entirely free
Symptom: A 'free tier' VM still incurs charges.
Cause: The boot disk is pd-balanced (always-free covers only pd-standard up to 30 GB) and external IPv4 is billed even on free-tier VMs.
Fix: Use pd-standard within the limit; delete unused resources after checking nothing references them (env, repo, startup metadata, reserved addresses) and no orphan disks remain.
Tip: A boot disk with autoDelete=true is deleted with the VM and the ephemeral IP is lost; warn before deleting.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Deleting and purging production data safely
Symptom: A 'delete id >= N' filter nearly swept legacy tickets; '3 junk rows' had become 5 including real tickets; 'everything migrated' was false for a few records; deleting a shared document nearly destroyed another product's data.
Cause: Parsing trailing digits matched legacy ids; the row count taken before deploy was stale; nobody compared id sets; the document held another product's subcollections.
Fix: List only by default; --apply requires --expect count and refuses if the count changed; anchored id regexes; delete by a verified id list. Back up first and delete only once the backup is complete; compare source and target by id; delete children before parents then read back.
Tip: Deletes on Firestore count as writes; batch commits (<=100-500 writes, back off on 429). Ask before deleting a heterogeneous set.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Slow, read-hungry Firestore: streaming whole collections, filtering in Python, N+1
Symptom: Millions of reads per day for a few thousand tickets; boards/filters take seconds, page 2 costs as much as page 1, limit=1 costs as much as 50, a one-row function costs ~10k reads.
Cause: Repositories stream whole collections then filter/limit in Python, no composite indexes, counts by streaming, reports/feeds read each ticket's events subcollection (N+1) and poll constantly. Keyset paging with filters cannot be pushed down so each page rescans the collection (quadratic cost).
Fix: Create composite indexes, push filters to the DB, use aggregation count, cursor pagination; denormalise/snapshot aggregate data on write. When all filtered rows are needed, scan once for rows, cursor and total; have writers push changes (socket + Pub/Sub) instead of polling.
Workaround: Raise the poll interval sharply to stop the bleeding; scheduled precompute caches only move cost away from user clicks.
Tip: Measure reads per route with a fake store counting queries and reads, on realistic data including subcollections. Do not migrate to a relational DB to fix the bill: same code paths, you only lose the meter.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Scripts pointing at the wrong backend: importing the app loads .env, two different config files
Symptom: A seed/measure script targeting production reports 'counter = 0, 0 companies' and nearly wrote thousands of documents into a scratch project; a new client connects but sees an empty store.
Cause: Importing any app module loads the repo's .env, overriding the project id and GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. The dev copy's config points at the dev project while the installed copy points at the real one, and the file is encrypted so reading it shows nothing.
Fix: Snapshot env before importing the app and restore it afterwards; require an explicit target project and refuse if the resolved root does not match. Measure record counts in each candidate store before connecting.
Tip: Always dry-run printing the project, database and live counts before any bulk write. The first Firestore call can take ~17 s; warm it up in a background thread at server start.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Bare except turns obvious errors into silent wrong results
Symptom: The Users screen nearly rendered empty and normal-looking because it called a helper that does not exist; a failing test only said 'nothing was granted'; a fail-open cache looked like an ordinary slow site.
Cause: Calls wrapped in 'except Exception: return [] / None / pass' without logging, so AttributeError, missing stubs or unreachable Redis became silent defaults.
Fix: Keep degrade-gracefully handlers where needed but always log with exc_info. Give fail-open features a health endpoint reporting enabled/ok so you can see when they are off or unreachable.
Tip: An empty result and a broken result must look different in the logs. Look for 'except Exception' around every newly added call.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: A shared event inbox returns another run's result
Symptom: Chat shows thinking progress but no answer (the model is assumed slow); later the progress line vanishes after the first thinking round.
Cause: Several workflows of one session post to the same inbox, and the waiter takes the FIRST finish event (from session-init) which has no reply. Sub-flows and resume rounds attach their own run id instead of the caller's so the filter drops them.
Fix: Attach the run id to every hook event and filter by it; sub-flows and resume rounds report under the caller's id and hook (stored in the checkpoint). Pass node hooks down only, never the child's finish event.
Tip: Dump the inbox in order with run ids: reading code proves nothing, the event log does. Before reusing a channel, check who reads it and when.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Nested timeouts must be ordered and say what happened
Symptom: The thinking indicator disappears with no answer; error 'result has no field thinking'; child runs abandoned with no exit code.
Cause: The client waits 60 s while the inner sub-flow allows 300 s; the sub-flow node ignores the 'stillRunning' flag. A shared boolean/status ends the waiting state when any job finishes.
Fix: The outer wait must exceed the inner budget; on timeout stop the child, return a message stating the seconds and progress, and always include the result field. Track pending answers with a per-turn counter decremented in finally.
Tip: A turn ending without an answer must write the reason to the transcript; an error that erases its own evidence is worse than a crash.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: A workflow engine reporting false success
Symptom: A flow returns 200 but does nothing or reports success after a failed step; branches do not run; loops are skipped; a node with an error branch still dies with 400 'output reads ... no such field'.
Cause: A node leaving via an unconnected handle ends the walk with success; an error handle wired to End also counts as success; templates render None as 'null'; a 'contains NONE' check matches wrongly; loop state is not reset. The engine applies strict output mapping before looking at the handle, so an error result raises before reaching the error branch.
Fix: Add a 'require' check at End to force failure on empty output; compare with equality instead of substring; reset loop state on exit; carry every turn-level input into sub-flows. Read outputs leniently (missing path -> None) when a node exits via its error handle, keep strict on success.
Tip: A document with the wrong schema version is accepted by PUT but fails only at run time; POST creates an EMPTY document (nodes must be PUT in). A flow stored only in the tool's DB has no history; export the JSON into git after each edit.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Leading zeros in ERP keys break mapping lookups and row matching
Symptom: Updates from SAP are treated as creates and fail with 'same key'; golden record sync produces identical CREATE/DELETE pairs flagged as duplicates.
Cause: SAP/CPI sends zero-padded numeric keys while the mapping table stores them unpadded; many code paths compare raw keys with ===/!==; the zero-stripping helper only runs for one hard-coded system type.
Fix: Normalise all-digit keys once where inbound keys are built/matched: exact match first, then retry with leading zeros stripped, still scoped to the target system. Align child keys to the parent's format.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Firestore restore works but the app cannot open the restored copy
Symptom: Backups are READY but cannot actually be restored into use.
Cause: A restore always creates a NEW database, while the app calls firestore.client() with no database id so it is hard-bound to (default). TTL policies, security rules and backup schedules are not in the backup.
Fix: Pass database_id via an env var at a single client-creation point (empty for (default)) and block every other client creation. Document how to reapply TTL and rules.
Workaround: An in-place restore (delete the source then restore under the same id) is irreversible; enable delete protection.
Tip: 'gcloud firestore databases restore' returns within seconds while the operation keeps running; measure with 'gcloud firestore operations list'. Real RTO = restore time + switch-over.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: In-process rate limits do not work on multi-instance serverless
Symptom: An hourly limit looks active but is not.
Cause: The counter lives in each instance's memory so it multiplies by instance count and resets on every restart/deploy. Another intake path calls the use case directly, bypassing every controller limit.
Fix: Count hourly from a durable store (count aggregation) and keep the in-process limiter as a burst filter. Put the guard at the layer every intake path passes through.
Tip: A rule placed in a controller is a rule other doors skip. Shared per-role buckets need a per-user floor and should run alarm-only first.
