LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: A poison message jams the queue because the server returns 500
Symptom: The agent keeps scanning but no new tickets appear; the queue is stuck with 'HTTP 500' on the same messages.
Cause: Two layers hold different limits: the route allows a 600 KB body, the domain raises ValueError beyond 8000 characters, and the uncaught ValueError becomes a 500. The client treats 5xx as transient so it stops and preserves order; the first message blocks all.
Fix: Keep one constant in the domain entity for both layers to read; reject with 4xx so the client dead-letters it. Add a test failing on hard-coded limits.
Tip: Never return 500 for input you will never accept. Bisect the size against the real service to find the actual guard.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Large attachment uploads through the API hit memory and body limits
Symptom: Uploads above ~20 MB fail with an HTML 413 from Cloud Run itself; concurrent uploads exhaust memory; slow networks hit the request timeout.
Cause: Files travel as base64 in a JSON body (4/3 inflation plus the decoded copy, all held in memory). Cloud Run limits bodies to ~32 MiB and /tmp is RAM.
Fix: Upload straight to storage with server-issued upload sessions (signed/resumable URLs, sequential chunks). Do not proxy large data through the app.
Tip: Browsing capacity says nothing about upload capacity; model them separately. Publish the limit the server really enforces, since one rejected attachment fails the whole request.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Seeding production with real contacts mass-mails customers
Symptom: Real people, customers included, receive thousands of surveys and 'ticket closed' mails about tickets that do not exist.
Cause: A stress-test seeder wrote 10k tickets into production with real contact addresses; the daily lifecycle sweep sent CSAT surveys, reminders and auto-closes. Auto-close left no event so the first count missed it.
Fix: Seed only into isolated environments with fake user data (example.com). Before seeding a live system, list and disable every scheduler job, sweep and outbound path; tag every seeded document with a batch id and delete early.
Workaround: Pause scheduler jobs and force a new revision to kill in-flight runs.
Tip: Ask not only 'what do I write' but 'what automation will act on what I write'. Count every outbound path before reporting impact.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: File download routes: Range, the 32 MiB limit and non-ASCII names
Symptom: Videos upload but preview does not play, large downloads 500 with no traceback, some downloads 502; container memory ~2x the file size.
Cause: The route buffers the whole object and returns 200 without Accept-Ranges, while MP4 keeps its moov index at the end so players need range requests. Cloud Run refuses non-chunked responses >32 MiB (logged only in varlog/system); a Content-Disposition with emoji raises UnicodeEncodeError swallowed by a broad except into a 502.
Fix: Forward the client's Range to the storage's pre-signed download URL and stream in chunks, sending Content-Length only below ~30 MiB. Use filename*=UTF-8'' (RFC 6266/5987) with an ASCII fallback; store files under a uuid name keeping the extension.
Tip: The framework's FileResponse handles Range, a hand-built Response does not. A 500 with no app traceback means the platform discarded the response.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: English-only embeddings and an intermediate translation step invert the question
Symptom: Vietnamese recall is weak; after adding a translate-to-English step, answers address the opposite question.
Cause: bge-small-en only supports English; the translator saw only the bare prompt with no context, and Vietnamese without diacritics collides with English words (no, so, may, co).
Fix: Give the translator the last few conversation turns as context, list ambiguous tokens, default to the Vietnamese reading and forbid adding negation. Recall before storing (or the question matches itself).
Workaround: Use a multilingual embedding model to drop the translation step, but every vector must be regenerated.
Tip: A/B prompts by calling the LLM node alone through the chat API (seconds per case), then confirm once through the whole flow.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Exact-match column-name joins drop columns when generating integration JSON
Symptom: The integration JSON generates 'successfully' but some columns are missing; the names differ only by case or a 'to_' prefix.
Cause: Three exact-match, case-sensitive joins with no normalisation; a miss only console.warns and drops the value. Keys are built from camelCase technical field names while the schema uses label-style names.
Fix: Build output keys from the schema's flattened/label names; normalise names consistently across every join; fail loudly on unmappable columns.
Tip: When it really fails, grep the service log for 'not found' messages. Check which environment/DB the failing run actually used.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Invisible handler crashes: SQLite locks under concurrent turns
Symptom: Callers get 'Remote end closed connection without response' from a local server; retries do not reproduce; no traceback.
Cause: SQLite in rollback-journal mode takes an exclusive lock per write; concurrent writes hit the 5 s busy wait and raise 'database is locked'. ThreadingHTTPServer does not catch handler exceptions and under pythonw stderr goes nowhere.
Fix: Open connections with journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout ~30 s, synchronous=NORMAL; route stderr/logging to a file so the next failure names itself.
Tip: With no traceback, record the mechanism as the best-fitting hypothesis, not a confirmed cause.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: postgresql:// URLs default to psycopg2
Symptom: Connecting with a hosted Postgres URL raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psycopg2' although psycopg is installed.
Cause: SQLAlchemy maps a bare postgresql:// or postgres:// scheme to the psycopg2 driver, while the project uses psycopg 3.
Fix: Normalise the URL at engine creation to postgresql+psycopg://, keeping explicit drivers and query strings (sslmode=require) intact.
Tip: Do not 'fix' it by installing psycopg2; that silently adds a second driver. Pin a test asserting exactly this default-driver trap.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Google API quirks: PATCH creates, HTML 404s, two credential stores
Symptom: An update 'succeeds' but lands on the wrong document; a batch delete returns HTML 'Error 404'; firebase_admin 403s while REST with the same account works; gcloud login fails with 'mismatching_state'; scripts run against the wrong project/account.
Cause: Firestore PATCH creates the document if missing; a wrong REST path hits the frontend router (HTML) instead of the API (JSON); two concurrent gcloud auth logins fight over the loopback port; the gcloud CLI account and ADC are separate stores.
Fix: Read back after every write; if the response is HTML fix the URL first (JSON means the request reached the API). Use REST with gcloud auth print-access-token for local admin tools; log in one at a time; set account and project explicitly for both ADC and CLI.
Tip: Google client libs can take minutes to fail when ADC is missing; REST diagnoses faster. In a type converter, check bool before int.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Route order: catch-all or parameterised routes swallow specific ones
Symptom: /healthz returns an HTML 404 in production; GET on a POST-only route returns 404 instead of 405; e2e fails with TooManyRedirects or a new page under /auth shows the sign-in page.
Cause: Starlette/FastAPI match in declaration/include order: a catch-all '/{path}' or '/auth/{provider_id}/login' declared earlier captures specific routes.
Fix: Choose new paths that cannot collide with parameter patterns (different prefix or segment count), register health/API and static paths before the catch-all. Point uptime checks at an endpoint that really answers.
Tip: Route order is invisible to whoever adds the next route; do not rely on it. With 'from __future__ import annotations', type imports inside a function do not resolve so FastAPI treats Request as a query param (422): import at module level.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Firestore deletes do not cascade to subcollections
Symptom: After deleting tickets, some event documents are still billed, still counted by collection-group queries and read by reports; the cleanup script cannot find them again.
Cause: Deleting a parent document leaves its subcollections. An interrupted cleanup left orphan events, and the script finds work by a field on the parent document so it cannot resume.
Fix: List and delete subcollections before the parent, count separately and verify afterwards. For orphans, scan the known id range and skip ids whose parent still exists; delete derived projections too.
Tip: A 40-item sample cannot size a problem across 10,000 items; say 'count unknown until fully scanned'.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: SQLite/SQLAlchemy schema evolution: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and create_all do not add columns
Symptom: A new column is missing on an existing DB and the first query fails; a dropped table still holds sensitive data; the running form differs from the seed file; hand-edited data is lost on reseed; deleting a session leaves orphan messages.
Cause: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and metadata.create_all only create missing tables, never add columns or drop tables; SQLite cannot alter a PK. The DB is what serves while the seed is only what the next reseed loads; foreign_keys defaults OFF and is per connection.
Fix: Add idempotent, additive-only boot migrations (ADDED_COLUMNS, value renames; DROPPED_TABLES with backup), and rename/recreate/copy for PK changes. Turn on PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON per connection; every DB edit must go into the seed and reseeding must not re-derive data.
Tip: Order by AUTOINCREMENT seq; timestamps are not an ordering contract; use AUTOINCREMENT (not MAX+1) for user-visible ids. Back up the real DB before migrating; an upsert-only save cannot express deletes.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Settings writes silently lose data
Symptom: Changing one provider field erased the default provider; saved settings vanish on reload; empty CLI arguments disappear; new sessions ignore the configured default model.
Cause: The config route replaces the whole key; the client-side reader drops unknown fields; an existing 'empty override means delete' rule; a clean() filter strips empty strings; hard-coded default constants.
Fix: Always GET-merge-PUT with a store that writes whole keys; teach the reader every field; review every empty-value case when structural meaning changes; keep empty strings; read defaults from settings.
Tip: Separate 'unset' (delete) from 'set to empty string'. Store check results server-side and invalidate when config or secrets change.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Measuring 'how much changed' in a ported codebase
Symptom: Reports say 'every unit drifted', 101% of files changed, or '3% changed means 97% old', and readers keep misreading the percentages.
Cause: The time window includes bulk import commits; files-touched and lines-changed differ ~40x; generated files and large fixtures dominate line counts; mirror repos double count; authors commit under several names/emails.
Fix: Exclude import commits from the baseline (detect by count of added paths); count only code extensions; dedupe mirrors by shared SHAs; match authors by name + email; report per repo with one denominator per row.
Tip: State the denominator and level (group/unit/repo) in every percentage label. Check HTML reports in a real browser, since a small JS error can silently kill the script.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: SharePoint DELETE is only a soft delete; use permanentDelete for real deletion
Symptom: Graph DELETE returns 204 and the file leaves the library, but a compliance claim of 'deleted' is false.
Cause: The item goes to the site recycle bin and version history keeps the old bytes.
Fix: Use POST /drives/{d}/items/{id}/permanentDelete (available in v1.0). If only soft delete is possible, report it as NOT deleted and alert.
Tip: Verify delete semantics on the real store before designing offboarding. Object store APIs may answer the same for 'no permission' and 'already gone', so compare files found against files deleted and stop on a shortfall.

Fix: Use POST /drives/{d}/items/{id}/permanentDelete (available in v1.0). If only soft delete is possible, report it as NOT deleted and alert.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Switching storage backend abandons old files
Symptom: After switching the attachment store, old files will 404 and offboarding reports them deleted while they sit in the old bucket.
Cause: The selector returns only one store, and download/delete paths only ask that store.
Fix: Keep the old backend as a read-and-delete fallback: fetch/delete try new then old, put/stat do not fall back. Log and swallow fallback errors.
Tip: Read the real store for old objects before switching. A fallback is not a migration; say so.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: A precompute job written and tested but never called
Symptom: The dashboard is never 'served from cache'; every open does a live scan.
Cause: The in-process scheduler thread is correctly disabled on serverless (K_SERVICE), and the replacement maintenance endpoint has no caller because no Cloud Scheduler job was created.
Fix: Create a Cloud Scheduler job calling the maintenance endpoint with its secret. Choose the frequency by cost since each run is a full scan.
Tip: When ruling out scheduled jobs, also ask which job SHOULD exist but does not. Measure a job's cost in a quiet 5-minute monitoring window, cross-checked with request logs.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Firestore billing and quota facts that change the maths
Symptom: The API quota shows 50,000 reads and 20,000 writes/day as 'fixed', yet actual reads are ~95x that with no errors.
Cause: That is the FREE allowance; exceeding it is billed, not blocked.
Fix: Budget by unit price: +1M reads/day is about $9/month.
Tip: Aggregations cost 1 read per 1,000 index entries; select() still costs 1 read per document; batching does not reduce reads; a listener disconnected >30 minutes is billed the whole query again. FAILED_PRECONDITION on RunQuery means a missing composite index.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Durable ordering for a mailbox-to-queue agent
Symptom: Design risk: lost mail on crash, duplicate tickets, or scans piling up.
Cause: The order of fetch, queue, mark-read and deliver decides the failure modes.
Fix: Fetch unread (oldest first), append to the queue and fsync, then mark read, then drain to an idempotent API (dedupe by message-id). Single-flight with lock.locked() then skip; dead-letter permanent 4xx, stop on 401/403/5xx.
Tip: Leave messages rejected at parse time unread so a fix resends them automatically. Graph webhooks must echo validationToken before any secret check, and subscriptions expire after ~3 days so a renewal job is needed.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Moving data between hot and cold stores
Symptom: Archiving was meant to stay within the Firestore free tier; board counts from the cold store were short; risk of duplicate ids after cutover.
Cause: The real free-tier limit is reads/day, not storage, and archiving does not reduce board reads; the two stores have separate id sequences.
Fix: Move = write target, read back and compare, then delete source (idempotent, sharing one predicate). Floor the hot allocator at the archive's high-water mark; merge paging with a shared value cursor.
Tip: Enable the read-path flag before moving data or boards go empty. Protect read quota with aggregate projection documents, not archiving.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Deleted records come back: seeding at cold start
Symptom: A deleted admin invite reappears minutes later with invited_by=seed.
Cause: An idempotent but unconditional seed in the startup hook rewrites the default admin on every cold start; the service scales to zero so it boots roughly hourly. An empty env override falls back to the hard-coded default.
Fix: Use the app's suppression mechanism (a tombstone both seed and login respect); write the tombstone before deleting the row. Long term make seeding conditional.
Tip: Correlate when the record reappears with instance startup logs.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Slow ticket creation: blocking I/O in an async handler, not the LLM
Symptom: Creating a ticket takes 2-3 s on the server and logs 'event loop stalled'; the inline LLM triage was blamed at first.
Cause: Triage was already deferred; the real cost was about a dozen sequential synchronous Firestore/Graph calls inside async def (re-reading the just-written document, re-reading the event log, stat per attachment).
Fix: Pass the document and events already in hand instead of re-reading, fold side writes into the first save, stat attachments in parallel. Move blocking clients off the loop (asyncio.to_thread or a sync route); test round-trip counts instead of time.
Tip: Before blaming a branch, check which branch actually ran. Look for logs after the reported event's timestamp, not before.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Redis from Cloud Run: use Direct VPC egress, no connector needed
Symptom: Cache code shipped but is not enabled, reported as 'Cloud Run cannot reach internal Redis; vpcaccess API not enabled'.
Cause: The production service has no VPC egress configured; a dev service in the same project already reaches Redis via Direct VPC egress with no connector or vpcaccess API.
Fix: Add Direct VPC egress (--network/--subnet --vpc-egress private-ranges-only) and the Redis URL. Separate environments by database index and key prefix; fail open with a short timeout and circuit breaker; invalidate with versioned keys (INCR).
Tip: Before concluding an infra limit, look at other services in the same project; one may already do it. Never expose Redis on a public IP.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: A Firestore merge write cannot remove a key from a map
Symptom: Revoking one key from a user's access map reports success but the key remains.
Cause: set(merge=True) merges nested maps recursively, so writing a map without a key does not delete that key.
Fix: Rewrite the whole document with merge=False or delete the field path explicitly. Via REST use PATCH with updateMask.fieldPaths so other fields (such as secrets) stay intact.
Tip: Always read back after a revoke/disable write.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Small HTTP server details causing misleading 404s
Symptom: Ids containing '#' 404 on every route; a wrong base URL returns 200 and reads as an empty table; logs full of ConnectionResetError; a route present in the source still 404s.
Cause: Path segments are not percent-decoded; the SPA returns index.html 200 for unknown paths; long-poll clients disconnect mid-response; the route was registered as PUT, not POST.
Fix: Decode each segment after splitting; treat a non-JSON 200 as an error; override handle_error to swallow client-abort exceptions; check the HTTP method before a known route returns 404.
Tip: Let the caller decide which status means 'does not exist' instead of mapping every non-2xx to None, or a dead server reads as 'no items'. Use urllib quote(safe='') for query values.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Latent hang risks: worker tasks without timeouts and unbounded row locks
Symptom: A handler can stall forever with no error, leaving a workflow step RUNNING until someone notices.
Cause: The worker-thread pool queues tasks with no deadline of their own; some SELECT ... FOR UPDATE have no wait so they inherit HANA's 30-minute lock-wait timeout; pool size is derived from container memory.
Fix: Wrap tasks in Promise.race with a deadline so the step is marked FAILED; give every forUpdate an explicit wait; add request timeouts to internal service calls.
Workaround: Run a sweeper marking every step RUNNING for more than N seconds so stalls report themselves.
Tip: Even if not the cause of the incident under suspicion, these are real defects worth fixing.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: An empty admin page in prod: the config row was never seeded
Symptom: The prod settings page shows empty fields with no error; Edit says 'Missing required fields'; the team suspects missing code or env vars.
Cause: The config table in prod HANA has 0 rows; the init action that seeds it exists in code but its only UI caller is commented out so it never ran in the new environment. The feature reads credentials from the DB row, not env vars.
Fix: Seed the row via the init action or a guarded INSERT (only when the table is empty) matching the seed file, then write per-environment credentials. Keep the row inactive until configured.
Tip: An empty result with no error is usually empty data, not a failed call. When promoting a new environment, list every init/seed action and check each one ran.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: 'Newest row' resume logic broken by another writer
Symptom: Approving a request fails with 'The current approval item is not available' although the task exists and the UI sends the right data.
Cause: The resume path takes the request's newest event-data row; another action inserts a row with an empty task list into the same table on every approve.
Fix: Take recent rows and pick the newest with a non-empty task list; better, filter by the row's purpose.
Tip: Whenever logic reads the 'newest' row, check what other features write to that table. An error message may describe the lookup that failed rather than the real state.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: AND combinations in a duplicate check degrade when a field is empty
Symptom: The log says 'Combination 3 matched' but shows only one field, and flags duplicates wrongly.
Cause: Condition building skips empty-valued fields, so an AND group (name + tax id) with no tax id runs as name only.
Fix: If any AND field of a combination has no value, drop that AND part and keep only independent OR fields.
Tip: Agree semantics with QA/BA: a missing key is skipped, null means the check runs but does not match, '' matches every blank row (up to 80% of real data). Test stubs that drop ''/null hide the '' path.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Rule condition lookup not scoped by object type
Symptom: A naming-rule call returns 400 ('business table not part of model') blocking Save/Submit; another rule shows 'Invalid Value'.
Cause: The rule-condition association is always empty so a fallback looks conditions up by condition ID only, and the same ID exists under another object type with a different table.
Fix: Scope the fallback by object type and attach to each rule only its own conditions.
Tip: IDs shared across object types are a trap. Write replay tests with real environment fixtures; SELECT COALESCE(...) FROM DUMMY always returns a row so the error branch may be dead code.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: CORS preflight not answered by a stdlib server
Symptom: A cross-origin app cannot start runs; the server looks normal because the POST never arrives; dropdowns are empty.
Cause: A JSON POST is not a simple request so the browser sends OPTIONS, and BaseHTTPRequestHandler returns 501; GETs lack Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
Fix: Implement do_OPTIONS returning 204 with Allow-Origin/Methods/Headers/Max-Age and add the origin header to responses (a wildcard is acceptable only when the server binds localhost only).

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Serverless Postgres: versions, pooling and idle suspend
Symptom: A schema that runs on local Postgres may not match production; the first request after idle is slow or hits a dead connection.
Cause: The managed provider runs a higher major version than the local Docker image; free-tier compute suspends and the pooler cuts idle sockets.
Fix: Rerun the schema suite on the target DB while it is empty; enable pool_pre_ping (adds ~1 s to the first request after idle).
Tip: Guard destructive DB tests: skip when the test URL is unset and refuse non-local hosts without explicit opt-in. Usually only the connection string is needed; skip the provider's onboarding wizard.

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: A message-fetching CLI silently capped at 200
Symptom: A large channel looks complete when read through the CLI.
Cause: The messages get command is hard-capped at 200 rows per call regardless of the limit passed.
Fix: Page backwards with the --before cursor until a page returns fewer than 200 rows.
Tip: The search filter takes authors as hex pubkey/npub, not display names.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: GCS buckets with UBLA and public access prevention
Symptom: Upload/download from a Cloud Run app to a private bucket is needed; signed URLs cannot be signed under ADC.
Cause: Uniform bucket-level access + public access prevention means no ACLs/public objects; ADC on Cloud Run has no private key so V4 signing needs IAM signBlob, which storage.admin does not grant.
Fix: Simplest: proxy bytes through a server API route (runtime SA holds the storage role, no CORS needed). For direct browser signed URLs, grant the SA serviceAccountTokenCreator on itself and add CORS to the bucket.
Tip: Use ADC on Cloud Run and 'gcloud auth application-default login' locally; do not use key files.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Hidden storage growth: backup retention and build junk
Symptom: Storage cost rises several-fold over months with no new users; the bucket inventory missed 99% of the volume.
Cause: Maximum backup retention fills up gradually; the Cloud Build source bucket accumulates a tarball per deploy with no lifecycle rule.
Fix: Decide retention as a policy. Add lifecycle rules (Standard -> Nearline -> Coldline, delete build junk).
Tip: Measure volume with Cloud Monitoring total_bytes across ALL buckets. Object versioning nearly doubles storage; soft delete does not save overwritten objects.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: A PyInstaller rebuild wipes settings and state
Symptom: After a rebuild the filled-in .env is replaced by an empty template and token/queue state risks being lost.
Cause: PyInstaller deletes the output folder before collecting, so the 'copy .env only if absent' logic always runs.
Fix: Move .env, config and state folders out before building and put them back afterwards, even on failure. Never build into a folder holding real credentials.
Tip: Prefer one-dir over one-file: one-file unpacks to temp so relative state lands in temp, is slower and more likely blocked by antivirus. Resolve config next to the executable, not by cwd.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Duplicate reads: load once, publish per-item results
Symptom: A list page runs one query per row to compute badges that the dashboard precompute already computed and discarded.
Cause: Aggregate and per-item computations read the same data separately.
Fix: Run the per-item computation during the existing load, publish results with computed_at, and have readers reuse them only when newer than the item's updated_at, else compute live.
Tip: On Cloud Run, socket push counts toward the request timeout, keeps a billed instance, occupies a concurrency slot and needs Pub/Sub fan-out with several instances.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: OCR language claims and confidence are unreliable
Symptom: An OCR model said to support Vietnamese produces wrong characters with 0.91-1.00 confidence.
Cause: The Latin recogniser's charset lacks most Vietnamese letters and all diacritic combinations, so it confidently substitutes look-alikes.
Fix: Check the charset embedded in the ONNX metadata (key 'character') before trusting language claims; pair a good detector with a language-specific recogniser.
Tip: Diff a known line instead of trusting confidence. RapidOCR 3.x is configured per stage (Rec.lang_type) and values must be enums.

LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: The local gate is green but the frontend does not compile
Symptom: The local CI gate reports all green, but the Docker build then fails on type errors or the merged frontend does not build.
Cause: The gate only runs Python checks and vitest, not 'tsc -b', so type errors in code no unit test touches slip through.
Fix: Add 'tsc -b' (and vitest) to the gate. Meanwhile, when changing the frontend run 'npx tsc -b' and 'npx vitest run' yourself.
Tip: Know exactly what the gate checks. A byte-compile step limited to one folder will not cover tools/ or scripts/.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: A local .env file breaks HANA test skips
Symptom: The gate reports HANA tests failing with 'connection refused' instead of skipping, or the suite hangs on an unrelated test; each test takes ~33 s and burns Firestore quota. A clean worktree passes.
Cause: The package loads the (gitignored) .env into os.environ at import so the 'HANA vars present' skipif does not trigger; an old .env still selects HANA; bare pytest without the runner's sqlite default calls real Firestore.
Fix: Run the suite via the repo's runner (default DB sqlite); export the HANA vars as empty strings (python-dotenv does not override existing keys, empty strings are falsy); blank DB env at job level in CI; start Docker/HANA when the live tier is needed.
Workaround: Run in a clean worktree or temporarily move .env aside.
Tip: 'Only fails on my machine' is usually env/config: diff the environment before debugging code, and spot environment faults by socket errors. Do not bypass the gate (SKIP_CI).

LESSON LEARNED [Backend & Data]: Paging and polling correctness details
Symptom: Clients misjudge the end of a list when the last page is exactly the limit; thread reply counts freeze in the channel view.
Cause: has_more inferred from row count; the poll short-circuits on the newest message id, which thread replies do not change.
Fix: Fetch limit+1 and return has_more explicitly; key the poll on all ids and reply counts. Use time-ordered ids (ULID) so keyset paging needs no timestamp index.
Tip: Test the exactly-limit boundary.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Tests calling helpers directly skip the real wiring
Symptom: Tests are green but the feature never ran live: a build script's --clean wiped settings while tests passed; an agent-to-agent chain died with 404; a 'use case' passed/failed for unrelated reasons.
Cause: Tests call inner functions directly or build inputs themselves (made-up session ids, self-created invoker ids) so they skip the main()/dispatch path with the ordering bug; __getattr__ delegation does not run on ABC subclasses; local stubs drift from real signatures.
Fix: Go through the real entry point/dispatch route with fakes for external tools; create preconditions via the app's own API; write explicit delegation so the ABC enforces the full interface; derive expected values from the original implementation.
Tip: Hand-built test inputs can skip the broken path. Fake stores must remember writes; use an injected clock instead of sleep.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Prove a test can tell pre-fix code apart
Symptom: Tests are green but would still be green without the fix.
Cause: Tests written together with the fix easily become tautologies.
Fix: Run the suite on a worktree of the pre-fix code (it must fail exactly the bug's assertion); disable each part of the fix in turn and restore (restore in finally); remove the fix from the built artefact and rerun the browser check.
Tip: Compare typecheck error sets before/after (normalised paths, line numbers), not just counts. Put the baseline worktree outside any node_modules so module resolution does not create phantom differences.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Port parity: measure the old library, do not read its code
Symptom: Parity tests fail on wrong expectations, or the harness passes without touching deep cases; a 'safer' port silently returns plausible wrong values.
Cause: Expectations derived from reading lodash/deepdash code were repeatedly wrong; an LCG seeded 1..N produced correlated draws so depth never exceeded 2; added optional chaining turned an old TypeError into 'Invalid Date'.
Fix: Run the old code verbatim with real dependencies alongside the port on a generated corpus (tens of thousands of cases) and diff everything, key order included. Build a differential harness per helper before the module composing them, have the harness assert its own coverage, keep old quirks and document them.
Tip: Exclude known-difference areas by name instead of silently passing them. Confirm the old code is really what runs before porting; rerun the runbook from an empty folder before committing.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: A hidden browser tab makes UI measurement meaningless
Symptom: A prompt sits idle until clicked; screenshots time out; a timer-based sampler has gaps and 'proves' a fix that was never verified.
Cause: Chrome freezes workers and throttles setInterval to ~1 per minute when document.hidden = true, even with focus.
Fix: Check document.hidden before measuring; use MutationObserver or server logs instead of timers; wake the tab with a real click. Countdowns must compute from a deadline, not subtract per tick.
Tip: Anything with a deadline must be driven by a script inside the page, not one tool call per click (the round trip arrives too late).

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Browser automation traps with Chrome tooling
Symptom: Clicks hit the wrong row or only hover, menus do not open, drag/focus do nothing, keystrokes vanish, file:// pages are refused, calls time out.
Cause: Screenshots are scaled/padded relative to innerWidth (DPR); find+ref click right after navigate in the same batch; Radix menus open on pointerdown; synthetic mouse drags do not start HTML5 drag; the extension refuses file://; long await loops exceed CDP's 45 s limit; CDP websockets with an Origin header are refused.
Fix: Click by element ref and verify via DOM/JS/API when screenshot width != innerWidth; separate find and click; dispatch PointerEvent/DragEvent sharing one DataTransfer; React inputs need the native value setter + an 'input' event; serve local files with a temporary http.server on localhost then shut it down; poll with short calls; websocket-client suppress_origin=True.
Workaround: If drag cannot be made reliable, create the state via the API then verify the rendering.
Tip: A locator matching the wrong element reports success exactly like a correct match. Leave no tabs/servers behind on the user's machine; single-key shortcuts in a panel can create junk records.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: dayjs is not a drop-in replacement for moment
Symptom: After replacing moment with dayjs, hundreds of date conversions differ from legacy: invalid dates roll over, '0', 1, -1, true parse as epoch.
Cause: dayjs non-strict mode is far looser; moment scores every format in an array and picks the best match; dayjs has no ISO_8601 token; moment().add(undefined) is a no-op while dayjs gives NaN.
Fix: Parse strictly per format, add a separate ISO branch (regex, calendar check, utc), mirror add() with '?? 0'. Prove it with a diff on a value corpus against real moment.
Tip: Watch for mixed-timezone arithmetic in old code; document it instead of silently fixing it, since fixing changes stored defaults.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: A DPI-unaware screenshot tool gives wrong results
Symptom: The UI seems to overflow the bottom of the window and a size 'fix' seems to confirm it; another time it captured a terminal but still reported success.
Cause: The capture tool runs DPI-unaware at 125% scaling so it grabs only the top-left 80%; it finds windows by the first title substring match (a terminal tab shares the project name).
Fix: Declare per-monitor DPI awareness before anything else; rank matching windows (exact title, terminals last); for Flutter use PrintWindow with PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT and a nudge-resize to force repaint.
Tip: A tool that reports plausible but wrong numbers is more dangerous than one that fails. Synthetic SendMessage clicks do nothing on Flutter windows.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: A slow test gate: a process per file, network by default, Defender
Symptom: The local gate takes 6-28 minutes; many tests take exactly ~33 s each; Defender eats CPU during tests.
Cause: One subprocess per test file (~1.5 s import), no pytest-xdist; the default DB backend goes to the real network so uniform 33 s means timeouts; some tests build huge fake data; Defender real-time scans every .pyc, temp DB and new worker.
Fix: Run one pytest session with the DB backend env = sqlite (job-level env in CI too), install xdist for parallelism, shrink fake data. Set PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX outside the repo, never run two gates at once, ask IT for a narrow Defender exclusion.
Tip: Identical repeated durations mean timeouts, not computation. Profile the slowest tests first; enable a require-flag so skipped guards turn red (skips print like passes).

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Before/after comparisons need an immutable baseline
Symptom: Failures are blamed on the wrong change; a 'before vs after' comparison was really new code vs new code; running a subset reports 'all green' while the full suite fails; tests pass alone but fail together.
Cause: The baseline was taken after the edit; git stash on a clean tree does nothing; only a few files were run; another session's uncommitted work shares the tree; some failures pre-exist due to env/Windows environment.
Fix: Create a detached worktree at the base commit, run the baseline there, then apply the diff (git diff > patch; git apply) to run 'after'. Record the baseline failure set, compare the after failure set, and always run the full suite via the repo's runner before reporting green.
Tip: Run the two comparisons sequentially; running in parallel makes one run 4x slower and look like a regression. If you stash for a baseline, remember to pop.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: A new worktree needs setup before gate results can be trusted
Symptom: In a new worktree the gate goes red as if the change broke it: WinError 206 'filename too long', tests returning 503, vitest failing with ERR_PNPM_ABORTED_REMOVE_MODULES_DIR_NO_TTY or skipped but counted as passed.
Cause: The runner builds one command line listing every test file by absolute path, exceeding Windows' 32,767-character limit with deep paths. Gitignored build output (dist, node_modules) is missing; a copied pnpm node_modules breaks the store layout.

Tip: Prove a failure pre-exists by running the same tests on a clean base.

LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Tests passing for the wrong reason (assertions that cannot fail)
Symptom: A test fails with an unexplained 'assert [] == [expected]'; a test does not catch the regression it was written for; an absence check passes because the page became a login redirect; async tests are skipped but reported as passing.
Cause: A missing stub for a new dependency plus 'except Exception: pass' swallowing the error; fixtures with a shape that does not exist so None == None; the test feeds the same value into two branches; an OR assertion with an always-true side; pytest-asyncio missing.
Fix: Stub every current call, build fixtures from the current contract, compare semantic fields rather than whole structs with timestamps. Feed different values into each branch, pair absence checks with a 'page rendered' check, install pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode=auto).
Tip: Presence is not correctness: assert the property you need (a real domain), not a proxy (contains @). Test against an independent implementation, not code sharing your own logic.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Process-global caches make tests order-dependent
Symptom: Tests pass alone but fail in the full parallel suite; env/config leaks between tests.
Cause: Global memo caches (command path resolution, an lru_cache composition root reading env vars, config imported once per process) were already filled by earlier tests.
Fix: In tests, take a shared lock and clear caches before and after the operation; clear the cached composition root in fixture teardown; split suites that set env at import into separate processes.
Tip: Any test changing PATH/env must reset global caches both ways, so it neither reads nor leaves dirty state.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Unreproducible gates and empty 'green'
Symptom: The README quotes test:cov/typecheck commands and coverage numbers nobody can rerun; a Playwright harness goes green against any process on a common port; repo typecheck shows thousands of errors.
Cause: The scripts were never defined and no coverage provider is installed; reuseExistingServer silently used an unrelated local server; pre-existing typecheck debt.
Fix: Wire the documented commands with hard coverage thresholds and replace old numbers with measured ones. Make server reuse opt-in and use a non-default port; if typecheck is not a gate, report per file (0 errors in edited files).
Workaround: Install browsers separately (PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1 for API-only projects) and split api/browser projects.
Tip: A reasoned skip when credentials are missing is fine; treating an unreachable backend as green (skip-as-pass) is not.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Driving a canvas UI (Flutter/Flet) through Chrome DevTools
Symptom: CDP clicks report success but screenshots are identical; screenshots are blank; clicks land off target; the debug port does not open.
Cause: Canvas UIs need buttons:1 in mouse events; Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride blanks the compositor; input uses CSS pixels while screenshots are device pixels; Chromium hands the URL to an already running profile.
Fix: Send buttons:1; resize with Browser.setWindowBounds after windowState:'normal'; divide screenshot coordinates by devicePixelRatio; launch with a dedicated --user-data-dir.
Tip: A screenshot identical to the last one means the input was dropped, not that nothing changed.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Config IDs are per environment; ticket repro steps can be wrong
Symptom: A route taken from a ticket crashes in another environment with 'Cannot read properties of undefined' and an endless spinner, looking like a broken build; or the repro steps never reproduce.
Cause: Template IDs and config exist per environment; the environment/link/template in the ticket does not match the config actually causing the failure.
Fix: Query that environment's own config (OData or DB) to find the template that really has the failing setup, then rewrite the repro.
Tip: Do not carry routes from one environment to another. When estimating impact, check where data was created; simple joins easily overcount.

LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Logic duplicated in two languages will drift
Symptom: The review screen shows wrong labels; the same option value means different things in two questions; form and export may disagree on visibility.
Cause: A parallel global label table needs manual sync; visibility logic exists in both Python and JavaScript.
Fix: Generate labels from a single spec; express rules as data run by the same evaluator on server and page; prove parity by running the page's JS against the server resolver on hundreds of random vectors.
Tip: Enforce invariants with seed-time guards that fail loudly (units for numeric questions, no orphan categories, no circular references).

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: An audit tool must evaluate the weakest branch, not the first
Symptom: A security audit reports a control as satisfied/partial when it is not.
Cause: Only the first matching ref was evaluated when a rule exists on several branches; rules for non-existent branches counted as 'weakest'; nothing compliant still reported partial.
Fix: Evaluate the weakest existing ref, ignore rules for refs that do not exist, report 'none' when nothing is compliant and 'unknown' when evidence is missing.
Tip: Write several use cases per control; never mark PASS from one case.

LESSON LEARNED [Testing & QA]: Flaky RTL tests reading data from a second fetch
Symptom: Tests pass locally but fail at the frontend gate in CI.
Cause: getBy* reads a cell synchronously before the second fetch fills it: a race local runs happened to win.
Fix: Use await findBy* for anything filled asynchronously; run repeatedly to confirm stability.
Tip: Record pre-existing failures so new ones stand out.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Headless 'claude -p' loads the user's settings, hooks and CLAUDE.md
Symptom: Asking for the single word 'ok' makes the CLI return a paragraph about a Stop hook; the agent posts its own hook chatter into a chat channel; tool-free turns inside a repo try to read files and run 2-3x slower.
Cause: 'claude -p' loads the settings/hooks/CLAUDE.md of the logged-in profile (inheriting CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) and the cwd's CLAUDE.md; --bare skips them but forces API-key auth.
Fix: Set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR explicitly per turn, pass --setting-sources '' (or 'project'), put instructions in --system-prompt, use --mcp-config with --strict-mcp-config, and run tool-free turns from a neutral temp folder.
Tip: An empty string is a real argument value: do not split args on whitespace or filter empty entries; keep flags from being overridden. Verify with a probe dir whose CLAUDE.md demands a marker word, and a prompt requiring an exact token (e.g. 'ENGINE_OK').

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Large hook output does not reach the model
Symptom: Rules delivered by hooks (a ~38 KB personalization block, a 12 KB prompt guard) are ignored; the assistant uses a forbidden form of address despite four rules forbidding it.
Cause: Claude Code saves hook output above ~10 KB to a file and shows the model only a ~2 KB preview; the payload is ordered by similarity so important rules fall outside the preview, and conflicting rules have no precedence.
Fix: Keep each hook payload small, deterministically ordered, with explicit precedence/supersedes; put critical rules in short always-loaded text phrased affirmatively.
Tip: Measure what actually enters context (the transcript), not what the hook emits.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Child CLIs inherit the environment of the Claude Code session that launched them
Symptom: A child CLI uses a different default profile, inherits the effort level or behaves like a child session.
Cause: The server was started from inside a Claude Code session so CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CLAUDE_EFFORT, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID... are in the env and passed straight through dict(os.environ).
Fix: Scrub those variables by EXACT NAME in the launcher or child env builder. Do not strip by prefix, because 'CLAUDE_CODE_' also matches CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and 'ANTHROPIC' matches the API key, silently logging the machine out.
Workaround: Start the server from a clean terminal.
Tip: Show inherited env in the settings UI to find leaked variables; making a leak visible is not fixing it.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: A static hook menu drifts from the policy table
Symptom: A newly pushed policy action (or renamed sub-action) is never chosen, although the API and the sqlite table look fine.
Cause: The UserPromptSubmit hook's action menu is static text stored in the hook rule, not generated from the policy table despite what its text says; agents may only choose from the menu.
Fix: Every time an action is added/renamed/removed, edit the hook text in the same job and verify by reading the hook row from the database, not trusting the POST response.
Tip: Publishing to the store and publishing to the surface that reads the store are two separate acts; only the second changes behaviour. Long term, generate the menu from the table.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Verify claims instead of carrying them forward
Symptom: The AI repeats 'the CI runner is dead', 'feature X has not started', 'nothing ran last night' and 'still open' items already fixed, all false when checked.
Cause: Claims copied from old logs, reports or subagent output without live verification; reading only agent logs without the work log/knowledge base.
Fix: Re-measure live (git fetch, ls-remote, platform CLI, source, work log) before stating status and mark what is unverified; independently check subagent results; answer within the project scope asked.
Tip: When corrected, fix the false claim at its source (docs, CI comment, report) so it stops spreading. 'No data' in a store being written to is only true at the moment of reading.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: A tool-less LLM reviewer fabricates results and hangs
Symptom: The reviewer returns UNKNOWN, invents Read/Glob XML tool calls and file content then writes VERDICT: PASS, or hangs until the 600 s limit.
Cause: The prompt carried only evidence paths and hashes, no code; a long prompt was spooled to a file the reviewer cannot read; 'docker run -i' kept stdin open; exhausting the model-start budget surfaced only as a RuntimeError.
Fix: Inline the (bounded) diff into the prompt with the sentence 'this turn has no tools'; inline spooled content instead of telling the model to read a file; gate only on listed tests; drop -i.
Tip: Keep the verdict parser fail-closed. Reproduce the exact prompt outside the pipeline to separate model faults from call-path faults.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: A silent agent: do not keep pinging, check the process and host connection
Symptom: A seat finally answers but has lost recent decisions; or a tagged agent stops answering while CLI posts still work.
Cause: Seats read only a small window (~12) of recent messages so repeated pings push the task message out; a silent agent is usually mid-turn; the desktop app hosting agents has an idle auto-disconnect while the CLI uses its own relay connection.
Fix: Do not spam pings; if context was lost, re-ground with ONE self-contained message pointing at committed state (branch, merge request, evidence file); reconnect the desktop app via its 'Reconnecting' control.
Workaround: Use a Win32 automation CLI so the agent can reconnect the desktop app itself (browser automation cannot drive a Tauri app).
Tip: Silence does not mean disconnection: check the process first, then the desktop connection state. Verify the responder's public key since an impostor seat with the same name can answer.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Relay-based agent communities: membership, identity, mentions
Symptom: A newly created agent never shows or answers; the runtime logs 'not a relay member' although start-agent reported success; lease returns 403; a seat ignores messages writing '@seat' in text; a colleague's machine's seat cannot be tagged.
Cause: Relay membership is per key with no auto-admission, so an owner/admin must admit each new key; the agent profile lacks status/channel_ids/respond_to; seats identify the addressee only by p-tag; a same-named local seat shadows the remote one in the mention picker.
Fix: Ask a real owner/admin to admit (verify the role); seal identity right after mount; republish the full profile signed by the seat key on lease 403; mention by pubkey, not prose.
Tip: A control verb's success is not evidence; read the runtime log. Resolve seat names on the relay with your own key before blaming membership; never hand-edit state files while the desktop app runs.

Symptom: A turn returns status 200, no stderr, but the answer is 'I need your permission to read marker.txt'.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Anthropic API parameters that fail silently
Symptom: Requests succeed but effort, thinking text or caching have no effect; or 400 when enabling thinking.
Cause: Top-level effort is ignored (it belongs in output_config); thinking display defaults to 'omitted'; temperature together with thinking is a 400; a cache breakpoint on a block holding per-turn data never hits; a prefix below the minimum is not cached and not reported.
Fix: Put effort in output_config and validate it; request summarized thinking display; drop temperature when thinking; place cache breakpoints on the stable system prompt.
Tip: Order prompts from far to near (stable policy/tools first, the user's words last) for both salience and prefix caching.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: A hook wired in settings but silently a no-op
Symptom: A PreToolUse hook declared in settings.json runs, returns 200 and exits 0 on every tool call but does nothing, still costing a round trip.
Cause: The hook fetches rule text from a local server and exits early when empty; the server had no rule row for that hook type; the matcher also missed Bash/PowerShell.
Fix: After wiring a hook, read back each event's actual payload and confirm it is non-empty; add a reconciliation check between declared hooks and rule rows; extend the matcher to shell tools. Or delete the hook entry.
Tip: ABSENCE-type faults pass every health check. PreToolUse (and Stop) are the only hooks that can deny; an empty one wastes the strongest control.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: TaskStop is not a kill
Symptom: A 'stopped' background delete was reported as having deleted nothing, but the data was actually gone.
Cause: TaskStop only detaches the harness from the process and the child keeps running; the output pipe was closed so the completion line was never recorded.
Fix: Kill the actual OS process and confirm it exited; verify the effect on the data, not the task status.
Tip: 'Task stopped' does not prove the work stopped. Destructive scripts should log progress to a durable file.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Guarding model-written shell commands
Symptom: A broad search command written by the model froze the whole machine; a templated 'command' field ran model text unguarded.
Cause: The guard was chosen by which field was filled, not by the text's source; no path fence; Get-ChildItem -Recurse ignores .gitignore and walks into node_modules.
Fix: Allow-list whole command phrases ('git status', not 'git'), reject command-chaining characters (; | & > < backtick $( newline) and recursive switches including PowerShell prefixes; an empty allow list means run nothing; cap commands per step and truncate output.
Tip: Suggest git ls-files instead of recursive walks; give the node a workingDirectory instead of 'git -C <path>'. Any design needing approval first needs a way to ask the user mid-turn.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: An MCP server that silently never starts
Symptom: The agent has no MCP tools; spawn returns an empty list in under two seconds with no visible error.
Cause: Two bugs hidden by per-server try/except: stdio_client held in an AsyncExitStack while asyncio.wait_for ran it in another task (anyio cancel-scope error), and MCP SDK 2.x renamed Tool.inputSchema to input_schema.
Fix: Run one long-lived task per server that enters/exits its own async-with context and returns the session via a future; use the 2.x field names; add a test spawning a REAL child MCP server.
Tip: Do not trust 'the code looks right' anywhere a per-item except exists; mocks would pass both bugs.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Another CLI reusing Claude's live sign-in
Symptom: Another AI CLI followed the setup guide and used Claude Code's signed-in helper in the default profile without logging in.
Cause: The guide defined a profile folder only for Claude Code, and the helper's credential-store key is per URL, not per profile, so every profile/CLI shares one sign-in.
Fix: Separate the helper home and credential key per profile; enforce ownership in code (the caller must be the owning CLI, checked via process ancestry); one profile, one sign-in.
Tip: Test isolation with a brand-new profile; an existing keyring entry makes a 'new' profile look signed in.

Symptom: An agent answered confidently from a stored document that had actually expired.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Claude CLI auth errors: the wrong profile, not a broken variable
Symptom: Pointing CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at the default folder seems to break auth; turns fail with 'Something went wrong' and an empty error.
Cause: That profile holds credentials without expiresAt so the CLI cannot refresh; the CLI reports errors in the result field with is_error=true, not in the error field.
Fix: Read both fields, show the error to the user, and name the profile folder and override variable in the auth hint.
Workaround: Run 'claude' interactively once with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointing at that folder, or point the override at a signed-in profile.
Tip: When an env var seems to break something, check whether it merely points somewhere else.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Agent shells have no stdin; claude -p does not wait for background work
Symptom: Interactive CLIs (cf login, account pickers) fail or loop on 'Enter a number' forever; a headless run ends right after printing a sign-in link and the login process dies with it.
Cause: Commands the agent runs (including '!' prefixed ones) have no keyboard on stdin; claude -p exits when the turn ends and does not wait for background tasks.
Fix: Pass answers as arguments (--sso-passcode, --subdomain) or pipe them in; hand interactive steps to the user in a real terminal, then resume the session.
Tip: Capture and forward expiring login URLs immediately. Do not prompt interactively when stdin is not a TTY; an empty Claude profile cannot run claude -p until someone logs in.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Where model-call latency goes when calling through the CLI
Symptom: Each turn takes 1-3 minutes; the progress line is decoration; the effort picker changes nothing.
Cause: Each call spawns the CLI (~2.5 s wrapper + ~22k-token system prompt), output tokens dominate the time, the CLI does not stream reasoning and drops the effort parameter.

Workaround: Show an elapsed-time pulse for each running node so silence is not mistaken for a hang.
Tip: Changing a default only affects new rows; migrate old sessions to apply it immediately.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Repeated hook text eats most of a session's tokens
Symptom: One session carried ~190k tokens of identical hook text, about a third of the conversation.
Cause: UserPromptSubmit runs on every message and PreToolUse on every matching tool call; the text is appended to history and resent all session; a static prompt hook ignores stdin and injects the full menu every time.
Fix: Inject only a short menu and fetch details on demand; make UserPromptSubmit read the prompt from stdin; use the hook 'if' field to filter without spawning; remove instructions duplicated across hooks.
Tip: Savings only happen at write time; only compaction removes history. PostCompact (not PreCompact) is the event that can reinject rules after compaction.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Writing code through shell heredocs corrupts escapes
Symptom: \n in Python source becomes a real newline and breaks f-strings; long heredocs fail with 'unexpected EOF' and write nothing; a PowerShell here-string run under bash creates empty files named after words in the text.
Cause: Shell heredocs/quoting interpret escapes and quotes; bash does not understand @'...'@ so it runs each fragment with redirection; the patch script writes the file before validating.
Fix: Write files with the Write/Edit tool or a small .py script; a patch script must parse (e.g. ast.parse) BEFORE writing; use gh --body-file; check git status --porcelain for junk after complex commands.
Workaround: git checkout the file and reapply only the correct hunk; or define a newline constant at module level.
Tip: Parse first, write second; do not stack a fix script on top of a broken fix script. Do not pipe a file-generating script through head (SIGPIPE kills the writer).

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Scripted text edits/regexes silently delete the wrong code
Symptom: A replace reports 0 hits, a 'successful' replace leaves a syntax error, deleting a function by regex causes NameError/IndentationError elsewhere.
Cause: Trailing spaces from someone else's edit, a mis-placed insertion anchor, a 'from def to next def' regex swallowing module-level constants or a try/except in between.
Fix: Assert the anchor occurs exactly once and print the surrounding bytes' repr on 0 hits; delete by AST or explicit line range; build edits in memory, write once, then syntax check and run tests immediately.
Workaround: Recover the lost part from git diff.
Tip: A printed 'ok' only means some substring matched. After a script aborts, check what was already written before applying parts by hand.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Browser automation stuck on a looping or frozen SPA tab
Symptom: Claude-in-Chrome times out (script injection, screenshots) though the server still answers; mentions post as plain text; the automation tab will not load video.
Cause: The SPA is stuck in a poll/reconnect loop that never goes idle or the renderer froze; reloading the same tab does not clear it; automation tabs block media loading.
Fix: Open a new tab instead of reloading; call the REST API from the signed-in page with javascript_tool instead of scraping the DOM; when posting mentions, pick the right person in the dropdown and screenshot to check before sending.
Workaround: Wait 10-20 s; a frozen renderer often recovers.
Tip: When a script times out, check whether it finished before retrying to avoid double writes. A negative media result from an automation tab is not evidence; check the server access log.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Several sessions working in one repo
Symptom: Commits land on a branch other than the checked-out one; files vanish from the working tree; pushes are repeatedly refused non-fast-forward.
Cause: Several agent and human sessions share the repo through worktrees sharing one .git and push straight to a shared staging branch.
Fix: Work in your own worktree on a new branch; read the branch name from git's output; run 'git worktree list' and 'git branch -a' before assuming loss; fetch before every push; cherry-pick exactly your commits and only reset your own refs.
Tip: Do not leave stashes that can resurrect files another session deleted. Diff a dirty tree against the remote before concluding it is someone else's work.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Tool descriptions must state how matching works and when to call
Symptom: The model searches with a natural sentence then reports 'not found' although the item exists; or it describes building an artefact instead of calling the tool made for it.
Cause: The store matches literal substrings but the model writes whole sentences; the tool description says what the tool does but not when in the flow to use it.
Fix: State in the description that the tool matches text, not meaning, and to pass a single literal word; state the trigger moment; end tool results with 'STOP THERE' when the next step belongs to a human.
Workaround: Retry the sentence word by word, ranking by hit count; or add a one-line reminder in chat.
Tip: Semantic hits over a few short tool descriptions are noise; use them only as hints beside the full catalogue. Do not build a duplicate of an existing tool.

Symptom: Pasting a 'claude setup-token' token into an x-api-key field gets 401 authentication_error.
Cause: OAuth tokens need 'Authorization: Bearer' plus the anthropic-beta oauth header; the API-key header is the wrong form.

Tip: Validate a token directly: rate_limit_error means authenticated, authentication_error means invalid. A token pasted into chat is exposed; rotate it.

Symptom: Every read-only turn costs an extra model round to check the log; interrupted turns and subagent work are never checked.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Agents inventing approval paths and treating memory as reading
Symptom: After a refused step, the model says 'waiting for approval, approve and I will continue' although no approval path exists; an otherwise accurate answer contains a file path that was never read.
Cause: There is no 'ask the user' tier so the model invents one; facts read and facts recalled look identical in prose.
Fix: Add prompt rules at both the reasoning and answer steps: a refusal is final; any path/line/symbol not seen in command output must be checked or marked unverified.
Tip: Force ReAct to stop by cutting everything after the first tool call rather than relying on stop sequences. A model NOT chaining two tools is a safe failure when a human decision is needed between them.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: A subprocess pool leaks slots and the stdio protocol desyncs
Symptom: After a few failed spawns every agent on the runtime returns 'queued' forever; or JSON-RPC over stdio desyncs.
Cause: The pool's semaphore is not released when spawn raises; stderr merged into stdout injects diagnostic lines into the protocol stream.
Fix: Release the slot in try/except/finally for every spawn error and test it; separate the child's stderr from stdout.
Workaround: Restart the container to reclaim leaked slots.
Tip: 'queued' from a bounded pool can be by design or a leak; check the slot accounting.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Agents do not call each other without a roster
Symptom: Agent-calls-agent works but agents never tag each other.
Cause: The system prompt mentions 'other agents' without naming them or saying how to reach them.
Fix: Inject a roster: other agents the calling agent can see and the user can call, one purpose line each, excluding itself and hidden agents; tell it not to tag colleagues out of politeness since each call costs money.
Tip: Keep a chain-depth cap and rate cap as a backstop; notices (queued/failed/spend limit) must not re-enter the tag router or they loop.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: WebFetch summaries drop instructions, or hit 403/empty pages
Symptom: A new agent following a setup page ran the right commands but ignored the user-communication rules; some sites return 403 or an empty body.
Cause: WebFetch returns a model summary (1.4 KB of a 5 KB page), keeping commands and dropping rules; sites block automated fetchers or render client-side.
Fix: Put a read-verbatim instruction in the opening line the user pastes ('read the page word for word with curl -s <url> and follow it exactly'); when blocked, report the data as unverified with references and how the user can fetch it.
Workaround: Try another source but never invent numbers.
Tip: Guides telling the assistant to act 'silently' or 'never show' get refused for transparency; write plainly, one step per line.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Sandboxed agents failing: expired tokens and stale binaries
Symptom: A sandboxed agent's turn ends quickly with no clone, push or reply; the model API returns 401.
Cause: The mounted OAuth token had expired, the read-only mount was root-owned, a helper binary copied from an old builder image returned no credentials, the image lacked the CLI.
Fix: Refresh the token before running (auto-refresh below a threshold), copy credentials in the entrypoint, build the helper binary from the current checkout inside the image.
Tip: The argument list is split on commas, so a NO_PROXY with commas breaks.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: A session cron is not a watchdog
Symptom: An hourly pull job vanishes after reboot and cannot be paused; a 'is Claude still running' check misses network drops and dead sessions.
Cause: CronCreate jobs live in memory, only run while the REPL is idle, die with the session and expire after 7 days.
Fix: Use an OS-level scheduled task for anything that must survive restarts or needs real liveness; use session cron only to resume interrupted turns from the worklog.
Tip: State the limits to the user and record the prompt needed to re-arm. Offset hourly jobs from :00.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: CDP screenshots of canvas UIs are blank or stale
Symptom: Screenshots of a Flutter/Flet app show a blank page after navigation or the frame from before a click; a false bug report was nearly filed.
Cause: Flutter only presents a new frame when it thinks the surface changed; a headed window driven via CDP often does not look changed.
Fix: Nudge the window size with Browser.setWindowBounds, wait, restore, wait, then screenshot.
Tip: Do not use Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride with canvas apps; CDP mouse coordinates are CSS pixels; canvas clicks need buttons:1; type with Input.insertText.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Claude in Chrome does not connect or cannot reach logged-in sessions
Symptom: list_connected_browsers is empty although Chrome is open with the extension installed; a copied Chrome profile carries no sessions; the extension cannot navigate to some hosts.
Cause: Two native messaging hosts (Claude Desktop and Claude Code) register the same extension id; Chrome's App-Bound Encryption blocks reusing copied cookies; the extension lacks site permission.
Fix: Back up then delete Desktop's NativeMessagingHosts registry key and reload the extension; or launch Chrome with --remote-debugging-port and a dedicated --user-data-dir, have a human sign in once, and run probes over CDP.
Workaround: Drive that dedicated Chrome with Playwright connect_over_cdp.
Tip: An open debug port lets any local process read cookies, so use a temporary profile and close it afterwards. Do not mint sessions yourself from secrets readable in env without being asked.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: /vector/add returns ok but the row cannot be read back (scope must be top-level)
Symptom: POST /vector/add returns {status: ok, vector_id} but the row never shows in /log/recent, /vector/scroll or scoped queries; many work logs were silently lost.
Cause: The server routes the row by the top-level 'scope' field (default 'knowledge'), metadata.scope is just a label; top-level project/topic/ts are ignored and the hub does not stamp ts itself.
Fix: Send scope (and project) at the top level AND in metadata, put project/topic/subject/ts (ISO-8601) in metadata, and read the row back after every write.
Workaround: Re-add the same payload with a top-level scope (same id upserts) so the row appears at once; use a wrapper script instead of hand-written curl.
Tip: 'ok' only proves the embedding was computed, not where the row landed. Build JSON bodies with Python/files (curl --data-binary @file), not shell heredocs or PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Default vector ids are a hash of the text: collisions and metadata-merging upserts
Symptom: Two identical messages overwrite each other; two parallel branches 'write once' but the row is filed to the thread that finished last; a metadata key cannot be removed.
Cause: Without an id the hub uses sha256 of the text, so identical text (even across projects) gets the same id; adding the same id upserts but MERGES metadata, and some read routes return no id.
Fix: Always pass an explicit deterministic id (e.g. <session>-<message>) and record the id at write time. To remove a metadata key, delete then re-add.
Workaround: Re-add with the same explicit id to replace the row in place.
Tip: Row counts cannot tell one write from two colliding writes. When deleting by id, delete one id first and check the copy in another project is intact.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Old/superseded records pollute semantic queries
Symptom: Several drafts or contradictory preferences on the same topic pile up; semantic queries return the outdated one and wrong rules still auto-load every session.
Cause: /vector/add always creates a new id, not keyed by topic; version/supersedes markers only help someone actively looking, semantic retrieval ignores them.
Fix: Each living document keeps ONE record: write the new one, read it back, then delete the old one by id (dry-run before and after), with a backup outside the store. Before storing, scroll the whole scope for the same subject.
Workaround: If deletion is impossible: add version + supersedes metadata, name the replaced entries on the first line, treat the highest version as live.
Tip: Do not delete auto-load rules without the owner's approval. Clean up pointers to deleted files too.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: A literal project matcher hijacked by short/generic keywords
Symptom: Project routing confidently (ambiguous=false) picks the wrong project, e.g. the Vietnamese 'nâng cấp hooks' routes to an SAP project, or 'this project'/ticket keys match nothing.
Cause: The matcher does substring matching on raw tokens and ranks by term length; 2-4 character keywords ('cap', 'ai') collide with Vietnamese syllables, and generic words ('implement', 'deploy', 'agent', 'hooks') outrank real aliases.
Fix: Treat keyword-only hits as weak evidence (return ambiguous/weak_only), let only id/alias route; remove generic words from the registry and set conflicts_with between similarly named projects.
Workaround: When matched via a keyword, check the term really is the request's subject; do not let a generic keyword override a scope the user stated or the previous session's scope.
Tip: Measure on the full set of folded terms instead of guessing a length threshold (a threshold would delete real acronyms like sap, btp). After creating/renaming a project, run a regression probe with other projects' common phrases.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: The local clone sits on a frozen default branch
Symptom: Locally read code contradicts current behaviour and nearly produced a wrong analysis; the code graph lacks real call edges.
Cause: The repo was cloned at the GitLab default branch, often a months-old backup/fork; the real working branch differs, and the graph was built from the stale clone.
Fix: Read via origin/<working branch> (git show origin/<branch>:<path>) or the GitLab API files/raw?ref=<branch>; when scanning, pick the richest branch with git rev-list --count.
Tip: Check git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD against the branch list before trusting files. Treat the graph as a hint source and confirm edges with git grep on the live branch.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Deleting data leaves residue in Chroma and shared stores
Symptom: After deleting a project/collection the disk is still large, old sensitive text is still readable, and the deleted project still shows through shared collections.
Cause: Chroma keeps orphan segment dirs and embeddings_queue (full text) after a drop, vacuum only frees pages; project delete misses shared collections and delete-by-id only deletes from the first collection.
Fix: For a clean copy, rebuild a new store through the client (copy id/document/metadata/embedding, verify every row); project delete must sweep every shared store and report per store.
Workaround: Stop the server, delete orphan segment dirs, vacuum; run delete twice for duplicate ids.
Tip: Treat 'delete' as unfinished until shared collections and on-disk residue are checked (one rebuilt store went from 677 MB to 5 MB).

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: A Chroma HNSW index unreadable while metadata is intact
Symptom: Every policy match call returns 500 'Error creating hnsw segment reader: Nothing found on disk'; list endpoints still return every row.
Cause: The vector store was copied by hand: the SQLite metadata copied fully but the HNSW segment folders did not (or the index is corrupt in a shared tier every query touches).
Fix: Post each row from the instance's own list endpoint back into the add/upsert route to re-embed and rewrite the index; only copy stores with the server stopped or via export/import.
Tip: With a broken index and intact metadata, ask at once whether the store was copied; do not chase coincident workloads. Failures even on brand-new collections point at a shared tier.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Wrong request shapes return empty instead of an error
Symptom: Search returns 0 hits, delete returns 200 but removes nothing, looking like 'no data'.
Cause: Field names differ between routes (add takes 'text', scroll returns 'source_text', hybrid needs 'query', resolve/hybrid need source_id); DELETE without data_scope is a no-op; project search needs both scope and project; /vector/scroll's scope is a collection name (a wrong name even creates a junk collection).

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Scroll 'matched' capped by the limit, broken offset
Symptom: A 104-row partition reports matched=5 at limit 5 and matched=50 at limit 50; offset >= limit returns an empty page although rows remain.
Cause: The route returned the fetched row count instead of the true total, and fetched limit rows from position 0 before slicing by offset.
Fix: Sum per-collection totals for matched and fetch offset+limit per lane.
Workaround: Treat the partition as fully read only when the returned count is strictly below the limit; otherwise raise the limit or paginate.
Tip: A 'paginate if matched > limit' rule never fires when matched is capped; test pagination on a partition of known size.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Registry POST merges lists but overwrites scalars
Symptom: Re-posting a project with trimmed alias/keyword lists (even with a replace flag) keeps the old keywords; an old project's bare keyword hijacks a new project.
Cause: The project upsert route unions list fields and replaces scalar fields; there is no route to remove a keyword.
Fix: To shrink a list: edit the projects manifest on disk (back it up first) then call the registry sync route; change scalars with a normal POST (idempotent upsert on the same id).
Tip: conflicts_with must be written on BOTH projects. After editing, verify with resolve queries and a few vector queries; check the resolver first to avoid duplicate ids.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Semantic routing (policy/project/intent) cannot be tuned cleanly
Symptom: The router fires the wrong policy for unrelated requests (git pull triggering the code-scan policy) or returns null for Vietnamese sentences.
Cause: The false-fire score band overlaps the true-positive band so no threshold separates them; the embedder (bge-small-en-v1.5) is English-only; intents stored as keyword bags and embedded tags dilute the signal.
Fix: Replace vector routing with a deterministic table: the agent picks an action label from a menu, lookup by exact SELECT, unknown labels return 404, 'none' is a valid answer.
Workaround: If vectors must stay: translate to English first, many short verb-first rows, no tags, fall back to conversation context.
Tip: A null match on a non-English sentence is a language problem, not proof there is no policy. A benchmark the agent grades itself is not independent evidence.
