LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Absolute paths in stored rules expire silently
Symptom: Hook/policy rules point at a drive or install path that no longer exists; every session starts with a failing call, and an HTTP fallback hid the error for weeks.
Cause: The install moved between drives/machines but stored text hard-codes the drive root; an older wrapper copy lacked the op the rule needed.
Fix: Reference files relative to the install (resolved at call time), sweep every table for old paths when the install moves, verify the target on disk before editing, keep a single copy of helper scripts.
Workaround: Read a hard-coded path as a file name inside the install and resolve it against the real install location; do not conclude a tool is missing just because the drive letter is wrong.
Tip: Beware decoy empty folders with correct-looking paths.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Install copies fork data and VERSION files cannot be trusted
Symptom: A test instance does not bind its port, lacks routes the live one has, or nearly writes into the real store; reads on one machine miss writes on another.
Cause: A hand-written VERSION file (old builds with the same VERSION string); copying an install with its data store creates an unsynchronised fork; copied project rows keep absolute paths into the real install; locked files copy as 0-byte stubs; startup takes 80-100 s loading the embedding model.
Fix: Identify the running build from the binary's mtime against commit dates and live behaviour; clone the current live install, use the SQLite online backup API, check row paths before testing writes; launch detached (Start-Process) and poll /health with a deadline.
Tip: Treat a copied data store as a fork and decide reconciliation explicitly. Make the hub URL one setting for every node and restore it after testing.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: graphify/gitnexus scans of large repos hang or go wrong
Symptom: A whole-repo extract hangs for hours with no output, import fails with 422, checkout refused as dirty, merged graphs have duplicate node ids, a rescan yields the union of two branches.
Cause: Without --code-only it runs a keyless LLM phase and retries silently; pathological files (100+ MB JSON fixtures, minified JS) and nested git repos cause hangs; node ids are relative to the scan root; the cache writes into the repo; /codegraph/import only upserts, never deletes.
Fix: Scan per group/repo with --code-only and --max-workers, put a .graphifyignore in each scan root, add artefacts to .git/info/exclude; namespace ids before merging; snapshot the old graph, diff and delete vanished ids.
Tip: graphify does not parse .cds, UI5 XML or HANA calc views (install tree_sitter_sql); for gitnexus use analyze --skip-git --index-only --embeddings 0. A code graph holds structure only; config questions go to the live system; skip vendored code communities.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: A write-side feature flag hides data on read
Symptom: Disabling a cache/window feature made rows still in the window vanish from every read and get stuck forever.
Cause: The read lane was gated by the same enable flag as writes, and the sweep exits early when disabled.
Fix: Gate reads by scope only; when disabled, drain the window to the system of record on the next write.
Tip: Never let a write-side flag control reads. Write-triggered sweeps: a new cap applies only on the next write, and spilling is one-way.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: PDF extraction: missing or broken text layer
Symptom: Text extraction returns empty although the PDF has content, or produces mangled diacritics (common with Vietnamese).
Cause: The PDF is an image-only scan, or its text layer has poor font encoding/embedded OCR.
Fix: Check the text layer first; if absent/broken render pages to PNG (~150-200 dpi with PyMuPDF) and read with vision/OCR, or obtain a clean conversion before ingesting.
Workaround: Store only reliable metadata (title, table of contents) and mark the record incomplete.
Tip: Spot-check text quality before storing as knowledge; note in the entry that re-reading needs OCR/vision.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: 'Full' source documents may be abridged or duplicates
Symptom: A file supplied as the 'full' document looks complete but is much smaller than the original; two files with different names/hashes are actually one document.
Cause: File names and closing notes overstate completeness (content summarised with ...); the same content re-exported gives different bytes.
Fix: Measure completeness before treating it as authoritative (size/line count vs page count, section count, count of ...); dedupe by extracted content, not hash or name.
Workaround: Store it explicitly as a summary, not as the legally effective text.
Tip: Never trust a file name's claim of being 'complete'.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Automation writes knowledge into the wrong project
Symptom: A work log about a project is stored in the chat app's partition by session topic; readers of the owning project never see it.
Cause: The end-of-turn workflow node hard-codes the project name instead of using the project resolved for the turn.
Fix: Map the resolved project from session state into the write node, with a separate branch for turns that resolved no project.
Tip: Conversation history may belong to the chat app, but knowledge it produces must go to the owning project.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Diacritic folding does not fold the Vietnamese letter đ
Symptom: An alias stored without diacritics ('dieu tra') does not match when the user types đ; queries sent through the shell sometimes turn diacritics into '?'.
Cause: Server-side folding strips tone marks but does not fold 'đ' to 'd'; the Windows shell corrupts non-ASCII characters before the HTTP call.
Fix: Store aliases containing 'đ' in both accented and unaccented forms; send non-ASCII queries from a UTF-8 client instead of curl in the shell.
Tip: Verify aliases by probing the matcher, not by reading back the alias list.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: Long single-vector entries lose their tail to search
Symptom: Semantic search never finds facts in the second half of long work logs, with no error.
Cause: Each entry is embedded as one vector without chunking; the small embedder has a hard 512-token limit.
Fix: Chunk long entries into several rows sharing topic/ts, or embed a short summary and store the full text as the document.
Workaround: Use time/topic scrolls (which return full text) instead of semantic queries for logs.
Tip: 512 is an architectural limit of small BERT-style embedders, not a setting.

LESSON LEARNED [Knowledge Hub & Tooling]: A 'configurable' default does not mean it was configured
Symptom: A value reported as set in .env is really a code default; editing .env has no effect; changing a shared env var nearly changed an unrelated cache size.
Cause: The default is derived from another variable, config is read once at import, and .env does not hold that value.
Fix: Set an explicit override for exactly what needs changing, restart the process after editing .env, verify via an introspection endpoint.
Tip: Prove config resolution by importing the config module under different environments instead of reading code lines.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Python crashes printing non-ASCII (cp1252)
Symptom: UnicodeEncodeError 'charmap' on print, often after the real work is done (a POST already created the ticket, a file was written), so it looks like a failure; child tools die before binding their port; HTTP 400 from a mangled body.
Cause: Windows consoles/pipes/file redirects give Python the cp1252 code page; arrows, em-dashes and Vietnamese cannot be encoded. PowerShell 5.1 reads BOM-less .ps1 as ANSI; open() defaults to cp1252.
Fix: Set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 / PYTHONUTF8=1 for every child process, or sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') at startup; always open(..., encoding='utf-8'); build request bodies with json.dumps(...).encode('utf-8'); keep scripts and log markers ASCII.
Workaround: Set the two env vars for just that command.
Tip: Crashing only when output is redirected is the telltale sign. A traceback at the final print: check whether the work already completed before redoing it; add a test with a cp1252 log sink.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: subprocess decodes the wrong code page and stdout becomes None
Symptom: "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip'" or json.loads(None), UnicodeDecodeError reading pwsh/git output.
Cause: subprocess.run(text=True) decodes with the locale (cp1252) while pwsh/git write in the OEM code page (cp437); invalid bytes raise in the reader thread, do not propagate, and stdout comes back None.
Fix: Pass encoding='utf-8' (or the OEM code page via GetOEMCP) with errors='replace', or capture bytes and decode yourself.
Tip: Characters the console page cannot hold are already '?' before decoding; no decoder can recover them. Add a unit test with high bytes.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode silently breaks scripts
Symptom: [Convert]::ToBase64String, .Substring(), [pscustomobject] and DateTime methods fail with 'Method invocation is supported only on core types'; 'powershell -File' cannot dot-source; a generated secret is EMPTY yet accepted.
Cause: Device policy (WDAC) forces PowerShell into ConstrainedLanguage mode: no .NET method calls, no custom objects, broken RNG; native stderr is treated as NativeCommandError.
Fix: Handle string/date/base64 work in Python or Git Bash; invoke scripts with & via pwsh -Command; generate secrets in Python and assert non-empty; call native build tools directly.
Tip: Validate any security material created in this shell before use. String concatenation starting from an ISO-8601 field (typed DateTime) throws; use interpolation or -join.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Command syntax must match the executing shell
Symptom: A command '$env:VAR="x"; gcloud auth login ...' given to the user says 'command not found' at the assignment but still runs the rest and writes into the default gcloud config; git commit -m @'...'@ in the Bash tool yields the subject '@'.
Cause: The '!' prompt and the Bash tool run bash, not PowerShell, even when PowerShell is the primary shell.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: The PowerShell layer corrupts the data you read
Symptom: Stored Vietnamese text looks corrupted; a day's logs seem to vanish; long fields are cut to ~240 characters.
Cause: The fault is in the console layer, not the server: output replaces multi-byte characters with an irrecoverable '?'; Invoke-RestMethod coerces ISO-8601 strings into local-time [datetime] so string filters miss; printing objects truncates to console width.
Fix: For non-ASCII or data you will write back, fetch HTTP directly to a file as bytes and decode UTF-8; convert ToUniversalTime before comparing; use pwsh 7.
Tip: Do not diagnose data corruption from what the shell displays. A read-modify-write through a lossy wrapper stores the corruption for real.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: An old server still answers after a code fix (several instances on one port)
Symptom: A newly added route returns 501/'unknown route', a fixed bug still reproduces, a restarted server looks healthy but runs old code, while the health check returns 200.
Cause: On Windows ThreadingHTTPServer sets allow_reuse_address so a second process binds the SAME port and the old instance keeps answering; a long-running server imports modules once at start; pkill -f or killing by exe name often misses.
Fix: Restart the server after every server-side module edit. Kill by PID from 'netstat -ano' (or match the command line via Win32_Process), confirm ONLY ONE listener on the port and prove the new build via an endpoint only the new code has.
Workaround: Compare the process CreationDate with the source file mtime to detect a server running old code.
Tip: Do not trust the health check alone. Right after a kill the port may still be held; open browser tabs need F5 to get the new bundle.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Windows CRLF breaks LF-enforcing repos
Symptom: Linter/biome reports format errors on files nobody edited, or on every file just edited by a Python script.
Cause: core.autocrlf=true without .gitattributes converts to CRLF on checkout; pathlib write_text (newline=None) writes CRLF; 'git show :path' applies conversion so it hides the problem.
Fix: Add .gitattributes '* text=auto eol=lf', check with 'git grep --cached -lI $'\r'', confirm 'git add --renormalize .' changes no content, then check out again. When writing from Python pass newline='\n'.
Tip: Rewriting JSON with json.dumps also turns CRLF into LF, making diffs look like full replacements. POSIX-only tooling (fcntl, dir_fd) should run in Docker or WSL.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Shell pipes hide exit codes and buffer output
Symptom: A job reports 'nothing new' although git fetch failed; a crashed clone exits 0; long commands look hung with empty output; a chained lint command says 'done' with exit 0 but whose exit code is it.
Cause: if cmd | tail tests tail's exit; piping through tail/head buffers until the end; && / || chains continue after failures; backticks inside double-quoted patterns trigger command substitution; PowerShell turns native stderr into NativeCommandError.
Fix: Use set -o pipefail/PIPESTATUS or capture separately (out=$(cmd 2>&1); rc=$?); redirect long output to a file then tail the file; run each check separately with its own exit code; verify results by reading real state.
Tip: A failed fetch is not evidence of no changes. Do not infer a pass from an exit code printed after a parse error; filter output with loose patterns.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Heredocs and quoting corrupt code/content
Symptom: 'unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote' and nothing written; files with real newlines inside string literals or NUL/backspace bytes; words missing from stored text; filter operators vanish causing HTTP 500.
Cause: Heredocs through the agent's shell interpret \n and escapes, and break on quote-heavy/non-ASCII content; unquoted heredocs expand backticks; PowerShell double quotes expand $eq; non-raw Python strings turn \b into backspace.
Fix: Write code and large documents with the Write/Edit tool instead of heredocs; single-quote JSON in PowerShell; use raw strings, forward slashes or chr(92) for Windows paths in Python.
Tip: Inside a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string single quotes need no escaping. Check for control bytes with cat -A after generating a file; this is a console limit, check the real file before 'fixing'.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Git Bash/MSYS rewrites paths and env vars
Symptom: Paths starting with '/' become '<path> Files/Git/...' causing ENOTFOUND/404 or 'cwd must be an absolute path'; Python cannot open /c/...; Node exits 127 instead of 1.
Cause: Git Bash's MSYS path conversion rewrites arguments and env vars starting with '/' when calling Windows exes, including inline VAR=/x; Python run from the Bash tool is Windows Python; process.exit() with a live fetch socket triggers a libuv assertion.
Fix: Export variables before the command and set MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1, MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=*, MSYS2_ENV_CONV_EXCL=<VAR>. Use C:/ paths in Python; send Connection: close and exit cleanly.
Tip: When a 'dead route' only appears through a script, curl it directly before concluding.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: shutil.which returns a shell script, not the .cmd
Symptom: Running npm/gcloud via subprocess (shell=False) fails with WinError 193 or WinError 2 as if not installed.
Cause: shutil.which('npm'/'gcloud') finds the extensionless shell script; CreateProcess cannot run it, the runnable file is the .cmd and needs cmd.exe.
Fix: Look up the .cmd first on Windows and call it via COMSPEC /c; avoid shell=True so arguments are not re-parsed.
Tip: Some subcommands can still break quoting through the .cmd launcher when the SDK path has spaces.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: git push fails after a long pre-push hook; SSH blocked; stale refs
Symptom: Push fails with exit 141 or 'unable to write flush packet: Broken pipe' right after the hook says 'passed'; push hangs 'port 22: Connection timed out' while fetch works; fetch --all is silent but branches are stale.
Cause: git opens the SSH connection and negotiates refs BEFORE running the hook; a long hook (a new branch has no range so the full suite runs) lets the remote drop the idle socket. Port 22 is firewalled; remote.origin.fetch is pinned to one refspec.
Fix: Use SSH keepalive (ServerAliveInterval/CountMax) or push over HTTPS; use ssh.github.com:443 with -i key; set the fetch refspec +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*; confirm with git ls-remote.
Workaround: Run the gate first so the hook sees a pass stamp and skips; skip hooks only when explicitly asked and the commit passed the full gate.
Tip: 'Connection closed by remote host' amid hook output is the tell. Check core.hooksPath (husky); git push --dry-run still runs hooks; verify pushes by reading the remote ref back; fetch right before pushing and rerun the gate after every rebase.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: The gcloud CLI works but ADC has expired
Symptom: Python SDK scripts fail with 403 PermissionDenied, 'Reauthentication failed. cannot prompt during non-interactive execution' or ~33 s retries, while 'gcloud' commands still work; it looks like a missing IAM role.
Cause: There are two separate credentials expiring separately: the gcloud CLI token and Application Default Credentials. Interactive login gets pushed to the background by the agent's shell; some APIs need a quota project with user tokens.
Fix: Ask the user to run 'gcloud auth login' / 'gcloud auth application-default login' in their own terminal. Call REST APIs (AuthorizedSession) with the working credential; add the 'x-goog-user-project' header when needed.
Workaround: Build clients with google.oauth2.credentials.Credentials(token=<gcloud auth print-access-token>) without ADC.
Tip: 'gcloud config set account' is global state; remember to restore it. Do not upgrade shared libraries just to fix one script; gRPC clients can hang in a sandbox, use REST.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Git credential helpers and SSH identity on Windows
Symptom: A Git Credential Manager popup appears when the agent pushes, or a custom helper fails; SSH auth still succeeds although IdentityFile is wrong.

Tip: When gh CLI is logged in to another account, push via the right SSH alias.

Symptom: Risk of killing other work: a running pytest, another Python server, or the agent's own Claude Code session.

Fix: Match the exact command line or the PID from netstat, and map the parent chain via Win32_Process before killing anything named like a tool in use.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: localhost vs loopback IP, and closed ports that hang
Symptom: Every call to a local server costs ~2 s regardless of endpoint; curl to the IPv4 loopback gets no answer while 'localhost' works (Vite), or the reverse; tests expecting a fast 'connection refused' time out.
Cause: On Windows 'localhost' resolves ::1 first; an IPv4-only server is missed and the refused IPv6 connect costs ~2 s before fallback; Vite binds only localhost. On some machines connecting to a CLOSED loopback port hangs until timeout instead of being refused.
Fix: Use the literal IPv4 loopback for Python/IPv4 servers and in dev proxies, matching the host the server binds; note the reason next to the URL. Probe daemons with a short timeout (~0.5 s) and cache the result; test failure paths with a '.invalid' host.
Workaround: Dual-stack binding works but is risky on Windows (IPV6_V6ONLY defaults can leave IPv4 unanswered).
Tip: Always time a do-nothing endpoint first to expose a fixed per-call penalty. Connect timeouts arrive as URLError while read timeouts do not; handle both.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Console windows popping up from servers or child processes
Symptom: Nameless black cmd windows keep opening, or a console window flashes on every shell/CLI step and steals focus.
Cause: A server run with python.exe owns its own console; when the parent has no console (pythonw, windowed exe), every console-subsystem child spawned without CREATE_NO_WINDOW gets a new console.
Fix: Launch servers with pythonw -u through a hidden launcher and redirect stdout/stderr to a log; pass creationflags=CREATE_NO_WINDOW (0x08000000, not DETACHED_PROCESS) through one helper used at every spawn site.
Tip: List top-level windows with their owning process (EnumWindows) before guessing; MainWindowHandle is useless because the window belongs to conhost. Under pythonw stdout is invalid unless redirected.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Keeping a long-running monitoring rig alive on Windows
Symptom: Log streams and ssh tunnels die silently; a poller crashes on one DNS blip; console windows flash constantly.
Cause: Shell background jobs die when the harness task ends; tunnels drop; token-fetch errors in the loop are treated as fatal; every pythonw child opens its own console.
Fix: Run one long-lived Python supervisor that Popens each child, polls and restarts children that exit; treat DNS/token errors as transient and retry; spawn children with CREATE_NO_WINDOW and stdin=DEVNULL.
Tip: A background task reporting 'completed (exit 0)' for something that should never exit means the rig is dead. Check tunnels periodically.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Use the project venv, not the global Python
Symptom: A global install 'works' with dependency warnings; tests fail at collection with ModuleNotFoundError; pip install exits 0 but a package is missing.
Cause: The machine's global Python holds conflicting packages; pip resolves drift silently; occasionally installs are incomplete without any report.
Fix: Always create and run tests from the project venv (./.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest); check imports after installing.
Workaround: Rerun the same pip install if an import is missing after exit 0.
Tip: Dependency warnings at install time are a state a later build will resolve differently.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Windows clock resolution produces duplicate ids
Symptom: Tests pass on Linux but fail on Windows: records get overwritten by later records and the audit trail is lost.
Cause: time.time_ns() on Windows advances in 15.625 ms steps so consecutive calls return the same value.
Fix: Add a uuid4 suffix to timestamp-based ids. Test by freezing time_ns rather than with a loop (the loop passes on Linux).
Tip: '_ns' promises nanosecond units, not nanosecond resolution.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: node EACCES while PowerShell and curl reach the same URL
Symptom: npm ci fails with EACCES/FetchError (empty reason), npm blames file locks/antivirus; DNS and HTTP probes from PowerShell/curl succeed; Get-NetFirewallRule shows no blocking rule.
Cause: An Intune/MDM-pushed outbound firewall rule blocks node.exe by path. Get-NetFirewallRule without -PolicyStore reads only the local PersistentStore; audit event 5157 is off so logs are silent.
Fix: Ask IT for an exception for the build agent (MDM rules cannot be deleted locally and revert on sync).

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: A background Python server prints nothing (buffered stdout)
Symptom: A background tool serves normally but stdout is empty, so the URL/port it prints never shows.
Cause: Python block-buffers stdout when attached to a pipe instead of a terminal; output appears only when the process exits.
Fix: Use print(..., flush=True) or python -u for every line callers need while the process runs (URL, port, ready signal).
Workaround: Find the port by listing listening sockets and matching the owning process.
Tip: In-process tests do not read stdout so they do not catch this.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: An app 'causing' lag was just the last straw
Symptom: The machine hits 100% CPU and lags when a desktop app opens, and recovers when it closes; a log-based hypothesis blamed a reconnect storm.
Cause: Live measurement showed the app used only ~14% CPU; the rest was Defender, WSL, redundant parallel tests, Task Manager, WebView2. The app's only real fault was idle WebView2 burning nearly a core.
Fix: Measure the whole machine live (CPU delta per process tree and system-wide) before concluding; remove large unrelated loads; add antivirus exclusions for the repo and log folders.
Workaround: Kill redundant test runs, close Task Manager, stop idle WSL.
Tip: Hypotheses from logs/source must be confirmed by live sampling; explicitly retract suspects that were ruled out.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Hermit shims do not run under Git Bash on Windows
Symptom: Every hermit shim dies with 'HERMIT_STATE_DIR_RAW: unbound variable' or '<pkg>: command not found'.

Fix: Install native Windows toolchains (rustup, pip cmake, ...).
Tip: Do not retry hermit on Windows.

LESSON LEARNED [Windows & Dev Env]: Moving a running tool's folder, and log redirects
Symptom: Moving files fails on Windows; after a restart untracked log files appear in git status.
Cause: The running server holds its SQLite file (locked); Start-Process -RedirectStandardOutput/Error creates files right in the target folder.
Fix: Stop the server before moving; move only source/data and rebuild node_modules/dist at the destination (pnpm symlinks do not survive a move); redirect logs outside the repo or add them to .gitignore.

LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Measure instead of inferring from code reading or absent logs
Symptom: Several confident root causes (worker pool missing timeouts, outbox, config drift, SIGPIPE) and test expectations derived from reading library source all turned out wrong.
Cause: Inference from reading code, error text or a missing log line; the message was never actually delivered so there was nothing to log, and an app with a log rate limit of 0 made the silence look meaningful.
Fix: Measure live state during the failure (threads/pool, outbox table, queue depth, subscription record); probe the real library with exact inputs before writing assertions; git fetch before concluding code is missing; follow the gate policy even when slow.
Tip: State what is proven and what is not; never put hypotheses into tickets as facts. Check 'cf app' for 'logging: 0B/s' before concluding an app does not log; eliminate candidates with arithmetic and measure a do-nothing baseline before attributing latency.

LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Non-technical framing decides the design
Symptom: A new project proposal was overturned about ten times, never for a technical fault; an architecturally strong design pack still scored low.
Cause: The design started from the requirements document instead of the buyer: market, buyer, target platform, systems consuming the output, personas and numbers were asked late or assumed; a rebuild was treated as greenfield, forgetting thousands of legacy configs/rules holding value.
Fix: Go in this order before any technical choice: actor/market, outcome ('so what'), constraints, existing platform read from real config, value/IP protection, personas, domain semantics, numbers, evidence, operability; add a self-challenge pass.
Tip: Record unanswered items as open decisions with an owner and assumption. Name the problem class and look for precedent before proposing; coherence is not evidence. Plan migrations of governance definitions, not just data.

LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Destructive operations on a live production system
Symptom: 'Delete everything' does not hold because QC keeps creating tickets; attachments of a new real ticket were nearly deleted; the backup was stale within minutes.
Cause: Production is a moving target while people use it, and the requested scope was ambiguous ('users' could mean roster rows, identity documents or auth accounts).
Fix: Back up immediately before deleting; build the keep-set live at delete time (current references plus things edited in the last few minutes); have the owner resolve ambiguous scope; verify by read-back; never touch shared collections other products read.
Tip: Check what a 'duplicate' really is before deleting (two rows for one person may be two login methods). State the blast radius, e.g. deploying main after a long gap ships every pending commit.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Safe push discipline: merge-base and rerunning the gate
Symptom: A conflict check says every file is touched; an experimental revert deleted a real fix; gate results are stale after a rebase.
Cause: A tip-to-tip diff counts your own commits as upstream changes; 'git checkout -- file' reverts the whole file; upstream changed while the gate ran.
Fix: Check overlap from 'git merge-base'; undo experimental edits precisely instead of checking out; after every rebase rerun the full gate on the exact tree to be pushed; stash other people's dirty files by specific path.
Tip: Do not commit large local tool caches (git never forgets blobs). Do not mechanically resolve two people's clashing designs yourself; ask.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Same symptom, different cause: reproduce with real data
Symptom: Two identical 'missing company' reports had different causes; data 'not copied back from SAP' was blamed on the Node/UI layer; a count of 0 nearly raised a false lockout alarm.
Cause: Pattern-matching instead of checking; an API dropping the field it filters on; seed data looking exactly like real behaviour; a Firestore REST map parsed as an array; data already missing in the SAP/CPI response.
Fix: Reproduce each report with real data, trace the data path hop by hop (live read, copy-back table, staging, final, with control records); ask the reporter for the raw API response; print value types before counting.
Tip: Users' observations are usually right while their diagnoses are wrong; query real data read-only before accepting a diagnosis. If the upstream source returns incomplete data, hand it to the integration team with evidence; copy incident evidence somewhere durable.

LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Separate inference from sourced fact
Symptom: Three log entries blamed data loss on a server left running and a start-over button, but the user had deleted the session themselves; the inferred conclusion was later treated as confirmed.
Cause: An unexplained state change was attributed to a plausible mechanism without checking the obvious possibility (the person using the tool); the inferred conclusion was stored unmarked.
Fix: Ask the user before recording a cause, especially a fault; label inferences, state what would confirm them, and correct old entries explicitly when wrong.
Tip: When a lookup fails, say you do not know instead of estimating. When resuming, verify file lists and pointers on disk since someone else may have cleaned up.

LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Guides for non-specialist readers: actions only
Symptom: The owner cut a guide over five rounds (~40%), removing correct facts, warnings and mechanism explanations; a handover runbook written in the wrong language had to be redone.
Cause: The draft described the system instead of letting the reader act, serving two audiences at once; the recipient's language was inferred from the handing-over person.
Fix: Write only what the reader can DO, each heading a question they bring; move limitations to the maintainer doc; ask the recipient's name and language in every handover.
Tip: Write too little and offer more in chat. When there is both a sample and a template, fix both; never reference paths local to the author's machine.

LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Check real ownership and liveness before taking or porting work
Symptom: The ledger says 'unassigned' while someone just committed to that file; a task points at code that is an old fork nobody loads; two lanes both claim to port one engine.
Cause: The ownership ledger lags git reality, task specs were written from an incomplete checkout, lanes were split without deduplication.
Fix: Before taking work, check git activity on the files; grep callers to confirm code is alive before porting; remove duplicates and point to the owning lane.
Tip: A ported engine no app depends on has no value; check something consumes it (package.json dependencies) before reporting progress.

LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Branch names do not match environment names
Symptom: A fix cut from one branch was 'verified' on an environment that actually runs another branch; a 'PR into dev' request targeted the wrong branch.
Cause: The branch -> environment mapping does not follow names (e.g. the 'staging' branch deploys the DEV environment, there is no 'dev' branch), and higher environments receive cherry-picks.
Fix: Record the branch -> environment mapping in the project descriptor; before using a measurement from one environment as evidence for another branch, diff the relevant files between the two branches.
Tip: When looking for commits to promote, search the ticket key, subtask keys and clone keys; drop unrelated commits riding on the feature branch. Respect the dev-first gate and state it clearly if the user overrides.

Symptom: A shared rule was edited for the wrong purpose after the user named one profile; the user was confused by a UI element nobody asked for; risk of deleting files the user thought were lost.

LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Outward-facing actions and runs on shared systems need explicit approval
Symptom: Risk of an agent posting to a team channel, merging, pushing to main or running workflows that change shared dev system state unasked; typing 'allow' in chat is still blocked by the permission classifier.
Cause: Outward actions and merges are the owner's decisions; one approval is not a standing grant; auto-mode treats permission grants and unreviewed merges as risky.
Fix: Push only to the agreed feature branch and when asked; ask before each live run on shared infrastructure, proving state-changing paths with unit tests; let the user do it themselves or add an explicit permission rule.
Tip: Least privilege for admin operations (add a member row instead of raising a role) and record how to undo. Before asking an agent seat to merge, confirm it has the rights; ask whether a repo is a private test build or a contribution before proposing commits.

Fix: Push only to the agreed feature branch and when asked; ask before each live run on shared infrastructure, proving state-changing paths with unit tests; let the user do it themselves or add an explicit permission rule.
Tip: Least privilege for admin operations (add a member row instead of raising a role) and record how to undo. Before asking an agent seat to merge, confirm it has the rights; ask whether a repo is a private test build or a contribution before proposing commits.

Symptom: The user read a correct 'yes, provided that' answer as a refusal and asked again.
Cause: The answer opened with limits/caveats instead of the conclusion.
Fix: The first line carries a clear conclusion; mechanism, conditions and caveats go in the detail.
Tip: When a user asks the same question again, suspect a buried headline.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Size by the dominant cost term, not by adjectives
Symptom: A design sized for one user and one file; 'large' was accepted as a number.
Cause: No arithmetic on the heaviest workload; e.g. matching cost is the sum of squared block sizes, so one broad rule brings the system down.
Fix: Compute the dominant term with realistic coefficients, estimate block sizes before running and warn, process incrementally, load-test at the computed scale and publish the measured ceiling.
Tip: Ask the volume unit first (rows, files, media, events), separating count and size; ask build and run budgets separately. Label estimates with no comparable data point as a GUESS.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Documentation rot: trust the code, update docs with the change
Symptom: The root README is an unedited template, a C4 diagram draws containers that do not exist; the design doc lags shipped code by several revisions, the progress tree is days old.
Cause: Top-level docs rotted and design-time diagrams draw the target architecture; paperwork is treated as later work; contract tests check only one direction.
Fix: Use a CLAUDE.md maintained under a 'code wins' rule as the orientation doc; update design revision, change log and progress tree in the same change.
Tip: A green suite does not prove docs are still right. A monorepo may have no single test command and a service may have two entry points; confirm which one a change affects.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: A capability found only by deduction is not a feature
Symptom: The user said an option was impossible although the code supports it; auto-start sat behind one sidebar click; the settings page was full of explanations and warnings.
Cause: Verification proved the mechanism, not discoverability; the capability lived at one entry point; reasoning was written into the UI.
Fix: Every operation gets a visible row/control; wire the capability into every entry point that needs it; keep rationale in code comments; configure only what differs between machines.
Tip: Moving half a concept (a variable name without its value) creates new questions; move it whole. Prefer inline actions with undo (countdown) over confirm dialogs.

LESSON LEARNED [Process & Collaboration]: Designing questions/forms for expert respondents
Symptom: Forms are stiff or lecturing; some fields an architect cannot answer; choice questions whose branches are equivalent.
Cause: Text written for an absent reader; asking for computable values; turning unknowable judgements into choices recorded as facts.
Fix: Each question states the design consequence it decides; drop fields computable from earlier answers; ask past facts instead of predictions; one idea per bullet.
Tip: Two options with the same consequence mean the question is at the wrong level.

LOCAL KH ON 127.0.0.1:9000 - HOW TO READ IT FROM A SESSION WIRED TO KH BTP (no hook change needed). Written 2026-10-02 at fen's request.

WHAT IT IS. Some users still run the older desktop KnowledgeHub on their own machine (KnowledgeHub.exe, port 9000). It holds their pre-BTP projects, knowledge, worklogs, findings and policy. The BTP hooks never call it. This guide is how you reach it anyway, with plain HTTP, when the user asks.

WHEN TO USE IT. Only when the user asks for it: 'KH 9000', 'KH local', 'local KH', 'KH tren may', 'the old KH', or asks for data that BTP does not have and says it lives on their machine. Otherwise BTP stays the only KH: policy, routing, the worklog of this turn and every write go to BTP as the hooks say.

HOW TO CONNECT.
- Base URL http://127.0.0.1:9000. Use the literal IP, NEVER 'localhost': localhost tries IPv6 ::1 first, local KH binds IPv4 only, and every call then wastes about 2 s.
- No sign-in, no key, no token. Send Content-Type: application/json on POST. Do not send the BTP token or X-KH-Key to it.
- Check it first: GET /health answers {"status":"ok","model":"bge-small-en-v1.5"}. Connection refused = it is not running on this machine; tell the user, do not try to start or install it.
- The port can differ (KH_PORT in its .env; a spare test copy may run on 9100). If 9000 refuses, ask the user for the port.
- PowerShell: Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri http://127.0.0.1:9000/vector/query -ContentType 'application/json' -Body '{"text":"...","k":5,"scope":"knowledge","project":"<id>"}'. Use pwsh, not Windows PowerShell 5.1 (5.1 escapes < > ' & into unicode sequences). Bash: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9000/vector/query -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{...}'.

READ ROUTES (same shapes as on BTP, verified 2026-10-02).
- GET /projects - every local project with id, aliases, keywords, descriptor.
- GET /orchestrator/project_match?text=<user's words> - which local project the words mean ({best, ambiguous}).
- POST /vector/query {text, k, scope, project} - by meaning. The field is 'text', not 'query'. scope = knowledge | log | findings | policy | personalization.
- POST /vector/scroll {scope, project, where?, limit, offset} - read a whole partition, e.g. where {topic:{"$eq":"<subject>"}}. 'matched' is the true total. A page is complete only when count < limit; otherwise page with offset.
- GET /log/recent?limit=50 [&project=<id>] [&since=<ISO UTC>] - newest worklogs first. For time questions use this or scroll sorted by metadata.ts desc, never /vector/query.
- GET /findings/list?project=<id>; GET /policy/actions; GET /policy/plan?action=<label>&project=<id>.
- Always read the full source_text of a row; never answer from a truncated preview.

RULES.
- Read-only by default. Write to local KH (POST /vector/add) only when the user says so in that turn.
- Local data has its own project ids. A local project and a BTP project with the same id are different stores until someone copies one into the other. Say which side an answer came from.
- Local rules (policy, hooks) are NOT the BTP rules. Do not obey local policy over BTP policy; read it only as information.
- This is the user's own machine and data. Do not read another person's local KH, and do not copy local rows into a shared BTP project without the owner asking.

COPYING A LOCAL PROJECT INTO BTP (done for m360 on 2026-09-30 and evo-buzz on 2026-10-02).
1. Export: /vector/scroll each scope (knowledge, log, findings, policy) with project=<id> and a large limit; keep rows whose metadata.project is that id. Read the bundle (descriptor, aliases, keywords, conflicts_with) from GET /projects.
2. Scan every row for secret values (keys, tokens, passwords, connection strings with credentials) before sending anything.
3. On BTP: POST /projects with the same id and bundle; set the owner the user names; POST /vector/add each row with its original id, scope and metadata (drop emb_* and source_text from metadata; the server recomputes them).
4. Verify by id and full text on BTP (missing 0, extra 0, text equal), then remove any temporary admin grant. Known gap: the server stamps metadata.author from the caller's token, so copied rows show the copier as author.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: Check every path in a script before running it - people switch between machines
Symptom: A long-running script (EvoBuzz bridge) started cleanly but failed every job with 'FAILED: [WinError 267] The directory name is invalid'; a live demo broke.
Cause: The script's default repo path (E:\Workspaces\EvoBuzz\game-center) belonged to another machine. The env var meant to override it was never set, because Start-Process pwsh -Command '$env:X="..."' lost its inner quotes on Windows. Nothing checked that the paths existed before launch.
Fix: Before running any script, read it and list every path it uses (hardcoded defaults, env-var fallbacks, cwd, interpreter/venv, log and lock files); test each one on THIS machine; set overrides for those that differ; after launch confirm from the output that the right paths are used. Make the script itself refuse to start when a required path is missing. On Windows pass env vars via pwsh -EncodedCommand (UTF-16LE base64), not inline quotes.
Tip: The same person uses Claude Code on 2+ machines with different layouts (C:\RWTemp vs E:\Workspaces vs a Linux host). A path from memory, notes or KH logs may be from another machine. A machine without KH (e.g. a server) will not know this rule: write it into that machine's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

LESSON LEARNED [AI Agents & Claude Code]: No browser extension or usable browser session: launch Chrome yourself with a debug port
Symptom: A task needs a browser, but the Claude in Chrome extension is not found, or no open browser session can be used.
Cause: The agent stops and waits for the human, although it can open a browser on its own.
Fix: Launch Chrome yourself with --remote-debugging-port=<port> and a dedicated --user-data-dir, then drive it over CDP (for example Playwright connect_over_cdp). If a sign-in page appears, sign in or ask the human to sign in once in that window.
Tip: Do not stop just because the extension is missing. An open debug port lets any local process read cookies: use a dedicated profile and close it when done. Related: the lesson on Claude in Chrome not connecting.

rows.text:
LESSON LEARNED [Auth & Security]: Use the local App Session Manager (AutoLogin) before asking the user to sign in.

Context: When a task needs the user signed in to a web app (SSO, password, or an SAP cf passcode) and you are on the user's Windows machine, check for the user's local App Session Manager first instead of asking them to sign in.

The tool: App Session Manager (formerly AutoLogin), a tray app with a local service on 127.0.0.1:47291 and an MCP server named 'app-session-manager'. The user stores their own accounts in it, encrypted with Windows DPAPI for that Windows user only. It signs in inside a dedicated Chrome window per account and never returns secrets or cookies. Using it is not borrowing the browser's login session, and you never type the password yourself.

How to use it:
1. MCP tool present: call list_apps to see the entries, then get_session(app) once per app per task. It reuses or opens that app's signed-in Chrome window and returns the tab and its debug address; drive that tab.
2. Not signed in yet / awaiting the user: the user finishes MFA or the IdP step once in that window; wait, do not call again in a loop.
3. 'Needs user confirmation': prod/UAT entries show an Allow/Deny popup on the user's screen; tell the user and wait up to 4 minutes. DENIED: stop; never retry or reach the app another way.
4. No MCP tool but the service answers on 127.0.0.1:47291: POST /signin {"url"} (or {"id"} / {"name"}) with header X-Auto-Click-Token = the token in <tool folder>\data\windows.json. A passcode entry (SAP 'cf login --sso-passcode') returns its passcode only here, never through MCP.
5. Tool absent, or no entry for that app: ask the user to sign in themselves as usual; you may mention they can add the account in the tool's Config page (double-click the tray icon). Never forced.

Not installed and the user wants to install it: the guide is in project kh-tools (kind=tool-guide, tool=app-session-manager). Do not load it for ordinary sign-ins.

Related: lesson "Do not let agents borrow the browser's login session". Built by Rowan, 2026-10-05; updated 2026-10-10 (MCP get_session, no cookies returned, token in <tool>\data, confirmation popup, guide moved to kh-tools).

Related: lesson "Do not let agents borrow the browser's login session". Built by Rowan, 2026-10-05; updated 2026-10-10 (MCP get_session, no cookies returned, token in <tool>\data, confirmation popup, guide moved to kh-tools).

ESTIMATION STANDARD [planning / Claude Code build speed] (Rowan, first 2026-10-03, revised 2026-10-11 after measuring a fully autonomous build). Pick the MODE first, then the number. Planned hours below means a conventional-style plan.

MODE A - INTERACTIVE (one Claude session, one person reviews and decides at each step). MEASURED 2026-10-01..03 on KH roadmap items A, B, C (tests, dev deploy, benchmark runs, docs): estimated 6-10 working days, done in 3 (ratio 0.375); +30% buffer = about HALF of a conventional estimate: small change in one module ~0.3 day, medium feature ~0.65 day, feature with several measure-and-tune rounds ~1.3 days, new tooling ~2 days. A 'day' here is a CALENDAR working day that already contains waiting for the person: never convert it to continuous hours (x8) and never use it for autonomous work - that conversion inflated a 2026-10-10 plan about 45x (178 h planned, 3.9 agent-hours done).

MODE B - FULLY AUTONOMOUS (design decided, no human gate, parallel subagents on disjoint modules, agents write their own tests and run them in the real environment). MEASURED 2026-10-10/11 on KH stage F (14 slices, 178 planned h): code modules ~1.0 min of agent time per planned hour; a shared foundation ~0.6 min/h; real-environment integration (port to the real DB, deploy, end-to-end simulation and the bug fixes it triggers) ~4.0 min/h. Multiply by buffers: orchestration + review by the lead session x1.25, network lag x1.30, other risks x1.20 (model API 429/overload/outage retries, Docker/DB restarts, flaky test reruns, rework when parallel agents collide) = x1.95. Wall clock = (foundation + code / modules in parallel (cap 3-4) + integration) x 1.95. Check: stage F gives 7.7 agent-h and ~5.5 h wall with buffers; measured 3.9 agent-h and ~3.5-4 h.

ADD SEPARATELY in both modes, never inside the coding number (these usually decide the calendar): fixed cycle times (dev deploy ~10 min, prod deploy + e2e ~1 h, identity-provider releases, cloud pushes, multi-instance load tests), runs that go at the model's speed (real-LLM benchmark or e2e 1-3 h each), human code review of autonomous output, waiting for data or credentials, and open design decisions.

CEILING: Mode A was measured on small-to-medium items without new storage schema or new LLM; Mode B on a backend platform with ~14 modules. Re-measure after the next items and revise when the numbers move.
